article_content: George Zimmerman has broken his silence, telling the nation the timeline of events the night Trayvon Martin was shot dead. He said he has been vilified as a racist and a murderer—two things he vehemently denies. Speaking exclusively to Fox News’ Sean Hannity, Zimmerman recounted the night of February 26 in the gated community of Sanford, Florida, and said he does not regret getting out of his car that night. Throughout the hour-long interview, Zimmerman maintained his composure, sitting with his hands folded neatly in his lap and wearing a stoic expression. When asked what he would tell the nation, he firmly stated, 'I’m not a racist, and I’m not a murderer.' This is the first time Zimmerman has publicly spoken about the fateful night. He explained that it was no longer a choice for him to reach for his gun once Trayvon Martin began slamming his head into the sidewalk and reached for his holster. He said: 'At that point, I realized it wasn’t my gun, it wasn’t his gun—it was the gun. I heard him say, 'You’re going to die tonight.' I felt one of his hands going down my chest toward my holster. It just happened so quickly.' Hannity later asked if Zimmerman regretted getting out of his car. Zimmerman replied no, adding he also did not regret being armed or his other actions that night. 'I feel it was all God’s plan. To second-guess it…' he trailed off. However, near the end of the interview, Zimmerman corrected himself: 'I do wish there was something—I would have done anything—to avoid having to take his life.' Zimmerman said Martin broke his nose and slammed his head into the pavement—a claim corroborated by Sanford Police Department photos from that night. He added: 'I want to tell everyone—my wife, my parents, and the parents of Trayvon Martin—I’m sorry this happened. I hate to think it’s polarized America.' He described Martin as walking 'very leisurely for the weather,' noting he didn’t appear to be a resident or a fitness enthusiast training in the rain. Zimmerman said Martin was 'skipping away quickly' and 'wasn’t running out of fear.' That sparked his suspicion. Zimmerman recalled Martin approaching him and asking, 'What’s your problem?' He said he responded, 'I don’t have a problem,' and reached for his cell phone. At that moment, Martin punched him in the nose, breaking it. 'I don’t remember if I went immediately to the ground,' Zimmerman said, 'but he started bashing my head into the concrete sidewalk.' Throughout, Zimmerman insisted the screams heard on the 911 tapes were his own. 'It was my voice, absolutely,' he said. His attorney, Mark O’Mara, sat beside him during the interview. At one point, O’Mara suggested that, given the evidence, Zimmerman’s second-degree murder charge should be reduced to manslaughter. Zimmerman added: 'I’m sorry they buried their child. I can’t imagine what that feels like. I pray for them daily.' The interview comes one day after it was revealed that Zimmerman and his wife spent $36,000 from his online legal defense fund on personal expenses—including car payments, cell phones, credit card bills, and internet service—even though he was in jail at the time. Among the expenses were $600 in jailhouse phone calls. Zimmerman reportedly spent three to five hours per day on the phone, averaging 13 calls daily, often using coded language to discuss funds from the PayPal account. The largest single payment was $5,000 toward his initial $150,000 bail. The couple also spent $7,000 to pay down credit card debt—$4,000 on their American Express bill alone. O’Mara said these debts stemmed from expenses incurred after the family fled their home due to death threats. Zimmerman, 28, received approximately $200,000 in donations through his website, therealgeorgezimmerman.com. His attorney emphasized he has not taken any legal fees from the fund.

Dheweke nganggap diriné kaya rasisme lan pembunuh—dua hal sing diingkarié kanthi tegas. Ngobrol eksklusif karo Sean Hannity saka Fox News, Zimmerman njelaske nalika tanggal 26 Februari ing komunitas tertutup Sanford, Florida, lan ngomong dheweke ora nyesal keluar saka mobilé nalika iku. Sajené wanci siji jam wawancara, Zimmerman tetep tenang, duduk karo tangane dilipat rapet ing pangkuan lan wajahé tenang. Nalika ditanyai apa sing bakal diomongake karo bangsa, dheweke nyatake, 'Aku ora rasisme, lan aku ora pembunuh.' Iki kali pertama Zimmerman ngomong publik ngenani wektu mauté. Dheweke njelaske yen wis ora pilihan maneh kanggo mbawa senjata nalika Trayvon Martin mulai ngadegake kepalaé ing trotoar lan nyenggol senjataé. Dheweke ngomong: 'Kala iku, aku sadar iku ora senjataku, ora senjataé—iku senjata. Aku dengar dheweke ngomong, 'Kowe bakal mati weton iki.' Zimmerman jawab ora, nambahake dheweke ora nyesal senjata, utawa tindakan liyane nalika iku. 'Aku rasakake kabeh iku rencanaé Allah. Kanggo ngrengganié…' dheweke nyambut. Nanging, ing akhir wawancara, Zimmerman ngoreksi pernyataané: 'Aku pengin ana sawetara—kula bakal lakoni apa wae—supaya ora kudu nyawiji nyawaé.' Zimmerman njelaske Martin nyiksa hidungé lan ngadegake kepalaé ing trotoar—klaim sing didukung foto saka Departemen Polisi Sanford. Dheweke nambahake: 'Aku pengin ngomong karo kabeh—istriku, orang tuaku, lan orang tua Trayvon Martin—aku sesal karo iki. Aku sesal karo iki ngrusak Amerika.' Dheweke nggambarke Martin lagi mlayu 'sangat santai kanggo cuaca iki,' nglirik dheweke ora kaya wong sing tinggal utawa atlet sing latihan karo hujan. Zimmerman ngomong Martin 'meluncur cepet' lan 'ora lari amarga takut.' Iki ngasilke keraguan. Zimmerman ngelingake Martin ngadep dheweke lan nanya, 'Masalahmu apa?' Dheweke ngomong jawab, 'Aku ora duwe masalah,' lan njangkung teleponé. Saiki, Martin nyerang hidungé, nyiksa. 'Aku ora ngelingi yen langsung jatuh,' dheweke njelaske, 'nanging dheweke mulai ngadegake kepalaé ing trotoar beton.' Sajené wawancara, Zimmerman njamin suara jeritan ing rekaman 911 iku suarane dheweke. 'Iku suaraku, pasti,' dheweke ngomong. Pengacarane, Mark O’Mara, duduk samping dheweke nalika wawancara. Ing sawijining wektu, O’Mara ngusulake yen, karo bukti sing ana, tuduhan pembunuhan tingkat loro Zimmerman bisa dikurangi dadi pembunuhan tidak sengaja. Zimmerman nambahake: 'Aku sesal karo dheweke ngubur anaké. Aku ora bisa bayangake rasane. Aku doa kanggo dheweke tiap dina.' Wawancara iki tekan siji dina sawise diwaca yen Zimmerman lan istrié ngeluarke $36.000 saka dana hukum onlineé kanggo biaya pribadi—termasuk cicilan mobil, telepon, tagihan kartu kredit, lan layanan internet—nanging dheweke lagi nahan ing penjara. Sawetara biaya iku $600 kanggo telepon penjara. Zimmerman diberitahaké nggunakake 3-5 jam saben dina kanggo telepon, rata-rata 13 telepon saben dina, sering nggunakake sandhi kanggo ngomong bab dana saka PayPal. Bayaran paling gedhe yaiku $5.000 kanggo jaminan pertamaé, sing ditetepake $150.000. Pasangan iki uga ngeluarke $7.000 kanggo ngurangi utang kartu kredit—$4.000 kanggo tagihan American Expressé. O’Mara njelaske utang-utang iku digunakake kanggo biaya nalika keluarga iku mundur saka omahé amarga ancaman kematian. Zimmerman, 28, menerima perkiraan $200.000 sumbangan saka situsé, therealgeorgezimmerman.com. Pengacarane ngingetake dheweke ora ngambil biaya hukum saka dana iku.

article_content: The PanicMe app lets smartphone users send color-coded alerts—red, amber, or green—to up to 30 trusted contacts when they feel unsafe. A red alert signals imminent danger, such as an ongoing attack; amber indicates urgent need for assistance; and green means the user is in a low-risk scenario, like being lost or stranded. The app uses GPRS to pinpoint the user’s real-time location, enabling contacts and emergency responders to gauge proximity and respond effectively. Alerts are delivered via push notifications on recipients’ phones and continue at regular intervals until manually deactivated by the sender. Police can access these alerts through a secure portal when notified at their control centers. Developed by DataMe in partnership with local police forces, PanicMe aims to empower individuals and provide reassurance to loved ones. David Lindley, former Deputy Chief Constable and project consultant, noted: 'With so many people carrying mobile phones, apps like PanicMe don’t just help those in distress feel safer—they also bring peace of mind to those who care about them.' A free version of the app offers only the green alert feature. The full version, priced at £14.99 per year, unlocks all three alert levels and is available on Apple, Android, and Windows smartphones. The app’s release follows a 2023 survey by Ipsos Mori and King’s College London, which found that two-thirds of UK adults believe crime rates have not decreased—highlighting growing public concern over personal safety. PanicMe joins other emerging safety tools, such as MyWitness, which records audio and video during confrontations to gather evidence.

Peringatan merah nandhakake bahaya segera, kaya serangan sing lagi berlangsung; kuning nandhakake butuh bantuan segera; lan hijau nandhakake situasi risiko rendah, kaya ilang utawa mogok. Versi lengkap, hargane £14,99 saben taun, mbukak kabeh tiga level peringatan lan bisa diundhuh ing Apple, Android, lan Windows smartphone. Peluncuran aplikasi iki nindakake survei taun 2023 dening Ipsos Mori lan King’s College London, sing nemokake yen loro sasiki wong Inggris percaya tingkat kriminalitas ora turun—nandhakake kekhawatiran publik sing makin meningkat babagan keselamatan pribadi. PanicMe nyambung karo alat keselamatan anyar liyane, kaya MyWitness, sing merek audio lan video nalika konfrontasi kanggo ngumpulake bukti.

article_content: If you're currently in university, take a moment to appreciate the chaos — late-night study sessions, canned beans for dinner, and spontaneous friendships might be the peak of your happiness. A recent survey reveals that for many adults, especially those over 45, university years are remembered as the most meaningful and joyful chapter of their lives — even more so than getting married, having kids, or landing their first job. The data, collected by Chimes Shopping Centre in Uxbridge from 1,000 UK adults, shows that 57% of respondents rank university as their best life experience. Among those aged 45 to 54, this feeling is strongest. Even more striking: one in three said they’d go back if they could. Students today aren’t as nostalgic — they’re anxious. Seventy-three percent of 18- to 24-year-olds feel they didn’t make the most of their time, longing for more adventures, connections, and memories. The top reasons university stands out? Living away from home for the first time and meeting people who change your life. Location matters too. Graduates from Leeds and Wolverhampton are most likely to look back fondly, while those from the North East and Scotland are least inclined to romanticize their time on campus. The survey also revealed that university topped a list of 13 major life events — beating out buying a house, getting a first car, or even your first kiss.
translated_content: Yan sanak pelajar, kalaian ngajeni kalaian ngedaunin kekacauan — sesi belajar malam, mangan kacang bakar kalengan, lan persahabatan spontan bisa jadi puncak kebahagiaan kalaian. Survei anyar nemokna yen kangge sabaré wong, khususé kang umure luwih saka 45 taun, taun-taun kampus diinget minangka bab paling berarti lan paling gembira ing uripé — luwih saka nikah, duwe anak, utawa nemu pekerjaan pertama. Data iki dikumpulaké dening Pusat Perbelanjaan Chimes ing Uxbridge saka 1.000 wong Inggris, nuduhaké yen 57% responden nyoblos kampus minangka pengalaman paling apik ing uripé. Kangge wong umur 45-54 taun, rasa iki paling kuat. Luwih menarik maneh: siji saka telu ngomong yen mereka bakal balik yen bisa. Pelajar saiki ora seneng nginget — wong kuwatir. 73% wong umur 18-24 taun rasane durung nggunakake waktune kanthi maksimal, pengin pengalaman, koneksi, lan kenangan luwih akeh. Alasan paling utama kampus dadi spesial? Ngadeg dhewe pisanan lan ketemu wong-wong kang mbenerake uripé. Lokasi penting. Lulusan Leeds lan Wolverhampton paling suka ngeling-eling, nanging wong saka Timur Lor lan Skotlandia paling kurang seneng ngidola taun-taun kampusé. Survei uga nemokna yen kampus nyeret 13 pengalaman urip utama — ngalahaké njual rumah, nemu mobil pertama, utawa ciuman pertama.

article_content: On 6 August 2012, a tragic traffic collision in Leicester claimed the lives of two young children. One-year-old Oliwier Baczyk died at the scene, and two-year-old Zofia Tabaka passed away shortly afterward after being struck by a BMW that had collided with a Mini Cooper and mounted the pavement. The incident occurred at the junction of Narborough Road and Braunstone Gate at approximately 9:52 a.m. CCTV footage captured the moments before the crash, showing the BMW veering toward two buggies where the children, accompanied by their fathers, were waiting at a pedestrian crossing. Both fathers, aged 28 and 29, sustained minor injuries. A 40-year-old woman and a 61-year-old man were arrested in connection with the crash but have since been released on police bail pending further investigation. Witnesses described the chaos following the collision. Builder Dave Marsh recalled rushing to the scene, finding Oliwier motionless and bleeding heavily, while others attended to Zofia. He held the boy’s hand until paramedics arrived, noting the father was in shock and the mother arrived later, accompanying the child to the hospital. Karzan Nasroullah, who runs a car wash nearby, described seeing the children lying in the road and the immediate response from locals offering blankets and assistance. Shop owner Bob Young, whose CCTV recorded the event, said the car 'careered off the road' after hitting the Mini. Floral tributes and heartfelt messages have been left at the site by grieving community members. Leicestershire Police have appealed for anyone with information about the incident or its lead-up to come forward, urging witnesses to contact them via 101 or anonymously through Crimestoppers at 0800 555 111.

article_content: Mashable — Google has removed 21 popular free apps from the Android Market due to malicious activity. According to the company, these apps were designed to gain root access to users' devices, harvest sensitive data, and silently install additional malicious code without consent. Although Google swiftly removed the apps after being alerted by the blog Android Police, at least 50,000 users had already downloaded them. The apps were particularly deceptive, mimicking legitimate versions of widely used applications. For instance, one was named simply 'Chess' — appearing as a harmless game, but functioning as malware once installed. All were pirated copies of popular games and utilities, making them easy targets for quick exploitation by cybercriminals. Once installed, the apps exploited known vulnerabilities like 'rageagainstthecage' to obtain root privileges. They then used Android APK files to extract personal information, including mobile provider details and user IDs. After gaining control, the apps opened persistent backdoors to download further malware. All malicious apps were developed by a single entity, Myournet. A partial list includes: Falling Down, Super Guitar Solo, Super History Eraser, Photo Editor, Super Ringtone Maker, Super Sex Positions, Hot Sexy Videos, Chess, Hilton Sex Sound, Screaming Sexy Japanese Girls, Falling Ball Dodge, Scientific Calculator, Dice Roller, Advanced Currency Converter, APP Uninstaller, Funny Paint, and Spider Man. If you’ve installed any of these apps, it’s advisable to contact your mobile carrier. While factory resetting may help, full device replacement is recommended only if you’ve conducted sensitive activities like mobile banking or online shopping, as the extent of compromise cannot be guaranteed. Remember: The Android Market was open by design — a feature that enabled innovation but also invited abuse. Always read user reviews before downloading, and when in doubt, avoid the app altogether.

Sawise ngendalikan, aplikasi punika mbukak backdoor kangge ngundhuh kode jahat liyane. Kabeh aplikasi jahat punika dikembangaken dening entitas tunggal, Myournet. Daftar sebagian: Falling Down, Super Guitar Solo, Super History Eraser, Photo Editor, Super Ringtone Maker, Super Sex Positions, Hot Sexy Videos, Chess, Hilton Sex Sound, Screaming Sexy Japanese Girls, Falling Ball Dodge, Scientific Calculator, Dice Roller, Advanced Currency Converter, APP Uninstaller, Funny Paint, lan Spider Man. Yen sampeyan wis instal salah sawijining aplikasi punika, disaranake kangge ngomong karo operator seluler sampeyan. Nanging, reset pabrik bisa mbantu, penggantian piranti direkomendasikan mung yen sampeyan wis melakuake aktivitas sensitif kaya perbankan seluler utawa belanja online, amarga tingkat kompromi ora bisa dipastikan. Ingat: Android Market dianakake kanthi desain terbuka — fitur sing ngajeni inovasi nanging uga ngajeni penyalahgunaan. Mangan review pangguna sadurunge undhuh, lan yen kurang yakin, hindari aplikasi punika.

article_content: In a remarkable breakthrough, Italian investigators have decoded a cryptic, hand-written document that details the secretive initiation rites of the 'Ndrangheta — Italy’s most powerful and brutal organized crime syndicate, based in Calabria. Found during a police raid on a suspect’s home in Rome, the three-page manuscript was covered in a complex cipher mixing symbols resembling Cyrillic, Arabic, and archaic Chinese characters. After months of analysis, two officers with a passion for puzzles cracked the code by identifying one recurring glyph as the letter 'C', unlocking the rest of the message. The text outlines a chilling ritual known as the 'baptism,' where a new member must cut their own skin with a knife, drink their blood, and swear eternal loyalty to the organization. The oath, recited three times for symbolic power, demands absolute obedience: the initiate must renounce their entire family and resolve all conflicts with cold, exacting precision. The ceremony must take place in a space previously sanctified by other members, and结束后 must be undone in reverse order. The document also describes mystical identifiers of a true 'man of honor': a gold star on the forehead, a knight’s cross on the chest, and a golden palm in the hand — all tattooed into the flesh, not worn as ornaments. The revelation comes amid renewed public attention on the 'Ndrangheta, following the exposure that Nigella Lawson’s former assistants, the Grillo sisters, had ties to the clan. This document represents the most comprehensive record of 'Ndrangheta initiation rituals ever uncovered by authorities.
translated_content: Dina kacarutan sing prasaja, penyelidik Italia ngrusak dokumen tulisan tangan sing mbeberake ritual inisiasi rahasia saka 'Ndrangheta — sindikat kriminal terorganisir paling kuat lan brutal ing Italia, sing ngemong ing Calabria. Dokumen kaping telu sing ditemokake nalika razia ing omah saka seorang tersangka ing Roma, ditutupi dening sandi rumit sing nyatut simbol kang mirip karo aksara Sirilik, Arab, lan Cina kuna. Sawise analisis pitung minggu, loro petugas kanthi minat marang teka-teki ngrusak sandi kasebut kanthi ngenali simbol sing njlajah minangka huruf 'C', kang mbukak bagian liyane. Teks iki mbeberake ritual sing ngrembugake 'pembaptisan', di mana anggota anyar kudu nggunakake pisau kanggo nggunakake kulité dhewe, ngombe darahé dhewe, lan ngadegake kesetiaan abadi marang organisasi. Sumpah iku, diulang telung kali kanggo kekuatan simbolis, ngandhut ketaatan mutlak: inisiator kudu nglawan keluargane kabeh lan nyelesaikan kabeh perselisihan kanthi presisi sing ketat. Upacara kasebut kudu dilakoni ing tempat sing wis disucike dening anggota liyane, lan sawise rampung kudu diputer balik. Dokumen iki uga mbeberake identitas mistis saka 'manusia terhormat': bintang emas ing dahi, salib ksatria ing dada, lan daun palem emas ing tangan — kabeh ditato ing kulit, ora dipaké minangka perhiasan. Panyataan iki ditemokake nalika atensi publik kembali ditekani marang 'Ndrangheta, sawise diwatesake yen asisten pribadi Nigella Lawson, para saudari Grillo, duwe hubungan karo klan iki. article_content: After arresting 19-year-old Aaron Phelps for allegedly operating a drug distribution hub from his home, the Warr Acres Police Department placed a stark message on his front door: 'The Dope Man is Out Of Business,' along with the department’s contact number. The sign was designed to send a firm message to the community: drug dealing will not be accepted in Warr Acres. Neighbors had long complained about constant visitors arriving at all hours, sometimes even forming queues outside the house. During a search of the property, officers recovered drug paraphernalia, a digital scale, a hand-drawn sign reading 'WEED,' and sealed plastic bags labeled 'OG Green' and 'Crack.' Phelps has been charged with distributing controlled substances, maintaining a premises for drug activity, possessing a weapon while committing a felony, and possessing drug paraphernalia. He is currently held in Oklahoma County Jail on a $15,500 bond. Although the photo of the sign went viral on social media—with users joking and tagging posts with #whosenext and #wewontstop—the department clarified that the intent was never comedic. Sergeant John Gray stressed that the action was a deliberate step to reassure residents that police are committed to making neighborhoods safer for families. The Oklahoma County Sheriff’s Office later shared the image on Facebook, adding a lighthearted Valentine’s Day twist to amplify visibility—but emphasized that the underlying issue remains serious. Behind the memes lies a sustained effort to disrupt drug networks and restore safety to affected communities.

article_content: More than 540 employees from Nexen Energy in Calgary recently turned Century Park into a Gotham City takeover — all in the name of charity. Dressed head-to-toe in full Batman gear — black suits, capes, masks, and signature yellow belts — they gathered for five minutes to officially shatter the previous Guinness World Record for the largest gathering of Batman enthusiasts. The old mark? Just 250. They didn’t just beat it — they nearly doubled it, with 542 costumed heroes standing shoulder to shoulder. Among them, fans of the Dark Knight weren’t alone: the Joker and Robin made surprise appearances, turning the event into a full-blown comic book festival. The stunt, held on September 18, kicked off Nexen’s annual United Way campaign under the theme ‘From Suits to Superheroes.’ Fang Zhi, CEO of Nexen Energy ULC, praised his team’s spirit, calling them ‘true superheroes’ for uniting to support the local community. It wasn’t their first record-breaking feat: back in 2011, 437 of their staff had worn Superman suits to claim a similar title. This time, they didn’t just aim to raise money — they wanted to inspire joy, foster teamwork, and remind everyone that even in everyday jobs, ordinary people can do extraordinary things.

article_content: Despite mounting allegations that New Jersey Governor Chris Christie was aware of the 2013 lane closures on the George Washington Bridge—a controversy later dubbed 'Bridgegate'—he spent the evening of February 1, 2014, mingling with celebrities at shock-jock Howard Stern’s birthday party in Manhattan. On the same day, David Wildstein, a former Port Authority official and Christie’s longtime friend, announced he possesses documentation proving Christie lied when he claimed to have no prior knowledge of the closures. Wildstein, who oversaw the traffic disruption, suggested the closures were politically motivated retaliation against Fort Lee’s mayor, who declined to endorse Christie’s re-election campaign. Christie, arriving at the Hammerstein Ballroom around 6:30 p.m., took the stage shortly after 7 p.m. to celebrate Stern and introduce fellow New Jerseyan Jon Bon Jovi, quipping, 'The representative from New Jersey you want to see right now… is one of New Jersey’s favorite sons.' Bon Jovi performed 'Wanted Dead or Alive,' and Christie departed soon after. Comedian Joan Rivers joked on Twitter about Christie’s arrival, asking, 'How was the traffic?'—a pointed reference to the gridlock that paralyzed Fort Lee for four days in September 2013. Wildstein’s attorney, Alan Zegas, sent a letter to the Port Authority asserting that evidence directly links Christie to knowledge of the closures during their occurrence, contradicting Christie’s public denial during a two-hour press conference on January 9. Christie had insisted he believed the closures were part of a traffic study and placed blame on Wildstein and Bridget Kelly. Emails between Kelly and Wildstein—including Kelly’s message, 'Time for some traffic problems in Fort Lee'—have fueled suspicion of intentional sabotage. Additional allegations in Wildstein’s letter claim Port Authority funds were withheld from critics of Christie’s administration and redirected to projects tied to his allies. Federal investigations by the FBI and U.S. Attorney were ongoing. Christie’s office continued to deny any wrongdoing, maintaining he had no prior knowledge. Two other aides—Bill Baroni and Bill Stepien—were removed after their own communications revealed awareness or celebration of the disruptions. The scandal threatened Christie’s political future, particularly his perceived viability as a 2016 Republican presidential candidate. As scrutiny intensified, the public awaited further disclosure of Wildstein’s undisclosed evidence.

Nalika hari sing same, David Wildstein, mantan pejabat Port Authority lan teman lama Christie, ngumumke nangana dokumen sing mbuktekne Christie bohong nalika dia ngaku ora tahu apa-apa nganti kagiatan iki. Wildstein, sing ngendalike gangguan lalu lintas, nyaranne kagiatan iki dadi balas dendam politik marang walikota Fort Lee, sing ora milih Christie ing kampanye re-eliginya. Christie, sing tiba ing Hammerstein Ballroom jam 6:30 sore, naik pentas setelah jam 7 sore kanggo ngucapaké selamat ulang taun kanggo Stern lan ngenalkan Jon Bon Jovi, wong New Jersey liyane, karo canda: 'Wakil New Jersey sing kowe pengin dekati saiki… yaiku salah siji putra paling dicintai New Jersey.' Bon Jovi mainake lagu 'Wanted Dead or Alive,' lan Christie lunga sawise kasebut. Komedian Joan Rivers nyeru nang Twitter babagan kedatangan Christie, nanya: 'Bagaimana lalu lintasna?'—sanajan sing ngandhut ing kemacetan sing ngganggu Fort Lee selama empat hari ing September 2013. Pengacara Wildstein, Alan Zegas, ngirim surat karo Port Authority sing ngaku yen bukti nyambung langsung Christie karo pengetahuane nang kala kagiatan iki berlangsung, nyelisihi pernyataan publik Christie ing konferensi pers dua jam ing 9 Januari. Christie ngaku dia nganggep kagiatan iki bagian saka studi lalu lintas lan nyalahke Wildstein lan Bridget Kelly. Email antara Kelly lan Wildstein—termasuk pesan Kelly, 'Waktune ana masalah lalu lintas ing Fort Lee'—nggawe dugaan kagiatan iki disengaja. Alegasi liyane nang surat Wildstein ngandhut dana Port Authority ditahan saka kritikus administrasi Christie lan dialihke marang proyek sing nyambung karo pendukunge. Skandal iki ngancam masa depan politik Christie, khususe kebolehane dheweke minangka kandidat presiden Republikan 2016. article_content: Soheil Feizi considers himself an optimistic person. But the University of Maryland computer science professor is blunt when summarizing the current state of AI image watermarking: 'We don’t have any reliable watermarking at this point,' he says. 'We broke all of them.' For one of the two types of AI watermarking he tested in a new study — 'low perturbation' watermarks, which are invisible to the naked eye — he is even more direct: 'There’s no hope.' Feizi and his coauthors — Vittoria Elliott, Alistair Croll, and Christopher Beam — examined how easily bad actors can evade watermarking attempts, a process he calls 'washing out' the watermark. Their study not only demonstrates how attackers can remove watermarks but also shows that watermarks can be falsely inserted into human-generated images, triggering false positives. Released online this week, the preprint paper has yet to be peer-reviewed. However, given Feizi’s longstanding leadership in AI detection research, the findings warrant serious attention even at this early stage. Watermarking has emerged as one of the most promising strategies to identify AI-generated images and text. Like physical watermarks on currency and stamps, digital watermarks aim to trace the origin of online content, helping users detect deepfakes and bot-authored material. With the 2024 U.S. presidential election approaching, concerns over manipulated media are mounting — and people are already being fooled. For example, former U.S. President Donald Trump shared a fake video of Anderson Cooper on Truth Social, where Cooper’s voice had been cloned using AI. This summer, OpenAI, Alphabet, Meta, Amazon, and other major AI companies pledged to develop watermarking technologies to combat misinformation. In late August, Google’s DeepMind released a beta version of its new watermarking tool, SynthID. The goal is to flag AI-generated content as it’s produced, much like physical watermarks authenticate banknotes during printing. Yet this straightforward strategy may not be effective. This study is not the only one highlighting watermarking’s vulnerabilities. 'It is well established that watermarking can be vulnerable to attack,' says Hany Farid, a professor at the UC Berkeley School of Information. In August, researchers from the University of California, Santa Barbara, and Carnegie Mellon published a paper with similar conclusions after conducting experimental attacks: 'All invisible watermarks are vulnerable.' This latest study goes further: while some researchers had hoped that visible ('high perturbation') watermarks might resist manipulation, Feizi and his team argue that even these more robust types can be compromised.

Nanging dosen ilmu komputer University of Maryland iki nyebut karo tegas ngenani keadaan saiki saking watermarking gambar AI: 'Kita teka nggawe watermarking sané bisa dipercaya, kala iki,' ujane. 'Kami gelem ngilangi kabehé.' Kangge salah siji saka loro jinis watermarking AI sané diuji néwé — watermarking 'low perturbation', sané teka teka kasat mata — dia malah leuwih tegas: 'Ora ana pangarep.' Feizi lan kawan-kawane — Vittoria Elliott, Alistair Croll, lan Christopher Beam — nganalisis seberapa gampang pelaku jahat bisa ngilangi upaya watermarking, proses sané dia sebut 'nyucihake' watermark. Penelitian iki ora cuma nunjukke carane penyerang bisa ngilangi watermark, nanging uga nyathet yen watermark bisa disisipke sawise gambar hasil buatan manusia, nglahirke false positive. Ngedolake online minggu iki, makalah preprint iki teka teka di-review rekan. Nanging amarga Feizi iku tokoh utama ing riset deteksi AI, temuan iki kudu diprihatinkan, sadurunge kapanpun. Watermarking muncul minangka salah siji strategi paling janji kanggo ngidentifikasi gambar lan teks hasil AI. Kayane watermark fisik ing duit lan perangko, watermark digital diarani kanggo njelesakke asal-usul konten online, mbantu wong ngelingi video deepfake lan buku hasil bot. Kangge pemilihan presiden AS 2024 sing bakal tiba, kekhawatiran marang media dimanipulasi munggah — lan wong-wong wis ketemu kepalsuan. Contone, mantan presiden AS Donald Trump mbagike video palsu Anderson Cooper ing platform Truth Social, suara Cooper wis dikloning nganggo AI. Musim panas iki, OpenAI, Alphabet, Meta, Amazon, lan perusahaan AI gedhe liyane ngangkat janji kanggo ngembangake teknologi watermarking kanggo ngalahke misinformasi. Ing akhir Agustus, Google’s DeepMind ngedolake versi beta saka alat watermarking anyaré, SynthID. Harapane yaiku alat-alat iki bakal nandha konten AI nalika dihasilke, kaya watermark fisik sing ngautentikasi duit nalika dicetak. Nanging strategi sing langsung iki mungkin ora bakal berhasil. Penelitian iki ora satunggalé sing nandhakake kewanangan besar watermarking. 'Ditepati banget yen watermarking bisa rawan serangan,' ujar Hany Farid, dosen ing UC Berkeley School of Information. Ing Agustus, peneliti saka University of California, Santa Barbara, lan Carnegie Mellon ngedolake makalah karo temuan padha setelah ngadegake serangan eksperimental: 'Kabeh watermark tak kasat mata rawan.' Penelitian paling anyar iki malah luwih jauh: nalika sawetara peneliti tetep nganggep yen watermark 'visible' ('high perturbation') bisa tahan serangan, Feizi lan timné nyebut yen jenis sing luwih kuat iki uga bisa dimanipulasi.

article_content: Eden Hazard has opened up about how painful it was to see his close friend Juan Mata leave Chelsea back in 2014. Though he understood Mata’s need to play regularly — especially after being benched under then-manager Jose Mourinho — Hazard admits he hoped the Spanish midfielder would have stayed. 'He was such a special player to play alongside,' Hazard told the Sunday Mirror. 'It wasn’t easy watching him sit on the bench when he deserved to be on the pitch.' The two shared many memorable moments at Stamford Bridge, including goals and hugs after victories, and their bond remains strong off the field. But come Sunday, all that friendship will be set aside. With Chelsea leading the Premier League and a chance to extend their lead to six points over rivals like Manchester City, Hazard is laser-focused on winning. He hasn’t reached out to Mata during this season, making it clear: 'He plays for United now. I play for Chelsea. I’m here to win.'

article_content: Electronic cigarettes have been aggressively marketed as tools to help people quit smoking for good. However, preliminary findings from a major new U.S. government study—released on Thursday—reveal that many smokers are using vaping devices not to quit, but to supplement their nicotine intake. Dr. Andrew Hyland of the Roswell Park Cancer Institute in Buffalo, New York, who leads the research, suggests some individuals treat e-cigarettes as a 'crutch,' allowing them to satisfy nicotine cravings indoors without lighting up a traditional cigarette. The study, part of the Population Assessment of Tobacco and Health (PATH) initiative, analyzed data from 20,000 participants. It found that 28% of adults and nearly 9% of youths currently use any form of tobacco. Among these users, 40% report using two or more tobacco products, and half of them list battery-powered e-cigarettes as one of those products. The most common combination? Cigarettes paired with e-cigarettes. Mitch Zeller, director of the FDA’s Center for Tobacco Products, called these early results compelling, highlighting just how widespread e-cigarette use has become. The full PATH study will track 46,000 Americans aged 12 and older over five years, providing critical data to guide future tobacco regulation. While many anti-smoking advocates view e-cigarettes as a less harmful option for those unwilling or unable to quit nicotine entirely, health officials warn they are far from safe. E-cigarettes heat liquid nicotine into an inhalable vapor and contain fewer toxic chemicals than burned tobacco—but their long-term health impacts remain poorly understood. Critics question whether e-cigarettes merely sustain addiction—or even act as a gateway to traditional smoking. Concerns intensified after a December government study found teens who had never smoked traditional cigarettes were experimenting with vaping. 'Is it a passing fancy or something that sticks with them?' asked Dr. Wilson Compton of the NIH’s National Institute on Drug Abuse. He hopes the PATH study will provide answers over the coming years. The FDA has proposed regulating e-cigarettes—including banning sales to minors, a measure already adopted by many states. But uncertainties remain: Nicotine levels vary dramatically across devices—from low doses to nearly matching traditional cigarettes. Even factors like device voltage and puffing technique can alter nicotine delivery. To address this inconsistency, NIDA plans to fund the creation of a 'standard e-cigarette' to serve as a benchmark for scientific comparisons.
translated_content: Rokok elektrik telah dipromosikan secara agresif sebagai alat untuk membantu orang berhenti merokok selamanya. Namun, temuan awal dari studi pemerintah AS yang besar—dipublikasikan pada hari Kamis—menunjukkan bahwa banyak perokok menggunakan perangkat uap bukan untuk berhenti, melainkan untuk menambah asupan nikotin mereka. Dr. Andrew Hyland dari Roswell Park Cancer Institute di Buffalo, New York, yang memimpin penelitian ini, menyarankan bahwa beberapa orang menganggap rokok elektrik sebagai 'penopang' agar bisa mendapatkan nikotin di dalam ruangan tanpa harus menghisap rokok tradisional. Studi ini, bagian dari inisiatif Population Assessment of Tobacco and Health (PATH), menganalisis data dari 20.000 peserta. Studi menemukan bahwa 28% dewasa dan hampir 9% remaja saat ini menggunakan bentuk tembakau apa pun. Di antara pengguna ini, 40% melaporkan menggunakan dua atau lebih produk tembakau, dan separuhnya menyebut rokok elektrik bertenaga baterai sebagai salah satu produk tersebut. Kombinasi paling umum? Rokok tradisional dipadukan dengan rokok elektrik. Mitch Zeller, direktur Pusat Produk Tembakau FDA, menyebut temuan awal ini meyakinkan, menekankan betapa luasnya penggunaan rokok elektrik. Studi PATH penuh akan memantau 46.000 warga Amerika berusia 12 tahun ke atas selama lima tahun, memberikan data penting untuk membimbing regulasi tembakau di masa depan. Meskipun banyak advokat anti-rokok melihat rokok elektrik sebagai opsi yang kurang berbahaya bagi mereka yang enggan atau tidak mampu berhenti dari nikotin, pejabat kesehatan memperingatkan bahwa mereka jauh dari aman. Rokok elektrik memanaskan nikotin cair menjadi uap yang dapat dihirup dan mengandung zat beracun lebih sedikit daripada rokok tembakau bakar—tetapi dampak kesehatan jangka panjangnya masih kurang dipahami. Kritikus mempertanyakan apakah rokok elektrik hanya mempertahankan kecanduan—atau bahkan bertindak sebagai pintu masuk menuju merokok tradisional. Kekhawatiran meningkat setelah studi pemerintah Desember menemukan remaja yang belum pernah merokok rokok tradisional sedang mencoba rokok elektrik. 'Apakah itu sekadar tren sementara atau sesuatu yang menetap?' tanya Dr. Wilson Compton dari National Institute on Drug Abuse NIH. Ia berharap studi PATH akan memberikan jawaban dalam beberapa tahun mendatang. FDA telah mengusulkan regulasi rokok elektrik—termasuk melarang penjualan kepada anak di bawah umur, langkah yang sudah diambil oleh banyak negara bagian. Tetapi ketidakpastian tetap ada: Tingkat nikotin sangat bervariasi di berbagai perangkat—from dosis rendah hingga hampir sebanyak rokok tradisional. Bahkan faktor seperti tegangan perangkat dan teknik menghisap dapat mengubah pengiriman nikotin. Untuk mengatasi ketidaksesuaian ini, NIDA berencana mendanai pembuatan 'rokok elektrik standar' sebagai tolok ukur perbandingan ilmiah.

article_content: The Italian magazine at the center of the royal privacy controversy has published photographs of Pippa Middleton holding hands with a mystery man. Chi magazine previously sparked outrage by running front-page images of the pregnant Duchess of Cambridge in a bikini during a family holiday on Mustique. The same edition also features pictures of her younger sister with a new companion. Prince William and Kate Middleton traveled to the private Caribbean island last week, later joined by her parents, Carole and Michael Middleton, and siblings Pippa and James. Unauthorized beach photos of the family surfaced in Chi magazine and are set to be published in Australia. Chi published images of the Duke and Duchess paddling in the sea under headlines like 'The Belly Grows' and 'Honeymoon for Three.' It also showed Pippa in an orange-and-pink striped bikini, holding hands with a broad, brown-haired man wearing black patterned swim shorts and sunglasses. In another photo, she walks beside James Middleton, who is tanned and dressed in blue swimwear. Chi claimed the man is James Matthews, a wealthy businessman Pippa dated before Christmas. However, sources close to Matthews, 37, denied it was him, suggesting Pippa may have a new partner. Matthews, an Eton graduate and CEO of Eden Rock Capital Management, was reportedly at his London office at the time. Pippa has not been in a serious relationship since splitting from City banker Alex Loudon in November 2011, though she has been linked to several aristocrats. St James’s Palace called the publication of the photos a 'clear breach of privacy.' One image shows Kate tying her hair up knee-deep in crystal-clear water, her pregnancy visibly apparent, with William nearby. Another bears the caption: 'The bump is starting to show, and the princess has a softer figure than on her 2011 Seychelles honeymoon.' Photos from that earlier trip were also included. Chi’s editor, Alfonso Signorini, defended the photos as 'unexceptional' and 'not scandalous,' arguing they were taken in public spaces with other swimmers present. He added: 'The Italian press doesn’t have a gentleman’s agreement with the British royal family.' Ironically, the article notes the royal couple hoped their villa was large enough to accommodate their bodyguards—protecting them from incidents like last summer’s topless photos taken in France. Chi has previously published topless images of Kate and infamously released a photo of Princess Diana moments after her fatal 1997 car crash in Paris. Australian magazine Woman’s Day acquired 39 photos from the Mustique holiday for nearly £100,000, planning to publish them on Monday. Editor Fiona Connolly insisted the images were captured by a civilian holidaymaker, not professional photographers, and emphasized they were not nude or telephoto shots. Critics question whether the photographer posed as a tourist to gain access. Either way, the incident is an embarrassment for Mustique, known for high-security villas. Connolly remarked: 'We see pregnant women in bikinis on public beaches every day in Australia—we’re less sensitive here.' Last year, the royal family took legal action against French magazine Closer over similar topless photos. A Paris court issued an injunction, but the case remains ongoing after Closer appealed.

Connolly berkomentar: 'Kami melihat wanita hamil mengenakan bikini di pantai umum setiap hari di Australia—kami jauh lebih kurang sensitif di sini.' Tahun lalu, keluarga kerajaan mengajukan tindakan hukum terhadap majalah Prancis Closer atas foto telanjang serupa. article_content: Washington (CNN) — The Pentagon has taken a significant step toward prosecuting Abd al-Rahim al-Nashiri, the alleged mastermind behind the 2000 bombing of the USS Cole, by formally referring charges against him to a military commission at Guantanamo Bay, Cuba. Al-Nashiri, a Saudi-born former millionaire, is accused of orchestrating the attack in Yemen’s port of Aden that killed 17 U.S. sailors, wounded many others, and severely damaged the warship. The referral by the Defense Department’s Military Commissions unit initiates the next phase: the appointment of a military judge, followed by a pre-trial conference among prosecutors, defense counsel, and the judge within weeks. An arraignment is expected within 30 days. If convicted, al-Nashiri could face the death penalty, as the charges have been referred to a capital military commission. In addition to the USS Cole attack, al-Nashiri is also charged in connection with an unsuccessful attempt to bomb the USS The Sullivans in January 2000 and the 2002 bombing of the French tanker Limburg, which resulted in one fatality. His defense team, composed of both civilian and military attorneys, expressed deep disappointment. 'We are disappointed the United States will now descend further down the path of expedient and secret justice that military commissions have come to represent,' said civilian attorney Rick Kammen. 'This is not a constitutionally adequate trial—and we are dismayed the U.S. government is pursuing the death penalty through this flawed process.' Legal filings argue that al-Nashiri was subjected to torture while in U.S. custody, including waterboarding, being threatened with a power drill and a loaded handgun while naked and hooded, and threats against his family. His lawyers contend these abuses forfeit the government’s right to prosecute him—or execute him. The military commission system, originally created by President George W. Bush and revised under President Barack Obama, has long faced criticism for permitting coerced testimony while suppressing evidence of torture itself. The ACLU condemned the system as fundamentally unfair. 'Unlike federal courts, military commissions allow coerced evidence—but censor proof of the torture that produced it,' said Denny LeBoeuf of the ACLU’s Capital Punishment Project. As the case prepares to proceed, Brig. Gen. Mark Martins, the new chief prosecutor, is stepping into a high-stakes role. A West Point valedictorian, Rhodes Scholar, and Harvard Law graduate, Martins is seen by the administration as a figure who can restore credibility to the military commission system. He may introduce reforms such as live closed-circuit broadcasts of proceedings to victims, families, and journalists—with a 'kill switch' to block audio if classified information is disclosed. Al-Nashiri is one of 171 detainees still held at Guantanamo Bay. This case represents the first full prosecution under the current military commission framework and serves as a critical test for the system before the much larger 9/11 trial proceeds.

Dokumen hukum ngargayani al-Nashiri kena penyiksaan nalika ing tahanan AS, kalebu disiksa air, diancam karo bor listrik lan senjata api sing lagi diisi, nalika telanjang lan ditutupi, lan ancaman marang keluargane. Pengacarane ngargayani penyimpangan iki ngilangi hak pemerintah kanggo ngadili—utawa ngajeni karo mati. Sistem komisi militer, sing diwatesi presiden George W. Bush lan direvisi dening presiden Barack Obama, wis lama kena kritik amarga ngijini kesaksian dipaksa nanging nyembunyikan bukti penyiksaan. ACLU ngomong sistem iki adil. 'Kajaba pengadilan federal, komisi militer ngijini kesaksian dipaksa—nanging nyembunyikan bukti penyiksaan sing nduweké,' ungkap Denny LeBoeuf saka Proyek Hukuman Mati ACLU. Saat persidangan siap maju, Brigjen Mark Martins, jaksa utama anyar, lagi masuk ing peran sing penting. Lulusan terbaik West Point, Beasiswa Rhodes, lan lulusan cumlaude Harvard Law, Martins dianggap pemerintah minangka tokoh sing bisa ngembalikaké kredibilitas sistem komisi militer. Dheweke bisa nggawe reformasi kaya siaran langsung acara militer karo video kabel—karo tombol 'mati' kanggo mblokir audio yen informasi rahasia negara diucapaké. Al-Nashiri iku salah siji saka 171 tahanan sing tetep ing Guantanamo Bay. Kasus iki mewakili pangadilan pisanan ing bawah kerangka komisi militer saiki lan minangka tes kritis kanggo sistem iki sadurunge proses besar 9/11 maju.

article_content: A striking new development dubbed 'The London Octopus' has been officially unveiled by developers Galliard Group and London & Bath Estates. This 160-foot-tall office tower, designed to resemble an octopus when viewed from above, will be clad in 6,000 square feet of LED screens displaying dynamic advertisements. Located near the busy Chiswick Roundabout in west London, the building will offer 46,500 square feet of premium office space, a grand double-height entrance lobby, and underground parking. Despite receiving planning permission in 2012, construction was delayed until market conditions improved. Now fully cleared and ready for launch, the project is listed for £120 million, with developers expecting a fierce bidding war among global investors. Speculation points to interest from royal families in Qatar and Dubai — including Her Highness Sheikha Mozah bint Nasser Al Missned of the Qatar Foundation and His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum of Dubai — who may see the building as a prestigious addition to their London real estate portfolios. The structure is projected to be seen daily by over one million commuters, with its advertising screens reaching a cumulative audience equivalent to the entire U.S. population within 11 months. Proponents argue it represents a bold new chapter in urban branding, likening it to a 21st-century Piccadilly Circus. However, the project has faced longstanding opposition from local residents and safety advocates, who warn that massive digital billboards beside a major highway could pose visual distractions and set a dangerous precedent for the city’s skyline. Critics fear it may lead to a 'Blade Runner'-style urban landscape dominated by glowing ads. Stephen Conway, CEO of Galliard Group, stated: 'The London Octopus is the most futuristic and exciting commercial building ever launched in London.' Kim Gottlieb, CEO of London & Bath Estates, added: 'We’ve already received strong interest from sovereign wealth funds and multinational corporations eager to showcase their brands on this unprecedented platform.'

article_content: By Tim Shipman. PUBLISHED: 21:26 EST, 14 October 2012. | UPDATED: 03:24 EST, 15 October 2012. Showdown: Chief Whip Andrew Mitchell will face the backbench 1922 Committee on Wednesday. Senior Conservative backbenchers will warn Mitchell that his foul-mouthed outburst at police officers has damaged the party and eroded support among MPs. The Tory Chief Whip will receive this message during a meeting with a six-member delegation from the influential 1922 Committee on Wednesday. The meeting is one of three major challenges Mitchell must overcome if he hopes to retain his position, according to senior Tories. Mitchell is under increasing pressure to resign following allegations that he called police officers 'f******* plebs' after they denied him access to Downing Street by bicycle. Mitchell says he will sit beside David Cameron during Prime Minister’s Questions at noon on Wednesday. Labour MPs have launched a 'Get Mitchell' campaign and plan to disrupt PMQs by shouting abuse at both Mitchell and Cameron for refusing to dismiss him. Later that afternoon, Tory MPs with grievances will have an opportunity to voice their concerns during a scheduled segment of the 1922 Committee meeting. Chairman Graham Brady will lead the delegation to meet Mitchell afterward. Allies of Mitchell claim he retains the backing of most ministers and MPs, though many have privately suggested he should step down. 'It is the 1922 Committee’s role to convey MPs’ views to the Chief Whip. You can be sure they will do so,' said one senior committee member. Mitchell will face additional pressure as Labour candidates running for newly created crime commissioner positions are being urged to publicly state whether they believe he should resign. Labour sources confirm that candidates will receive letters challenging them to take a stance on Mitchell’s future. Conservative Chairman Graham Brady will lead the meeting with Mitchell. Yesterday, several cabinet ministers publicly defended Mitchell, criticizing the Police Federation for using the incident as leverage in its dispute over funding cuts. The Police Federation of West Mercia had called for Mitchell’s resignation after a meeting on Friday, despite the Metropolitan Police officers involved having accepted his apology. Justice Secretary Chris Grayling said: 'His conduct was unacceptable, and he has acknowledged that. He has apologized. I think the matter should now be put to rest. He has issued a full, public apology and apologized directly to the officer concerned.' 'It is a mistake for the Police Federation to exploit this incident in this manner. We need to focus on addressing the real challenges facing policing,' Grayling added. Tory chairman Grant Shapps stated: 'Clearly, such behavior is unhelpful—you should never be rude to a police officer.' When asked how many MPs had approached him demanding Mitchell’s resignation, Shapps replied: 'I cannot recall a single MP who has come to me.'

article_content: It’s hard to imagine a more painful reminder of decline than watching Nemanja Vidic thrive at Inter Milan — a player United once let go for nothing. Inter’s sporting director, Piero Ausilio, didn’t mince words: Vidic was a free, flawless signing who brought leadership, grit, and winning DNA to San Siro. Meanwhile, at Old Trafford, the defense has become a punchline. With Chris Smalling suspended, Phil Jones, Jonny Evans, and Rafael all sidelined, Louis van Gaal has been forced to cobble together a backline from midfielders, wingers, and teenagers. Against Manchester City, the lineup read like a fantasy draft gone wrong: Antonio Valencia at right-back, Michael Carrick in the center, 19-year-old Paddy McNair alongside rookie Luke Shaw. Even Marcos Rojo, United’s sole £16 million summer defensive signing, is out with a dislocated shoulder. The result? A 1-0 loss and a defense described by Jamie Redknapp as 'the worst back four you’ll ever see.' The cupboard isn’t just bare — it’s practically empty. The next tier of defenders includes Tyler Blackett, Tom Thorpe, Reece James, Marnick Vermijl, and 17-year-old Saidy Janko — all with fewer than 10 Premier League appearances combined. Thorpe, captain of the U21s and a Youth Cup winner, is seen as the future. But right now, Van Gaal isn’t building a dynasty — he’s improvising with players who’ve never played a full 90 minutes in the top flight. January can’t come soon enough.

article_content: Vince Cable, the UK’s Business Secretary, has sounded the alarm over Britain’s declining appeal to high-spending Chinese visitors, blaming overly rigid visa rules. He warns that while countries like France and Germany are rolling out the red carpet, the UK is pushing away potential economic boosters with red tape. With Chinese tourist spending having surged 400% in the past decade — and each visitor averaging £1,600 — Cable argues that the UK can't afford to stay on the sidelines. He insists that opening borders to genuine travelers and investors isn’t about weakening security, but about recognizing China’s growing economic power as an opportunity, not a threat. Cable’s stance, published in the Telegraph, puts him at odds with Home Secretary Theresa May, who defends the current system as robust and worthy of pride. Yet even within his own coalition, figures like George Osborne agree with Cable’s vision of Britain as an open, globally competitive hub. The reality? Only 180,000 Chinese tourists visited the UK in 2011 — a tiny fraction compared to mainland Europe. Cable’s message is clear: if Britain wants to thrive in the global economy, it must stop acting like it’s closed for business.

article_content: A government audit has revealed that the U.S. State Department has no clear record of how $1.2 billion meant to train Iraqi police was spent. The funds, awarded to contractor DynCorp International, vanished into a tangle of missing paperwork and unchecked invoices. According to Glenn Furbish, a veteran auditor with the Special Inspector General for Iraq Reconstruction (SIGIR), the department simply couldn’t say what was bought—or even if it was delivered. While Iraqi police were indeed trained and some gear was distributed, the supporting documents from DynCorp were chaotic, and INL, the office in charge, admitted it hadn’t verified most payments made before October of last year. With no proper tracking system, the situation opened the door to possible waste—and even fraud. Furbish, who spent two years on the ground in Iraq, compared the chaos to many other post-invasion efforts: too much work, too few people, and too little structure. The State Department acknowledges the mess. Spokesperson Susan Pittman confirmed that staffing in both Washington and Baghdad is being expanded—from four to eleven in the capital, and five to seven in Iraq—as soon as security clearances are processed. But even then, it could take years to sort through the backlog. DynCorp’s representative, Gregory Lagana, said their operations are inherently complex—buying everything from bulletproof vests to radios—and occasional billing errors happen, though they often catch them internally during routine audits. This report is the second in a planned series of ten reviews by Congress into how billions in reconstruction money were handled. Earlier, a similar audit slammed Bechtel for poor oversight. Officials say progress is being made, but the road to accountability remains long.

article_content: This is the moment a stray cat was pulled from its hiding place by firefighters after becoming wedged in the engine of a car. The startled animal appeared far from amused after being rescued from the engine block in the city of Van, eastern Turkey. Driver Nurullah Kurman discovered the cat after noticing his vehicle was not driving properly while on his way to the shops. After attempting — and failing — to free the cat himself, the 40-year-old called the fire service for help. Even emergency crews initially struggled to find a solution. Mr. Kurman told local media: 'I opened the hood and realized there was a cat inside, interfering with the mechanism. I tried to get it out but failed, so I called the fire service to see if they could help.' He said he was worried about driving with the animal inside, fearing a possible crash, and didn’t want to see the cat hurt. Despite trying several methods — including pouring cold water on the cat — firefighters eventually decided to tow the car to a nearby garage. Mechanics spent two hours dismantling the vehicle before firefighters could reach inside and extract the cat. The stray cat is now recovering after receiving veterinary treatment for a broken leg, likely sustained during its ordeal. Photos show the soaked cat being handed over to staff from an animal charity. Charity officials are working to find the cat a new home. Mr. Kurman, who was billed £50 for the repairs, added: 'I thought that since I called the firefighters and they towed the car here, the state would cover the cost. It’s a stray cat — why should I have to pay?' In the end, he paid the bill and left, saying: 'I hope the cat recovers soon. Next time, it should stay away from car engines — no matter how warm and inviting they may seem.'

article_content: In 2013, Tanya Bardsley—a reality TV personality known for ITVBe’s The Real Housewives of Cheshire—experienced a harrowing violation while asleep in a hotel room. After attending a family celebration, she returned to the hotel exhausted and intoxicated, falling into a deep sleep while her husband, footballer Phil Bardsley, remained out with friends. She awoke in confusion to find a stranger touching her body. Terrified, she screamed and immediately called Phil, who rushed back with friends and contacted the police. Tanya was taken to the hospital for forensic exams, enduring painful and distressing procedures to determine if rape had occurred. Thankfully, the results confirmed sexual assault but not rape. Still, the trauma lingered. What haunted her most was learning a hotel staff member had entered her room while she lay unconscious, naked, under a clearly displayed ‘Do Not Disturb’ sign. Though the employee later admitted to moving her body during the incident, he denied any sexual intent. Despite Tanya’s cooperation with law enforcement and a months-long investigation, the Crown Prosecution Service concluded there was insufficient evidence to pursue charges. Devastated but determined, Tanya decided to break her silence. She waived her legal right to anonymity and shared her story in her memoir, Just A Girl Who Got It All, hoping to give voice to others who’ve suffered in silence. Her journey—from being a single mother working in a call center to becoming a published author and reality TV star—mirrors her resilience. She credits Phil as her anchor through the pain, though healing took years. ‘Holding onto anger only hurt me and the people I love,’ she says. Today, she channels her pain into advocacy and visibility, turning her personal tragedy into a platform for change.

article_content: Mauricio Pochettino said Tottenham Hotspur can expect to win major silverware within two years but warned that difficult times lie ahead. The Spurs manager said: 'Sometimes to change something, you need time. You need to suffer and endure bad moments. We know we're heading in the right direction. It may take six months, one year, or two years — but I'm sure the club will eventually win an important trophy.' Pochettino believes his Tottenham Hotspur side should aim for a trophy within the next two years. The team trained ahead of their Europa League clash with Asteras Tripolis on Thursday. Spurs sit third in their Europa League group and host the Greek Super League side on Thursday. They slipped to ninth in the Premier League after a 4-1 defeat at Manchester City on Saturday. Despite winning just two of their last nine games, they remain only two points away from a Champions League place — far from a crisis. The concern, however, is that key players are struggling to deliver. Roberto Soldado, a £26 million striker with just six goals in 31 league appearances, had his penalty saved by Joe Hart in his first league start of the season against City, while Emmanuel Adebayor has scored only once this campaign. Add to that defensive frailties in big games — including a 3-0 home loss to Liverpool — and it's clear why Spurs have the worst goal difference in the top half of the table. Pochettino admitted results are a concern but remains focused on the bigger picture. 'We need to start scoring goals, but we have confidence in our strikers,' he said. 'We made many changes at the start of the season, introducing a new philosophy. The same happened at Southampton when we arrived. In four or five months, we hope to have changed the mentality. We need time — then we’ll show more consistency.' Spurs chairman Daniel Levy is known for quickly replacing managers, having overseen ten different head coaches in his 13-year tenure. But Pochettino insists he and the board share the same vision. 'When they offered me the job, Daniel was very clear: we need to move the club forward. We agreed — we want to build something special at Tottenham, different but better than before.' The rebuilding process continues as Spurs host Asteras Tripolis, who lead Group C after defeating Partizan Belgrade and drawing with Besiktas. Spurs have drawn both their previous Europa League matches. Harry Kane could make another European appearance for Tottenham. Asteras Tripolis’s squad includes seven Argentines, including strikers Facundo Parra and Pablo Mazza. Pochettino, a former Argentina international, knows how dangerous his compatriots can be. 'It's a very good team,' he said. 'I know a lot about these Argentines — they're offensive, brave, and we expect a tough game.' Left-back Ben Davies, who has struggled to secure regular playing time since joining from Swansea in the summer, is expected to start. The 21-year-old said he won’t complain as he competes with Danny Rose for the starting spot. Pochettino remained non-committal about whether Davies will become his first choice. 'He’s still young. We knew his potential when we signed him. It’s competition with Danny Rose. I have a strong squad, but we must pick the players who can get three points on Thursday. It’s a very important game.'

article_content: This week, Phoenix, Arizona kicked off the 23rd edition of the Scott Firefighter Combat World Challenge — a high-stakes, globally recognized competition where elite firefighters from across the planet push their limits under extreme conditions. Teams from nations like the U.S., Canada, New Zealand, Portugal, and France have gathered not just to win, but to showcase the raw physicality behind their daily work. Dressed head to toe in full turnout gear and breathing through respirators, competitors race against the clock to conquer a brutal five-stage obstacle course. Tasks include scaling a five-story tower, lifting heavy equipment, wielding axes, hauling fire hoses, and carrying a 175-pound mannequin simulating a rescued victim — all while sweat pours and hearts pound. Organized annually, the event isn’t just about athleticism; it’s a powerful public demonstration of what firefighters truly endure when lives hang in the balance. Viewers tuning in via ESPN witness not just sport, but sacrifice. Preliminary rounds continue through November 7, with the championship finals set for Saturday, November 8.

article_content: There’s a classic joke: if you play a country song in reverse, the singer gets their job back, wins their lover over, finds what they lost, stops crying, and walks out of the bar—sober and happy. Sounds like a fantasy, right? Because in today’s America, that kind of clean ending feels rare. But what makes country music endure isn’t the fairy-tale endings—it’s the raw truth in every lyric. Karla Lawson, a morning host at Nashville’s WSIX, puts it plainly: 'It’s real. It’s simple. It speaks to everyday life. That’s why it’s the most honest music out there.' On November 9, the Country Music Association celebrates its 45th annual awards show live on ABC—a staple among the most-watched award ceremonies, ranking right beside the Oscars, Grammys, and Golden Globes. This year’s lineup isn’t just country legends like Rascal Flatts and Kenny Chesney; it’s also pop icon Natasha Bedingfield, rock powerhouse Grace Potter, and Motown legend Lionel Richie, whose new duets album 'Tuskegee' proves country’s reach is wider than ever. The genre’s expansion didn’t happen overnight. For over 20 years, country has quietly grown, starting with trailblazers like Garth Brooks and Trisha Yearwood in the '90s who blurred lines between cowboy boots and leather jackets. Soon, hits like Shania Twain’s 'I Feel Like a Woman' and Billy Ray Cyrus’s 'Achy Breaky Heart' were stuck in everyone’s heads—even if they’d never set foot in a honky-tonk. Since then, artists from nearly every genre have dipped their toes in: Kid Rock, Sheryl Crow, Bon Jovi, Hootie & the Blowfish’s Darius Rucker, Jewel, even Jessica Simpson. But 2010–2011 marked a turning point. Gwyneth Paltrow belted out a country ballad on live TV. Justin Bieber announced a collab with Rascal Flatts, sending teen fans into overdrive. Lady Antebellum swept the Grammys. Lady Gaga performed a country-style rendition of 'Born This Way' (though Little Big Town’s version stole the spotlight). Even 'Footloose' got a full country makeover—with Blake Shelton leading the soundtrack and inviting original star Kenny Loggins to join him at the CMAs. And it wasn’t just the charts. The World Series opened with three straight country singers: 'American Idol' champ Scotty McCreery, Trace Adkins, and Ronnie Dunn. Bieber included The Band Perry on his holiday album. Jason Aldean and Lady Gaga were the first names announced for the Grammy nominations special. And now, rumors swirl that Adele—fresh off global domination—is planning a country album, calling the discovery of American country artists 'like being a 4-year-old in a candy shop all over again.' As Scott Stem of the CMA jokes, 'Everyone likes country music—they just won’t admit it.' What pulls people in isn’t the fame or the crossover hype. It’s the stories. The heartbreak. The small victories. The missed jobs, the lost loved ones, the sudden joy. In a world full of noise, country music still whispers the truth—and that’s why it feels more American than ever.

Kaya mimpi, kan? Amarga ing Amerika saiki, akhir sing apik kaya ngono rasane ilang. Nanging apa sing nyebabake musik country tetep eksis bukan akhir sing sempurna—namung kejujuran ing saben lirik. Karla Lawson, host pagi ing WSIX Nashville, ngomong nganggo jelas: 'Nyata. Simpel. Nggawe hubungan karo urip sehari-hari. Iku sebabé iku musik paling jujur ing donya.' Ing 9 Nopember, Asosiasi Musik Country nglakoni acara penghargaan taunan kaping-45 live ing ABC—acara sing tetep ana ing jajaran panggung paling ditonton, njaba Oscar, Grammy, lan Golden Globe. Tahun iki, daftar penampil ora mung legenda country kaya Rascal Flatts lan Kenny Chesney; padha uga pop Natasha Bedingfield, rocker Grace Potter, lan legenda Motown Lionel Richie, sing album duet anyaré 'Tuskegee' mbuktekake jangkauan country sing luwih luas. Pengembangan genre iki ora langsung kaya ngono. Saka 20 taun, country wis berkembang pelan-pelan, dimulai karo pelopor kaya Garth Brooks lan Trisha Yearwood ing taun '90-an sing ngilangi batas antara sepatu boot lan kulit. Sawise iku, hit kaya 'I Feel Like a Woman' saka Shania Twain lan 'Achy Breaky Heart' saka Billy Ray Cyrus katon nganggo nyanyian ing saben kepala—nak maneh wong ora pernah mlebu bar country. Sajen iku, artis saka kabeh genre wis nyoba-nyoba: Kid Rock, Sheryl Crow, Bon Jovi, Darius Rucker saka Hootie & the Blowfish, Jewel, malah Jessica Simpson. Nanging 2010–2011 dadi titik balik. Gwyneth Paltrow nyanyi lagu country live ing TV. Justin Bieber ngumumake kolaborasi karo Rascal Flatts, nyebabake para remaja heboh. Lady Antebellum menang kaping-kaping ing Grammy. Lady Gaga nyanyi versi country saka 'Born This Way' (meski versi Little Big Town luwih apik). Bahkan 'Footloose' diubah dadi versi country—Blake Shelton pimpin soundtrack lan undang bintang asli Kenny Loggins muncul ing CMAs. Uga, iki ora mung nang chart. Tiga penyanyi lagu kebangsaan pertama ing World Series iku artis country: pemenang 'American Idol' Scotty McCreery, Trace Adkins, lan Ronnie Dunn. Bieber masukke The Band Perry ing album Natalé. Jason Aldean lan Lady Gaga dadi nama pertama sing diumumake kanggo konser nominasi Grammy. Lan saiki, kabar gosip nyebut bahwa Adele—sing lagi lagi dadi bintang global—rencanane bakal rekam album country, nyebut nemu musisi country Amerika 'kaya bocah umur 4 taun ing toko permen sing nemokake permen maneh.' Kaya sing dikatake Scott Stem saka CMA, 'Saben orang suka musik country—namun ora mau ngaku.' Sing nyedot wong iki ora ketenaran utawa promosi lintas genre. Iku cerita-cerita. Patah hati. Kemenangan cilik. Pekerjaan sing ilang, orang sing ilang, sukacita sing dadakan. Ing dunia sing penuh kebisingan, musik country tetep bisikake kebenaran—lan iku sebabé rasane luwih Amerika saka kapanpun.

article_content: For more than half a century, Paul Brockmann has shown his love for his wife Margot in the most extraordinary way: by buying her a new dress for every ballroom dance they shared. Over 56 years, that adds up to 55,000 gowns — a collection so vast it filled six storage units. Paul, now 78, first discovered ballroom dancing at age 13 in Germany, and when he met Margot at a dance floor in the 1950s, he knew she was the one. He followed her to America, even when it meant losing touch with his family. Their life together unfolded across the Midwest before settling in Los Angeles, where Paul’s passion for vintage 1950s dresses blossomed into an all-consuming quest. He scoured estate sales, flea markets, and department stores, sometimes returning home with 30 new dresses in a single day. It wasn’t just about the style — he imagined Margot twirling in each one, the rustle of tulle, the sway of a full skirt. Size didn’t matter; if he loved the look, he bought it, convinced she’d eventually fit into it. Many dresses remain unworn. Now, after decades of collecting, health challenges and the cost of storing thousands of garments have led the couple to sell most of the collection online. But they’re keeping a handful of favorites — the first dress he ever bought her, and the one that makes the perfect swishing sound when she dances. What Paul didn’t realize when he bought them? Some of these dresses are now rare vintage treasures by legendary designers like Oscar de La Renta and Vera Wang — hidden gems in a love story written in silk and satin.

Kebanyakan baju ora kepake. Saiki, sawatara taun ngumpulake, masalah kesehatan lan biaya simpenan ratusan ribu baju nyebabke pasangan iki njual kebanyakan koleksi neng situs web. article_content: By Daily Mail Reporter. Osama bin Laden’s words to his son-in-law hours after the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks were recounted during a surprise testimony in Manhattan today. Sulaiman Abu Ghaith, who was recruited as a spokesperson for al-Qaeda, told the court how bin Laden arranged for him to be driven to a meeting in an Afghan cave. Upon arrival, Abu Ghaith recalled bin Laden saying: 'Did you hear what happened? We are the ones who did it.' When bin Laden asked what he thought would happen next, Abu Ghaith testified that he responded: 'America will not rest until it kills you and topples the Taliban.' Bin Laden replied: 'You’re being too pessimistic.' Then, he instructed Abu Ghaith: 'I want to deliver a message to the world. I want you to deliver it.' The testimony came during Abu Ghaith’s trial on charges of conspiring to kill Americans and aiding al-Qaeda as its spokesperson. He is the highest-ranking member of bin Laden’s inner circle to face trial in a U.S. civilian court. His decision to testify was announced by his lawyer, Stanley Cohen, surprising a nearly empty courtroom that quickly filled with spectators. Abu Ghaith, seated to the right in court sketches, appeared calm while testifying—wearing a blue shirt, open at the collar, under a charcoal jacket. His hands were often folded, but he gestured for emphasis. Abu Ghaith testified that he first traveled to Afghanistan in June 2001 out of a 'serious desire to understand the new Islamic government.' He met bin Laden after the al-Qaeda leader, based in Kandahar, summoned him upon learning he was a Kuwaiti preacher. Bin Laden reportedly said the harsh conditions in training camps needed balance—he wanted Abu Ghaith to reach recruits emotionally and show them another side of life. Although Abu Ghaith knew bin Laden was suspected in past attacks—including the 1998 U.S. embassy bombings and the 2000 USS Cole attack—he said he still wanted to 'see what he had, what he wanted.' He claimed his televised sermons, which warned of future attacks and called for Muslim resistance, were based solely on bin Laden’s words, not his own planning. He denied having prior knowledge of Richard Reid’s failed 2001 shoe bomb plot. 'My intention was to deliver a message I believed in,' he said. 'I hoped the U.S. would say, “Let’s sit down and talk,” but America did what I expected.' On cross-examination, prosecutor Michael Ferrara pressed him on why he met bin Laden despite knowing al-Qaeda was responsible for hundreds of American deaths. Abu Ghaith replied he went only out of respect for bin Laden as a sheikh and to learn his intentions. He described bin Laden as 'worried' on September 11. U.S. District Judge Lewis A. Kaplan has not yet ruled on Cohen’s renewed request to call Khalid Sheikh Mohammed—a prisoner at Guantanamo Bay—as a witness via video link. Cohen withdrew the motion temporarily, acknowledging it was not the right moment.

Sawise tiba, Abu Ghaith inget bin Laden nyebut: 'Kowe gelem apa sing wis kajaba? Kita sing nduwe iku.' Sawise bin Laden nanyani apa sing dikira bakal kajaba, Abu Ghaith nglaporake yen dheweke njawab: 'Amérika ora bakal mutus kanti nemokake kowe lan nggulingaké negara Taliban.' Bin Laden njawab: 'Kowe kebangetan pesimis.' Banjur, bin Laden nyaurake juru bicara iku: 'Aku pengin ngirim pesen kana dunya. Aku pengin kowe ngirim pesen iku.' Pangadilan iki ndadekaké sidang Abu Ghaith kanggo tuntutan nggabungake pembunuhan wong Amérika lan mbantu al-Qaeda minangka juru bicara kelompok teror. Dheweke yaiku tokoh paling senior neng lingkaran kadheman bin Laden sing diajukaké neng pangadilan sipil Amérika. Keputusan dheweke kanggo ngadeg minangka saksi diumumaké dening penasihat hukume, Stanley Cohen, sing ngagetaké pangadilan sing banter kosong nanging cepet dipadheti wong-wong sing padha nyimak. Abu Ghaith, neng sisi kanan neng gambar sketsa, tampak rileks nalika ngadeg—mangkone baju biru, dibuka neng leher, ing ngisor jaket warna abu-abu gelap. Tangane kadhang-kadhang dilipat, nanging kadhang-kadhang diangkat kanggo ngedhongkong. Abu Ghaith nggawe pangadilan yen dheweke mlebu Afganistan pertama kali ing Juni 2001 amarga 'kemauan serius kanggo ngerti pemerintahan Islam anyar neng Afganistan.' Dheweke ketemu bin Laden sawise pimpinan al-Qaeda, sing tinggal neng Kandahar, nglamar dheweke sawise mendhem yen dheweke iku pendeta saka Kuwait. Bin Laden kabeh yen kondisi keras neng kamp pelatihan kudu diimbangi—dheweke pengin Abu Ghaith nyentuh hati para rekrut lan nuduhaké sisi liyane kehidupan. Nanging, Abu Ghaith ngerti bin Laden dicurigai neng serangan masa lampau—termasuk serangan kantor kedutaan Amérika neng Kenya lan Tanzania taun 1998 lan serangan USS Cole taun 2000—nanging dheweke tetep pengin 'ngerti apa sing dheweke duwe, apa sing dheweke pengin.' Dheweke ngaku pesen-pesen sing diwiwiti neng video, sing ngancam serangan liyane kana Amérika lan ngajak wong Islam njaluk dukungan, mung didasarké katrangan bin Laden, bukan rencanane dhewe. Dheweke nolak dugaan pemerintah yen dheweke duwe informasi sabanjure neng serangan sepatu bom gagal dening Richard Reid taun 2001. 'Niatku mung ngirim pesen sing aku yakin,' dheweke ngombe. 'Aku harap Amérika bakal ngombe, “Ayo kita duduk lan ngobrol,” nanging Amérika njaluk apa sing aku ekspektasi.' Neng pangadilan silang, jaksa Michael Ferrara nanyani Abu Ghaith babagan alasan dheweke ketemu bin Laden nanging ngerti al-Qaeda tanggung jawab kanggo ratusan korban wong Amérika. Abu Ghaith njawab dheweke mung mlebu amarga hormat kana bin Laden minangka syekh lan kanggo ngerti maksud dheweke. Dheweke nggambaraké bin Laden minangka 'cemas' neng 11 September. Hakim Pengadilan Federal AS Lewis A. Kaplan belum ngluarkan putusan neng permintaan Cohen kanggo ngajak Khalid Sheikh Mohammed—tahanan neng Guantanamo Bay, Kuba—minangka saksi neng jaringan video. Cohen mundur permintaan iku sawise ngakoni yen iku ora wektune.
