article_content: A 19-year-old Kentucky woman who has been missing for more than a week is believed to be with a registered sex offender with a history of kidnapping and unlawful confinement, authorities said Tuesday. Brittney Kustes was last seen on July 17 at her grandparents' home in Brooks, just south of Louisville, according to Detective Scott McGaha of the Bullitt County Sheriff’s Office. Witnesses reported that Roy Vernon Elwell, 34, was seen driving repeatedly along the street where Kustes’ grandparents live on the day she disappeared. 'Shortly after, she was gone,' McGaha told CNN. Since her disappearance, multiple individuals—including friends of Elwell—have reported seeing the pair in Louisville and nearby areas. 'We think they’re staying close because Elwell has contacts here and a built-in support system,' McGaha said. Kustes’ mother, Laurie Kustes, said her daughter had prior contact with Elwell involving drugs. 'This guy came into my daughter’s life with drugs,' she told WHAS. The last time Elwell was with Brittney, she returned home addicted to methamphetamine—a habit she had recently overcome. McGaha, who knows Kustes personally, encountered her shortly before she vanished. 'She looked really good,' he said. Her mother echoed this, telling WHAS, 'She was doing great. We talked every day. There was no reason for her to leave. She hated this guy.' McGaha believes Kustes is being held against her will. 'What I believe from the information we’re receiving is that drugs are being given to her,' he said. Laurie Kustes told HLN’s 'Issues with Jane Velez-Mitchell' that 'it’s a very sick, sick situation.' 'There is no way she left with him intending not to come back,' she said. She added that witnesses reported Kustes has attempted to escape and use her cellphone—but Elwell controls all her devices. McGaha confirmed Elwell is aware police want to speak with him. Friends say Elwell laughs off requests to turn himself in. Meanwhile, he remains noncompliant with Kentucky’s sex offender registry laws—a Class D felony punishable by up to five years in prison. CNN’s Sarah Aarthun contributed to this report.

Brittney Kustes pungkasan kali dipandang ing 17 Juli ing omah nenek-neneké ing Brooks, tenggara Louisville, menurut Detektif Scott McGaha saka Kantor Sheriff Bullitt County. Saksi melapor yen Roy Vernon Elwell, 34, dikendelake ngadeg-ngadeg ing jalan tempat omah nenek-nenek Kustes ana ing dina ilangé. 'Sawise iku, dia ilang,' ujar McGaha marang CNN. Sawise ilange, sawetara wong—kang kalebu teman-teman Elwell—melapor dheweke ndeleng pasangan iki ing Louisville lan wilayah sekitare. 'Kami yakin wong-wong iki tetep deket amarga Elwell duwe kontak ing diek lan sistem pendukung sing wis ana,' ujar McGaha. Ibu Kustes, Laurie Kustes, nyebut putriningé pernah kena pengaruh Elwell ngluwari obat-obatan. 'Pria iki nyerbu urip putriku karo obat-obatan,' ujare marang WHAS. Saat pungkasan Elwell karo Brittney, dia balik ngomah karo kecanduan metamphetamine—kebiasaan sing wis katon ora karo. McGaha, sing kenal Kustes sawetara, ketemu putri iki sawetara sadurunge ilang. article_content: In a remarkable display of stamina and dedication, Ben Berger, a former professional golfer from Indiana, completed 612 holes of golf in just 16 hours to support a cause close to his heart: autism awareness. Starting at 5:29 a.m. and finishing at sunset — 9:30 p.m. — at Juday Creek Golf Club, Berger kept up an astonishing pace, averaging more than two full 18-hole rounds every hour. Riding a golf cart between shots, he managed to complete each par-four hole in about 90 seconds, only slowing down slightly as hip pain began to set in near the end. His performance wasn’t just about endurance — it was also about precision. Berger carded 95 birdies and five eagles throughout the day, with his final eagle coming on the last hole after a spectacular chip-in. Of his 33 total rounds, 12 were at or under par, and even his worst round was a respectable 82. The event, part of 'Par for the Cause,' has raised more than $200,000 over five years to benefit autism organizations. While Berger’s effort is extraordinary, it doesn’t top the official Guinness World Record: Robb James of Canada completed 851 holes in 24 hours using a cart on a nine-hole course. Berger, who once worked as a pro at a nearby club before joining his family business, was cheered on by a crowd of supporters — including his wife Stephanie, who is eight months pregnant. As he sank his final putt, he shouted, 'That’s the way you finish!' before embracing her, the putter still in her hand.

Mulai pukul 05.29 pagi dan berakhir saat matahari terbenam — pukul 21.30 — di Juday Creek Golf Club, Berger menjaga kecepatan menakjubkan, rata-rata lebih dari dua putaran penuh 18 lubang setiap jam. Menggunakan kereta golf antar shot, ia berhasil menyelesaikan tiap lubang par-empat dalam sekitar 90 detik, hanya melambat sedikit saat nyeri pinggul mulai muncul di akhir. Performanya bukan hanya soal ketahanan — tapi juga presisi. Berger mencatat 95 birdie dan lima eagle sepanjang hari, dengan eagle terakhir datang di lubang terakhir setelah chip yang spektakuler. Dari 33 putaran totalnya, 12 di antaranya sama atau lebih baik dari par, bahkan putaran terburuknya pun tetap layak yaitu 82. Acara ini, bagian dari 'Par for the Cause,' telah mengumpulkan lebih dari $200.000 selama lima tahun untuk mendukung organisasi autis. Meski usaha Berger luar biasa, ia belum mengalahkan rekor resmi Guinness World Records: Robb James dari Kanada menyelesaikan 851 lubang dalam 24 jam menggunakan kereta golf di lapangan sembilan lubang. Berger, yang dulunya bekerja sebagai pro di klub terdekat sebelum bergabung dengan bisnis keluarganya, didukung oleh banyak pendukung — termasuk istrinya Stephanie, yang sedang hamil delapan bulan. Saat ia memasukkan putt terakhir, ia berseru, 'Itulah cara kamu menyelesaikannya!' sebelum merangkul istrinya, tongkat putter masih di tangannya.

article_content: Joe Launchbury could have been courted by top clubs like Saracens, but instead, he chose to stay with Wasps — and for deeply personal reasons. At 23, the England lock didn’t just see a contract; he saw a future. With a baby on the way and a desire to grow as a player, he needed more than just a paycheck — he needed belonging. That’s why he signed a three-year extension, even though leaving might’ve meant more money or glamour elsewhere. The real pull? Dai Young, Wasps’ director of rugby. A former British & Irish Lions prop and a man Launchbury calls 'incredibly wise', Young’s mentorship shaped his development. Launchbury didn’t just admire Young’s tactical brain — he trusted his character. And then there was the club’s big move: securing a permanent home at the Ricoh Arena in Coventry. After years of bouncing between grounds, Wasps finally had roots. Launchbury was awestruck by the new training facilities — state-of-the-art, professional, intentional. 'This is the kind of environment I believe in,' he said. For him, staying wasn’t loyalty; it was alignment. Meanwhile, in France, Wales star Jonathan Davies isn’t hiding his disappointment. Despite a foot injury slowing his start at Clermont Auvergne, he refuses to use it as an excuse. His coach, Franck Azema, didn’t sugarcoat things — telling him plainly his performances were below par. Davies didn’t argue. 'He’s right,' he admitted. 'I need to do better.' On the other side of the world, Australia’s Kurtley Beale got a second chance. After being fined AU$45,000 for sending an inappropriate photo to an ARU staff member, a tribunal spared him from suspension or dismissal. Beale called the outcome 'relieving' and vowed to rebuild trust — with teammates, fans, and the wider Australian public. For now, he’s back in the Wallabies camp, ready to prove he’s more than his mistake.

article_content: The Christmas period in football is notorious for turning up the heat on managers — and right now, two are feeling it more than most. Ronald Koeman, once riding high after a stunning start with Southampton, has now lost five games in a row. What began as a dream season — following the departure of the club’s CEO, captain, and star players — has turned into a battle for survival. Fans expected a scrap against relegation, but few predicted this level of early brilliance. Now, every slip-up is met with growing criticism. Losing to Manchester City or Arsenal? Understandable. But falling to Burnley and then being knocked out by Sheffield United? That’s where the real questions begin. Koeman, usually composed, snapped after refusing to shake hands with Nigel Clough, a rare display of emotion that revealed just how much the pressure is getting to him. Meanwhile, Steve Bruce’s Hull City are in freefall. Just one win in 15 matches. Nineteenth in the table. After last season’s miraculous FA Cup run and Premier League escape, Hull splashed out £40 million in the summer. The big-money buys — Abel Hernandez for £10m, Robert Snodgrass for £8m, Michael Dawson for £10m — have mostly been disasters, hampered by injuries and minimal impact. Hernandez, the club’s record signing, has netted just three goals. Bruce, once a master of mid-season rescues with players like Jelavic and Long, now faces a dilemma: how many more expensive gambles can he afford before his future at the club hangs in the balance? For Koeman, this is his first true test. For Bruce, it might be his last chance.

Kalah dari Manchester City atau Arsenal? Bisa dimengerti. Tetapi kalah dari Burnley dan tersingkir oleh Sheffield United? Di situlah pertanyaan-pertanyaan serius mulai muncul. Koeman, yang biasanya tenang, meledak setelah menolak berjabat tangan dengan Nigel Clough, sebuah tindakan langka yang mengungkap betapa besarnya tekanan yang ia rasakan. Sementara itu, Hull City milik Steve Bruce tengah terjun bebas. Hanya satu kemenangan dalam 15 pertandingan. Peringkat ke-19 di liga. Setelah pencapaian luar biasa di Piala FA musim lalu dan lolos dari degradasi, Hull menggelontorkan £40 juta di musim panas. Pemain-pemain mahal — Abel Hernandez senilai £10 juta, Robert Snodgrass £8 juta, Michael Dawson £10 juta — sebagian besar gagal, terhambat cedera dan kontribusi minim. Hernandez, rekor pembelian klub, baru mencetak tiga gol. Bruce, yang dulu ahli dalam menyelamatkan tim di pertengahan musim lewat pemain seperti Jelavic dan Long, kini menghadapi dilema: berapa kali lagi ia bisa menghabiskan uang klub sebesar ini sebelum masa depannya di klub ini terancam? article_content: It’s Belgian Grand Prix weekend. As the rhythmic roar of Ferrari engines echoes in my ears and my heart races at 140 beats per minute, I can almost imagine what it’s like to be an F1 driver. But this isn’t Spa — not quite. I’m on a secret test track just minutes from the legendary circuit, where Shell and Ferrari have created an extraordinary experiment: 'The Science of Driving.' The setup? A winding course lined with snow, illuminated by a neon-lit tunnel — all designed to measure emotional intensity via heartbeat and skin conductance sensors. I’m driving a Ferrari 458 Speciale with test driver Andrea Bertolini at the wheel, while journalist Matt Morlidge captures the experience. Ferrari legends Fernando Alonso and Kimi Räikkönen had already completed their laps earlier that morning. Their heart rates? Around 170 BPM — peak race-day levels. Mine? Fluctuating between 70 and 150. The contrast is stark. The 458’s V8 engine produces around 597 horsepower — impressive, though still less than the total system output of current F1 hybrids (which exceed 1,000 hp including energy recovery). Still, its raw, naturally aspirated character delivers a visceral thrill unmatched by modern F1 cars. Shell, Ferrari’s fuel partner since 1947, explains that its V-Power Nitro fuel shares the same base hydrocarbons as retail Super Unleaded, but includes proprietary performance additives developed over 21,000 hours of laboratory testing. These enhancements optimize combustion efficiency and engine protection under extreme conditions — not a different fuel, but a refined one. Alonso, ever the competitor, remains confident: 'Mercedes have the advantage — but when I get in the car, I always believe I can win.' Räikkönen, ever the enigma, simply quipped: 'Thanks to Shell, I now know to look for tunnels when I’m not on the track.' Behind the spectacle lies a decades-long alliance built on innovation, trust, and the shared belief that even in defeat, the pursuit of excellence never stops.

Shayk has been overwhelmed with questions on Instagram from fans wondering if they had broken up. Her last post, made four days ago during a vacation in the Maldives, remains her most recent update. Representatives from her New York-based agency told Goal.com: 'The Ballon d’Or didn’t fit into her schedule—it was purely a matter of work commitments. We have no further comment.'

article_content: A sixth-grade teacher, Amy Persky Newman, 48, died by suicide after a heated phone conversation, according to a police source. Newman, who had taught for 20 years at Francis Scott Key Elementary School in South Philadelphia, left the school Thursday morning and drove about a mile south to a Holiday Inn. She was found in a bathroom stall on the first floor, surrounded by blood, with a steak knife and scissors nearby. The stall was locked when hotel staff discovered her. She was rushed to the Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania in critical condition shortly after 8 a.m. and was pronounced dead at 3:40 p.m. following surgery. Investigators later found what appeared to be a suicide note at the school. There is no indication the incident was connected to the school or occurred on school grounds. Newman, a mother of two, was described by students and colleagues as kind and dedicated. Her Facebook page featured photos with her children and husband, alongside posts expressing joy—such as 'Can't wait for summer' and 'Home after a fabulous trip with my awesome daughter.' Students and former students expressed profound grief on social media. One wrote, 'I will be praying for her friends and family. Rest in peace, Mrs. Newman.' The School District of Philadelphia confirmed that grief counselors are available for students and staff affected by the tragedy. Police reviewed surveillance footage showing Newman entering the restroom at 7:46 a.m. and confirmed she had dropped off materials at school earlier that day before leaving. To speak with a trained counselor, call the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline at 1-800-273-8255.

article_content: England suffered their fifth consecutive defeat against the All Blacks — and their fourth in just five months. In torrential rain at Twickenham, this was a demoralizing result for Stuart Lancaster’s side. After a summer tour marked by narrow losses in New Zealand, this performance felt like a step backward. The final score was entirely justified. Though a late penalty try offered some respectability, the match became a one-sided affair after halftime. England simply vanished as an attacking threat — too late to recover. The world champions seized control with poise and experience. Steve Hansen’s team handled the conditions far more intelligently, while England struggled deep in their own half. Despite plenty of heart and determination from the white shirts, they were outclassed in decision-making and composure under pressure. England lost 24–21 to New Zealand at a rain-soaked Twickenham on Saturday, undone by a dominant second-half display from the All Blacks. Though England dominated the opening quarter, they failed to convert territorial advantage into points. New Zealand gradually took command and sealed the win. England went into halftime leading 14–11, but their advantage evaporated after the break. New Zealand celebrated a hard-fought victory, thanks to clinical execution and superior game management. England’s lineup: Mike Brown; Semesa Rokoduguni, Brad Barritt, Kyle Eastmond, Jonny May; Owen Farrell, Danny Care; Billy Vunipola, Chris Robshaw (capt), Tom Wood; Courtney Lawes, Dave Attwood; David Wilson, Dylan Hartley, Joe Marler. Replacements: Rob Webber, Matt Mullan, Kieran Brookes, George Kruis, Ben Morgan, Ben Youngs, George Ford, Anthony Watson. New Zealand’s lineup: Israel Dagg; Ben Smith, Conrad Smith, Sonny Bill Williams, Julian Savea; Aaron Cruden, Aaron Smith; Kieran Read, Richie McCaw (capt), Jerome Kaino; Sam Whitelock, Brodie Retallick; Owen Franks, Dane Coles, Wyatt Crockett. Replacements: Keven Mealamu, Ben Franks, Charlie Faumuina, Patrick Tuipulotu, Liam Messam, TJ Perenara, Beauden Barrett, Ryan Crotty. England opened the scoring with a stunning solo try by Jonny May after just three minutes. Brad Barritt’s perfectly timed pass released May, who outpaced Conrad Smith and evaded Israel Dagg to touch down in the corner. Owen Farrell missed the conversion, but England were flying. They nearly doubled their lead minutes later when May caught a box-kick and attempted an offload to Farrell — but failed to connect. Moments later, Mike Brown fumbled a clear overlap chance, allowing New Zealand to regain momentum. Ben Smith recovered a high kick from Cruden, sparking a powerful All Blacks surge. Julian Savea broke through Care’s tackle, and Jerome Kaino powered over the line after a sequence of phase play. The try was awarded, though replays showed possible grounding issues. Cruden missed the conversion, leveling the scores at 7–7. Farrell kicked two penalties to restore England’s lead, but Cruden responded with a penalty of his own. Before halftime, Farrell added a third penalty to put England ahead 14–11. The turning point came in the 49th minute. With England’s debutant lock George Kruis out of position, New Zealand exploited the gap. Owen Franks carried hard, and Richie McCaw received a short pass from Israel Dagg to dive over for a try. Cruden’s difficult conversion attempt failed, leaving New Zealand ahead 16–14. England were handed a golden opportunity after Dane Coles was sin-binned for kicking out in a scrum. But instead of capitalizing, England attacked recklessly from deep in poor conditions, giving New Zealand time to regroup. Beauden Barrett added a penalty in the 64th minute to extend New Zealand’s lead to 19–14. Then, in the 72nd minute, Charlie Faumuina bulldozed over from close range after sustained pressure, making it 24–14. England rallied late with a powerful scrum, earning a penalty try that George Ford converted with a drop goal. But with just minutes remaining, the comeback was too little, too late. New Zealand held firm to secure a hard-earned win.

article_content: George Golubovskis, a homeless man in Traverse City, Michigan, has launched a write-in campaign for mayor. In a YouTube video posted on October 25, he pledged to trim his beard, get a haircut, and dress more formally if elected. The video, uploaded by user Tyler Durdin, has garnered nearly 3,000 views. Golubovskis says he does not receive public assistance and claims to hold two degrees from the University of Michigan in Ann Arbor—including a Master’s in Public Policy. He also states he has worked in politics and the private sector in Washington DC, New York, and Europe. These claims have not been independently verified. He emphasizes his commitment to local issues such as preserving open spaces, supporting the Farmers Market, and fostering creativity—particularly in blending arts with emerging high-tech industries. 'We could be the most creative community on the Great Lakes,' he says. To appear on the ballot, voters must write his name in—an option permitted under local law. However, the Traverse City City Clerk informed him that, as an unregistered voter, he is ineligible to run for office under current regulations. Despite this, he continues his campaign via social media, including an active Twitter presence.

article_content: A Japanese biotech company, Spiber, has unveiled an electric blue dress made from Qmonos — a synthetic spider silk engineered using genetically modified bacteria. The dress, displayed at Tokyo’s Roppongi Hills complex, serves as a demonstration of the material’s potential across industries including fashion, automotive, and medicine. Qmonos, derived from the Japanese word 'kumonosu' meaning 'spider web', mimics the structural protein fibroin found in natural spider silk. Gram for gram, natural spider silk exhibits a tensile strength five times greater than steel and greater flexibility than nylon. When used in body armor, it could be up to three times stronger than Kevlar, depending on the spider species. Spiders, however, cannot be farmed like silkworms. They are territorial, prone to cannibalism, and produce only tiny amounts of silk — enough for their own webs, often consuming excess. To overcome these limitations, Spiber uses synthetic genes to instruct bacteria to produce fibroin, then cultivates and spins the protein into usable fiber. The company, a spinoff from Tokyo’s Keio University, has filed 16 patents related to its technology and is partnering with car parts manufacturer Kojima Industries to build a facility capable of producing approximately 100 kilograms of Qmonos per month. Spiber aims to achieve mass production of 10 tons annually starting in 2015. This innovation represents a major step toward sustainable manufacturing, reducing dependence on petroleum-based synthetics. Spiber President Kazuhide Sekiyama told The Asahi Shimbun, 'It is a major first step toward a manufacturing process that does not depend on petroleum.' Synthetic spider silk is not new: in 2012, the Victoria and Albert Museum exhibited a yellow cape woven from silk of the Madagascar Golden Orb Spider — whose silk is more than ten times stronger than Kevlar. Other experimental approaches have included genetically modifying goats to produce silk proteins in their milk. But Spiber’s bacterial fermentation method offers greater scalability and control. Beyond clothing, spider silk’s properties — water resistance, antibacterial action, and high tensile strength — make it promising for wound dressings, artificial blood vessels, parachute cords, and optical instrument components. Even in nature, the Darwin’s Bark Spider produces the toughest biological material ever recorded, inspiring both science and naming.
translated_content: Perusahaan bioteknologi Jepang, Spiber, telah meluncurkan gaun biru elektrik yang terbuat dari Qmonos — sutra laba-laba sintetis yang direkayasa menggunakan bakteri yang dimodifikasi secara genetik. Gaun tersebut, dipajang di kompleks Roppongi Hills, Tokyo, menunjukkan potensi material ini di berbagai industri seperti mode, otomotif, dan kedokteran. Qmonos, yang berasal dari kata bahasa Jepang 'kumonosu' yang berarti 'jaring laba-laba', meniru protein struktural fibroin yang ditemukan dalam sutra laba-laba alami. Per gram, sutra laba-laba alami memiliki kekuatan tarik lima kali lebih besar daripada baja dan fleksibilitas lebih tinggi daripada nilon. Ketika digunakan dalam rompi anti peluru, ia bisa tiga kali lebih kuat daripada Kevlar, tergantung pada spesies laba-laba. Laba-laba, bagaimanapun, tidak dapat dibudidayakan seperti ulat sutra. Mereka bersifat teritorial, cenderung kanibal, dan hanya menghasilkan sedikit sekali sutra — cukup untuk jaring mereka sendiri, sering kali mengonsumsi kelebihannya. Untuk mengatasi keterbatasan ini, Spiber menggunakan gen sintetis untuk memerintahkan bakteri memproduksi fibroin, lalu membudidayakan dan memintal protein menjadi serat yang dapat digunakan. Perusahaan ini, hasil spin-off dari Universitas Keio di Tokyo, telah mengajukan 16 paten terkait teknologinya dan bekerja sama dengan produsen suku cadang mobil Kojima Industries untuk membangun fasilitas yang mampu memproduksi sekitar 100 kilogram Qmonos per bulan. Spiber bertujuan mencapai produksi massal 10 ton per tahun mulai tahun 2015. Inovasi ini merupakan langkah besar menuju manufaktur berkelanjutan, mengurangi ketergantungan pada bahan sintetis berbasis minyak bumi. Presiden Spiber, Kazuhide Sekiyama, mengatakan kepada The Asahi Shimbun, 'Ini adalah langkah pertama besar menuju proses manufaktur yang tidak bergantung pada minyak bumi.' Sutra laba-laba sintetis bukan hal baru: pada tahun 2012, Museum Victoria dan Albert memamerkan jubah kuning yang ditenun dari sutra Laba-laba Emas Madagaskar — sutranya lebih dari sepuluh kali lebih kuat daripada Kevlar. Pendekatan eksperimental lain termasuk merekayasa genetika kambing untuk memproduksi protein sutra dalam susunya. Namun metode fermentasi bakteri Spiber menawarkan skalabilitas dan kontrol yang lebih baik. Di luar pakaian, sifat-sifat sutra laba-laba — tahan air, antibakteri, dan kekuatan tarik tinggi — menjadikannya menjanjikan untuk perban luka, pembuluh darah buatan, tali parasut, dan komponen instrumen optik. Bahkan di alam, Laba-laba Bark Darwin menghasilkan bahan biologis terkuat yang pernah tercatat, menginspirasi ilmu pengetahuan dan nama.

article_content: By David Martosko, U.S. Political Editor. Published: 12:08 EST, 6 January 2014. Updated: 14:12 EST, 6 January 2014. Chelsea Clinton has unparalleled access to her mother’s inner circle, as revelations emerged about Hillary Clinton’s informal 2016 presidential campaign planning. 'Chelsea talks to Hillary about her political future more than anyone else,' a longtime Clinton insider said Monday in Washington. That 'anyone else' likely includes Bill Clinton, the former president. 'Everyone else is just guessing at this point, but her daughter will have more influence than all the fundraisers and political operatives combined,' the insider added. In a profile published Sunday night, Politico noted that 'it would be hard to overstate the closeness between Hillary Clinton and her only child,' who shares her mother’s cautious, private demeanor rather than her father’s more outgoing style. Now a 33-year-old married woman, Chelsea has become a trusted confidante during a pivotal moment in her mother’s decision-making process. In October, Chelsea said, 'I am very strongly exercising my prerogative as a daughter to make sure my mom has this year to rest and reflect.' That closeness now extends into Hillary’s political calculus. 'Hillary Clinton has met with political professionals who want her to run—of course,' the strategist told MailOnline. 'But you can count those meetings on one hand.' 'She talks to her daughter several times a week—not just about the foundation or when they’ll get a grandchild. They’re discussing the family legacy, including a possible 2016 White House run.' Chelsea, now 33, serves as a prominent spokesperson for the Clinton Global Initiative, a charitable organization bearing her name alongside her parents'. As the newest generation of the Clinton legacy, she is frequently asked for insight into a potential second Clinton presidency. 'Before anything else, she is my mom,' Chelsea said in October at Fortune magazine’s 'Most Powerful Women Summit' in Washington. 'So I want her to do whatever she wants to do... I am very strongly exercising my prerogative as a daughter to make sure my mom has this year to rest and reflect.' She expressed confidence that her mother would 'make the right choice.' The decision remains underway: On Monday, a New Hampshire political reporter noted the presence of Clinton national adviser Craig Smith in the state. Hillary is also consulting with longtime aides such as Huma Abedin. New Hampshire’s first-in-the-nation primary is often seen as a bellwether for both parties’ nominations—though Hillary won it in 2008 but ultimately lost the nomination to Barack Obama. Clinton advisers plan to visit Iowa, another key early primary state, later in January. According to Politico, Democratic-aligned campaign professionals have been actively recruiting Hillary to run. In summer 2013, veteran field operatives from the Dewey Square Group presented a formal 2016 strategy to her—an effort Politico described as 'the only formal 2016-related presentation Clinton has received from anyone outside her immediate circle.' Meanwhile, independent groups are building a parallel campaign without official Clinton involvement. The national 'Ready For Hillary' initiative, backed by retired Army General Wesley Clark, launched a bumper sticker campaign urging public support: 'One of the best ways to spark these conversations about Hillary potentially running in 2016 is by showing your support right now,' Clark wrote in an email to supporters. The Clinton campaign organization—which lost the 2008 Democratic nomination to Barack Obama—has lent its donor list to 'Ready For Hillary.' Additionally, Priorities USA, a pro-Obama super PAC, is preparing to launch a full-scale campaign the moment Hillary formally declares her candidacy. That announcement is not expected until after the November 2014 midterm elections. The Clinton Foundation did not respond to requests for comment regarding Chelsea Clinton’s role.

Sementara itu, kelompok independen sedang membangun kampanye paralel tanpa izin resmi Clinton. article_content: By Martin Robinson. PUBLISHED: 08:15 EST, 29 May 2013. | UPDATED: 08:25 EST, 29 May 2013. Trial: Mark Bridger, the man accused of murdering five-year-old April Jones, arrived at Mold Crown Court today as the jury retired to begin its deliberations. Bridger, 47, a former slaughterhouse worker from Ceinws, denies charges of abduction, murder, and attempting to pervert the course of justice. He claims he accidentally struck April with his Land Rover while intoxicated and panicked, leaving him unable to recall what he did with her body. The jury — composed of nine women and three men — was instructed by the judge to take all the time they needed after a month-long trial. In her closing speech, prosecutor Elwen Evans QC stated: 'The evidence overwhelmingly compels the conclusion that the defendant is guilty of each count in this case.' Defending counsel Brendan Kelly QC urged the jury to set aside emotional reactions and base their verdict solely on the evidence. He added: 'Mark Bridger denies these offenses. He rejects the inferences drawn by the prosecution, challenges the so-called 'compelling' evidence, and maintains his innocence.' Trial judge Mr Justice Griffith Williams gave the jury legal guidance, urging a dispassionate review of the facts. April disappeared on October 1, 2012, while playing with a friend near her home on the Bryn-y-Gog estate in Machynlleth, Powys.

Bridger, 47 tahun, bekas pekerja di rumah pemotongan haiwan di Ceinws, membantah tuduhan penculikan, pembunuhan, dan usaha menghalang jalan keadilan. article_content: Manchester United were held to a shocking 0-0 draw by League Two side Cambridge United in the FA Cup fourth round on Friday night. Despite fielding stars like Angel di Maria and Radamel Falcao, United’s attack failed to find the back of the net, forcing a replay at Old Trafford. Manager Louis van Gaal was left visibly frustrated by the result. This result joins a list of infamous cup upsets in United’s history. In 1976, Second Division Southampton stunned the Red Devils with a 1-0 win in the FA Cup final, thanks to Bobby Stokes’ 82nd-minute goal. Four years later, Division Three club Bournemouth defeated United 2-0 at home, with goals from Milton Graham and Ian Thompson — a victory masterminded by then-manager Harry Redknapp. In 2005, non-league Exeter City held United to a 0-0 draw at Old Trafford, even after Sir Alex Ferguson introduced Cristiano Ronaldo as a substitute. United eventually won the replay 2-0. Then, in 2006, Championship side Southend United knocked United out of the League Cup with a stunning 30-yard free kick from Freddy Eastwood. Perhaps the most humiliating of recent shocks came in 2014, when League One side MK Dons thrashed a weakened United side 4-0 at Stadium MK. Will Grigg and Benik Afobe each scored twice, leaving Javier Hernandez and Danny Welbeck looking shell-shocked.

article_content: New York (CNN) — Competitive eater Joey 'Jaws' Chestnut reclaimed his title as the official king of the hot dog-eating world, devouring 62 hot dogs and buns in 10 minutes at the 96th annual Nathan’s Hot Dog Eating Contest in Brooklyn’s Coney Island on Monday. But his longtime rival, Takeru Kobayashi, stole the spotlight with an astonishing performance — eating 69 hot dogs and buns in an unofficial, off-site challenge on a Manhattan rooftop. Though Kobayashi surpassed Chestnut’s 2009 record of 68, Major League Eating (MLE) refused to recognize it, insisting records must be set at Coney Island. Kobayashi, banned from the official contest due to a contract dispute, watched the live event on TV as crowds chanted 'Kobi! Kobi!' behind him. Chestnut dismissed the feat, comparing it to his solo practice sessions. 'It wasn’t a competition,' he said. 'I could break a record at my house.' MLE President Richard Shea called the event 'a bit of a farce,' reinforcing the organization’s stance. Meanwhile, in the first-ever women’s division, Sonya 'The Black Widow' Thomas devoured 40 hot dogs and buns to claim victory over eight competitors, narrowly missing her personal best. Both champions earned $10,000 and custom belts: Chestnut received the iconic mustard-yellow championship belt, while Thomas became the first recipient of a pink belt, sponsored by Pepto Bismol. Kobayashi, who gained 18 pounds during his effort, said his goal was simple: 'to remind the world that I’m still good.'

article_content: CNN) — Imagine New York or California facing this: Tap water is safe only for flushing toilets — not for drinking, cooking, washing, or showering. More than a dozen people have been hospitalized due to exposure to a mysterious chemical contaminant, and residents stand in long lines for bottled water or wait for ice to melt just to stay hydrated. This has been daily life since Thursday in Charleston, West Virginia’s capital, where roughly 300,000 people lost access to safe drinking water after chemicals spilled into the Elk River. While some taps have begun flowing again and cleanup efforts are underway, the contamination — traced to a leak from a chemical storage tank upstream from the city’s water treatment plant — continues to cripple the community. One Washington Post reporter described living there as 'like camping.' A local resident put it more bluntly: 'It’s like a zombie apocalypse here.' Where is the national outrage? Our collective indifference is troubling. We seem to think: It’s fine — the water’s still usable for toilets. Or: Whatever — it’s just West Virginia. This would be the dominant story across America if a similar spill had occurred in a state with greater political influence and media visibility — say, New Jersey. There, Governor Chris Christie’s administration faces accusations of orchestrating traffic jams as political revenge — a scandal dubbed 'Bridgegate.' The public has devoured every detail: damning emails, calls for federal investigations, and high-profile fallout. Meanwhile, West Virginia matters just as much — especially to the people who rely on clean water to survive. I’m not saying Bridgegate doesn’t matter. It’s a legitimate political story. But it’s heartbreaking that disasters now seem to require branding to gain attention. 'If we called this the 4-methylcyclohexane methanol leak 'Watergate,' would the political press pay more attention?' asked Ana Marie Cox of The Guardian. The answer, as she implies, is yes. Jason Linkins noted on The Huffington Post that none of the major Sunday morning news programs gave significant coverage to the spill. 'Sunday shows to West Virginia: Drop Dead!' read his headline. They were fixated on Christie — a story with plenty of time to unfold before the 2016 presidential election. This issue runs deeper than media bias. Major outlets, including CNN, did send reporters to West Virginia. Information exists. The problem isn’t lack of coverage — it’s lack of urgency. West Virginia is so stigmatized in the national psyche that many assume environmental disasters like this are inevitable there. Yet access to clean drinking water is one of government’s most fundamental responsibilities. We should be having a national debate on how to protect our water from industrial chemicals. People in West Virginia are already leading that conversation. Angela Rosser, executive director of the West Virginia Rivers Coalition, told The New York Times: 'We need to overhaul our entire system and seriously rethink how we value our natural resources over corporate interests.' She and others ask critical questions: Why was a chemical storage tank permitted next to a drinking water source? Why hadn’t it been inspected since 1991? Ken Ward Jr. of The Charleston Gazette reported that the U.S. Chemical Safety Board had recommended, three years ago, that West Virginia establish a new program to prevent hazardous chemical accidents. The state ignored it. It must act now. Let’s join Rosser and Ward in demanding answers — because no community should ever have to live through this again.

article_content: Seattle Seahawks head coach Pete Carroll has taken full responsibility for the controversial play call in the final moments of Super Bowl XLIX, explaining that he opted not to run the ball because he believed his team had enough time to secure the win. With the ball on the one-yard line and Marshawn Lynch — one of the league’s most dominant running backs — in the backfield, Seattle chose to pass. Quarterback Russell Wilson targeted receiver Ricardo Lockette, but Patriots cornerback Malcolm Butler read the play perfectly, intercepted the pass, and sealed New England’s fourth Super Bowl victory. Carroll later clarified that the decision stemmed from concern over the Patriots’ goal-line defense. He stated that Seattle had planned to wait until third or fourth down to attempt the winning score and viewed the first-down pass as a way to 'waste' a down while keeping the defense off-balance. 'We didn’t want to run against their goal-line personnel,' Carroll said. 'We had plenty of downs and a timeout. We were playing for third or fourth down — it just didn’t work out.' Wilson echoed Carroll’s sentiment, saying, 'If it was a catch, it would be a completely different story. I thought it was going to be a touchdown.' Both coaches expressed disbelief in the immediate aftermath, sharing a silent look of shock. The call ignited fierce criticism from former players and analysts. Hall of Famer Emmitt Smith called it 'the worst play call I’ve ever seen in football.' Terrell Owens declared, 'That play call will haunt Pete for the rest of his career.' Meanwhile, Seahawks linebacker Bruce Irvin openly questioned the decision, stating, 'We have the best back in the league.' Some social media users drew parallels between Carroll’s explanation and Bill Belichick’s response during the Deflategate scandal — though no direct connection exists. Others joked that Carroll would never sleep soundly again. Despite the backlash, Wilson was consoled by Patriots quarterback and MVP Tom Brady after the game.

article_content: Future wars may be fought entirely online, according to UK Defence Secretary Philip Hammond. Speaking at a Westminster event, he stated that cyber warfare is rapidly becoming the defining battlefield of the 21st century — much like how tanks replaced horses in the 20th century. Hammond emphasized that internet-based attacks could eliminate the need for troops on the ground, driven partly by public reluctance to accept military casualties. 'I can tell you with some degree of confidence,' he said, 'that there will never again be a conflict in which cyber does not play a major role.' He clarified that while cyber operations won't resemble video games like Call of Duty, malicious software such as viruses will become the weapon of choice for nations seeking to strike without risking soldiers’ lives. Hammond described the internet as the 'new frontier' for military power, noting that modern societies and armed forces are deeply vulnerable to networked IT disruptions. 'This vulnerability makes our exposure all the more significant,' he added. He stressed that military capability must now be measured against global adversaries who are continuously evolving. 'We can’t stand still because our enemies don’t stand still,' he said. Investment priorities, he noted, must focus on cyber, intelligence, surveillance, target acquisition, and reconnaissance. Hammond also referenced the 2010 Stuxnet attack — widely believed to be a joint Israeli-US operation — which targeted Iran’s Natanz uranium enrichment facility. The virus secretly increased centrifuge speeds until they failed, while disabling monitoring systems to deceive operators. Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad later confirmed the attack had delayed Iran’s nuclear program. 'We must honor our military traditions,' Hammond concluded, 'but we must also embrace the future.'

Hammond menekankan bahwa serangan berbasis internet bisa menghilangkan kebutuhan akan pasukan darat, sebagian karena ketidaksediaan publik menerima korban militer. 'Saya bisa katakan dengan tingkat kepercayaan tertentu,' ujarnya, 'bahwa tidak akan pernah ada lagi konflik di mana siber tidak memainkan peran besar.' Ia menjelaskan bahwa operasi siber tidak akan mirip game video seperti Call of Duty, tetapi perangkat lunak jahat seperti virus akan menjadi senjata pilihan bagi negara-negara yang ingin menyerang tanpa merisikokan nyawa prajuritnya. Hammond menggambarkan internet sebagai 'perbatasan baru' untuk kekuatan militer, mencatat bahwa masyarakat modern dan angkatan bersenjata sangat rentan terhadap gangguan sistem TI berjejaring. 'Kerentanan ini membuat eksposur kita semakin signifikan,' tambahnya. Ia menekankan bahwa kemampuan militer sekarang harus diukur melawan lawan global yang terus berkembang. 'Kita tidak bisa diam karena musuh kita tidak diam,' katanya. Prioritas investasi, menurutnya, harus fokus pada siber, intelijen, pengawasan, akuisisi target, dan pengintaian. Hammond juga merujuk pada serangan Stuxnet tahun 2010 — yang secara luas diyakini sebagai operasi bersama Israel-AS — yang menargetkan fasilitas pemerkayaan uranium Natanz di Iran. Virus itu secara diam-diam meningkatkan kecepatan sentrifugasi hingga rusak, sambil menonaktifkan sistem pemantauan untuk menipu operator. Presiden Iran Mahmoud Ahmadinejad kemudian mengakui serangan itu telah menunda program nuklir Iran. 'Kita harus menghormati tradisi militer kita,' simpul Hammond, 'tetapi kita juga harus merangkul masa depan.'

article_content: In the Omani industrial city of Sohar, weekend protests demanding better employment opportunities turned violent, leaving around ten people injured and at least two protesters dead, according to Oman TV editor Asma Rshid. She stated that police opened fire after demonstrators set fire to vehicles and stores. However, another source suggested rubber bullets were used instead. Several officers were also reportedly hurt, though exact numbers remain unverified. The unrest began Saturday as a largely peaceful gathering of roughly 1,000 people, but splinter groups later targeted a supermarket, a police station, and the Walli House—the official residence of the sultan’s representative in Sohar. Zamzam al Rashdi, head of the state-run Oman News Agency, confirmed the escalation. CNN’s Caroline Faraj and Victoria Brown contributed reporting from the scene.

Dheweke nyebut polisi mbukak tembakan sawise para demonstran mbakar kendaraan lan toko. Nanging, sumber liyane mawa sugesti peluru karet sing digunakaké. Sawetara petugas uga dilaporaké luka, nanging jumlah pastine ora dikonfirmasi. Kekacauan mulai Sabtu minangka kumpulan sekitar 1.000 wong sing padha damai, nanging kelompok cilik malah nyerang supermarket, stasiun polisi, lan Gedhong Walli—residensi resmi wakil sultan ing Sohar. article_content: Known as 'The Lizard' and compared to a swan—calm on the surface, fiercely active beneath—Tony Bloom is the quietly powerful owner of Brighton & Hove Albion. As Arsenal prepare to face the Seagulls in the FA Cup fourth round, Bloom’s influence looms large over the club he loves. His nickname, 'The Lizard,' originated from a poker-playing friend who joked Bloom had alligator blood at the table. His career winnings exceed £2 million, but his true legacy lies far beyond the cards. Since taking over Brighton in 2009, Bloom has invested approximately £200 million into the club, transforming it from a struggling lower-league side into one of England’s best-run football organizations. A mathematics graduate from Manchester University, Bloom first made his fortune as a professional gambler and later founded Premierbet in 2002, selling it for a £1 million profit three years later. Today, he is a property developer and director of 12 companies—but poker remains central to his philosophy. 'It teaches you to read people, assess risk, and make tough calls under pressure,' he once said. These skills, he believes, are essential to running a football club. His most significant contribution came in 2009, when he stepped in with £93 million to fund the construction of the Amex Stadium after public grants failed to materialize. Without him, Brighton might still be playing in a dilapidated ground. He also financed the club’s £32 million state-of-the-art training complex, which received the highest-ever rating from the Premier League’s independent auditor. Though wealthy enough to travel in luxury, Bloom commutes to away matches by train and often speaks with fans. Yet behind his quiet demeanor lies a steely resolve. Former chairman Dick Knight recounted how Bloom abruptly took control, rejecting any mentorship: 'I don't need your advice.' Sources suggest Knight’s version was diplomatic—the real exchange was far sharper. Bloom’s family ties run deep: his grandfather, Harry, was vice-chairman during Brighton’s 1979 promotion to the First Division and died of a heart attack on the team bus; his uncle, Ray, remains a club director. Bloom grew up attending games, likely from the directors’ box, but never as a typical terrace fan. Even as Brighton struggles this season, their infrastructure is elite. They’ve narrowly missed promotion via the playoffs in two consecutive years. With a packed Amex Stadium set to host Arsenal, Bloom’s vision is clear: sustainable success, not spectacle. To fans, he isn’t just a benefactor—he’s the quiet force who turned their dream into reality.

Sakwise Arsenal bakal nemu Seagulls ing babak papat FA Cup, pangaruh Bloom nyata ing klub sing dikasihi e. Julukan 'The Lizard' tekan saka teman sing main poker sing njaluk Bloom duwe darah buaya ing meja. Kemenangan karir e luwih saka £2 juta, tapi warisan sejati e luwih saka kartu. Sakwise munggah ing Brighton ing 2009, Bloom wis nginvestasi kira-kira £200 juta ing klub, ngowahi e saka tim sing kesulitan nang level bawah dadi salah sawijining organisasi sepak bola paling apik ing Inggris. Lulusan matematika saka Universitas Manchester, Bloom pertama kali nggawa dhuwit minangka penjudi profesional lan banjur nyetel Premierbet ing 2002, dijual karo untung £1 juta telung taun setelah. Saiki, e minangka pengembang properti lan direktur saka 12 perusahaan—nanging poker tetep dadi inti filosofi e. 'E ngajari kowe kanggo maca wong, nggawe risiko, lan ngambil keputusan sulit ing tekanan,' kaya sing diucapake e. Keterampilan iki, sing dianggep e penting kanggo ngatur klub sepak bola. Kontribusi paling penting e yaiku ing 2009, nalika e munggah karo £93 juta kanggo ngedhukung pembangunan Stadion Amex sawise hibah publik ora teka. Tanpa e, Brighton bisa uga tetep main ing stadion sing rusak. E uga ndhana kompleks latihan £32 juta sing canggih, sing menerima rating paling dhuwur sing pernah ditekani saka auditor independen Premier League. Sadurunge cukup saged kanggo bepergian karo mewah, Bloom njaluk kereta menyang pertandingan tandang lan sering ngobrol karo para suporter. Nanging ing mbalik sikap tenange ana tekad sing tegas. Mantan ketua Dick Knight ngelingake carane Bloom ngambil kendali kanthi tiba-tiba, nolak pangajaran apa wae: 'Aku ora butuh nasihatmu.' Sumber nglalekake versi Knight iki katon sopan—percakapan asline luwih tegas. Ikatan keluarga Bloom erat: kakek e, Harry, minangka wakil ketua nalika Brighton dipromosi menyang First Division ing 1979 lan meninggal akibat serangan jantung ing bis tim; pamandhe e, Ray, tetep minangka direktur klub. Bloom tumbuh karo nonton pertandingan, kemungkinan saka kotak direktur, nanging ora kaya suporter biasa. Meskipun Brighton kesulitan ing musim iki, infrastruktur e elit. E njaluk dekat kanggo promosi lewat playoff ing loro taun pungkasan. Karo Stadion Amex sing penuh bakal ngedol Arsenal, visi Bloom jelas: kesuksesan berkelanjutan, ora spektakel. Kanggo para suporter, e ora cuma donatur—e kuwat tenang sing ngowahi mimpi e.

article_content: More than two years after being abducted in Lahore, Pakistan, 72-year-old American development consultant Warren Weinstein has appeared in a new video, making a heartfelt plea to President Obama for his release. This is the first confirmed sighting of him since late 2012, raising concerns about his deteriorating health and prolonged isolation. Weinstein, who served as country director for J.E. Austin Associates—a U.S.-based firm supporting public and private sector development in Pakistan—was taken captive in August 2011. In the 13-minute recording, he speaks calmly but emotionally, describing the psychological toll of his captivity and urging Obama, as a father and fellow human being, to intervene. 'I came to Pakistan to support my country’s mission,' Weinstein says, 'at a time when few Americans dared to come. Now, when I need help most, I feel utterly forgotten.' He emphasizes that his age and declining health mean time is running out. Accompanied by a letter dated October 3, 2013, the video was sent anonymously to journalists and carries the branding of As-Sahab, al-Qaeda’s official media arm. While its origin aligns with known terrorist communications, independent verification of its authenticity remains impossible. Al-Qaeda has demanded that the U.S. cease all drone strikes in Afghanistan, Pakistan, Somalia, and Yemen, and free all imprisoned members of their network and the Taliban in exchange for Weinstein’s freedom. The White House has repeatedly condemned the kidnapping and called for his immediate release—but has steadfastly refused to engage in negotiations with terrorists, citing policy and security principles. In previous videos from 2012, Weinstein appealed to Israeli leaders and the Jewish community. This latest message marks a shift in focus toward the U.S. president, underscoring his desperation to reconnect with his family. Photographs show him wearing a gray jacket and black knit cap, his face obscured by a growing beard, a stark contrast to his earlier appearances.

Iki dadi panglihatan pertama sawise akhir 2012, sing nglahirke kekhawatiran ngenani kesehatané sing mlayang lan isolasi sing dawa. Weinstein, sing ndhudhut jabatan direktur negara kanggo J.E. Ing rekaman 13 menit iku, diajak ngomong tenang nanging emosional, njelaske beban psikologis saka penahanane lan ngajak Obama, minangka bapak lan sesama manungsa, kanggo ngintervensi. 'Aku lunga menyang Pakistan kanggo ngayomi misi negaraku,' ujar Weinstein, 'ing wektu sawetara wong Amérika ora berani lunga. Saiki, nalika aku butuh bantuan paling gedhe, aku rasane diluputake.' article_content: By Helen Pow. PUBLISHED: 21:49 EST, 16 October 2012 | UPDATED: 21:54 EST, 16 October 2012. A homeless man described as 'looking like Jesus' saved the life of a newborn baby delivered prematurely at a truck stop in Oklahoma City. Heavily pregnant Keaton Morris went into labor four weeks early while driving home with her fiancé. She gave birth to her daughter, Tatum, in the passenger seat of their Honda after pulling into the Choctaw Road truck stop. When the infant was found with the umbilical cord wrapped tightly around her neck and not breathing, Gary Wilson — a homeless man standing nearby attempting to hitch a ride east — stepped in. Wilson calmly followed instructions from the 911 dispatcher over the phone: he freed the cord from the baby’s neck, tied it in a knot, and rubbed her back until she began breathing on her own. 'He was our angel that night, that's for sure,' said Keaton Morris to News9. Witness Jennifer Morris recalled hearing the mother scream, 'My baby, my baby's blue... she's not breathing.' Paramedic Sandra Lesperance confirmed Wilson performed every step correctly. 'He did everything perfectly right,' she told News9. Wilson remained calm throughout, reassuring the mother: 'Everything's OK. She's OK, she's breathing.' After the rescue, truck stop employees offered Wilson a hot meal and a place to sleep — which he accepted. But by the next day, Wilson was gone. He had been holding a sign reading 'Memphis' when the incident occurred and told people he was traveling from Montana to Jacksonville, Florida. Waneva Morris, a truck stop worker, described him as 'a very nice gentleman' who resembled the traditional image of Jesus — with long hair and a long beard. Baby Tatum weighed 4 pounds, 11 ounces at birth and is now thriving.

article_content: Starting at the end of April 2013, McDonald’s UK will serve only pork certified under the RSPCA’s Freedom Food program across all its sausage and bacon dishes. This means every pig used in these products comes from farms that go above basic legal requirements to ensure better living conditions — including well-lit, ventilated housing, clean bedding, and enough room for pigs to roam freely. The move positions McDonald’s as the second-largest purchaser of Freedom Food pork in the UK, supporting a scheme that’s been quietly expanding for years. Around 30% of British pig farmers already meet these higher welfare benchmarks, and McDonald’s hopes its influence will inspire even more to join. A survey of 2,000 UK consumers found that nearly 75% prefer buying food from farms that treat animals humanely, ranking animal welfare alongside price and product traceability as top decision-making factors. Warren Anderson, McDonald’s UK supply chain vice president, said the shift makes ethical eating more accessible and affordable for everyday customers. He added that the goal is to give farmers the confidence to invest in long-term, humane practices. David Squair, head of RSPCA Freedom Food, called the partnership a turning point — proving that high-welfare meat can thrive on fast-food menus. He urged other chains to follow suit and encouraged more farmers to adopt these standards. The UK’s Farming Minister, David Heath, publicly endorsed the announcement, highlighting its significance for the future of responsible agriculture.

Menteri Pertanian Inggris, David Heath, nyambut gawe pangumuman iki, nggawe pentingé kanggo masa depan pertanian sing tanggung jawab.

article_content: A Florida pizzeria has found a unique solution to the state’s growing wild Burmese python problem: eat them. Evan’s Neighborhood Pizza in Fort Myers offers an unusual pie called the Everglades—featuring python meat as a topping. Curious diners can also choose versions with frog legs and alligator sausage. Owners Evan and Avis Daniell conceived the idea a few years ago, as reports of Burmese pythons invading the Everglades began gaining national attention. 'I’m very adventurous when it comes to food,' said Evan Daniell, 52, in an interview with the New York Daily News. The Everglades Pie combines locally sourced ingredients from the surrounding wetlands: python, frog legs, alligator sausage, swamp cabbage (similar to hearts of palm), and tomatoes. The python, which has a strong gamey flavor, must be marinated before cooking. Frog legs, according to Daniell, taste cleaner than chicken. The alligator and spicy sausage blend completes the meat trio. 'You get different flavors in every bite,' Daniell said. He estimates that around 150 of these pies have been sold over the past two years. The novelty appeal draws mostly tourists seeking a 'when in Rome' experience. The pie costs $45 for a medium size—largely due to the python meat, which retails at $66 per pound. Despite the high price, sales have exceeded expectations. Daniell hopes to one day introduce a 'roadkill pizza' featuring raccoon, armadillo, or possum—but so far, he hasn’t found a reliable supplier. 'It’s a happy accident,' Daniell said. 'It’s about being creative.'

article_content: On Christmas Day last year, Alan Henning was sitting in a brightly lit café in southern Turkey, sharing laughter with friends before setting off on their journey. Henning, a kind-hearted taxi driver from Bolton in northern England, was part of a volunteer team traveling from Britain to Syria to deliver humanitarian aid to those affected by the civil war. Nicknamed 'Gadget' by his peers, Henning was the only non-Muslim in the convoy. He gave up Christmas, weekends, and family time to help those hardest hit by the conflict — earning deep admiration from fellow volunteers. On January 3, 2015, his life of service ended. A short video released by ISIS showed the apparent beheading of Henning. Before his death, he addressed the camera, referencing the British Parliament’s decision to join airstrikes against ISIS. At the end of the video, ISIS also showed American aid worker Peter Kassig and threatened his life. A father of two, Henning had made four trips to Syria. While most of the aid convoy remained at the Turkish border, Henning joined a smaller group willing to enter Syria. In footage taken that day, he explained his motivation: 'It's all worthwhile when you see what is needed actually gets where it needs to go,' before embracing a colleague. Henning was kidnapped by ISIS the day after the video was recorded. His colleagues recalled why he came: 'Alan was moved by the suffering of the Syrian people, especially the children,' said Abu Abdullah in a YouTube appeal to his captors. His wife, Barbara Henning, publicly begged for his life. Her plea was echoed by Muslim leaders worldwide, including Shaykh Haitham Al Haddad of the London Shariah Council, who stated, 'Whatever your grievance with American or British foreign policy, executing this man is not the answer.'

Henning, supir taksi welas asih saka Bolton, Inggris utara, kumpulan tim sukarelawan sing mburi bantuan kemanusiaan saka Britania ka Suriah kanggo wong-wong sing kena dampak perang sipil. Neng 3 Januari 2015, uripé dheweke sing pungkasané mati. Video pendek sing dirilis ISIS nuduhake pembunuhan sing katon karo pemenggalan kepala Henning. article_content: A former care home manager in Derbyshire, Beverley Jeffs, is accused of orchestrating an elaborate scheme to steal from an elderly resident after his death. According to court testimony, Jeffs, 52, forged the last will of William Mansfield—a retired Rolls-Royce engineer—who lived at the Overseal Residential Home. The altered document named her as the recipient of 40% of his £760,000 estate, while also promising gifts to staff, including a minibus and £10,000 for an employee, along with a lavish party for residents. But the real twist? Jeffs claimed to be Mansfield’s long-lost daughter. To back this up, she doctored her own medical records to list him as her father and even sent a letter to his cousin, Terry Mansfield, falsely asserting that a DNA test had confirmed their biological link—with 99% certainty. Prosecutors say handwriting experts conclusively proved the will’s signatures were fakes. Worse still, Jeffs is also accused of stealing £51,000 from another resident by forging cheques from his personal account. After Mansfield died in April 2009, his cousin grew suspicious and alerted authorities. Jeffs, who no longer works at the home, now faces eight counts of fraud and two theft charges. Alongside her daughter and two others, she also denies charges related to laundering proceeds from a vehicle transfer. The trial is ongoing.

Tapi kejutan sebenarnya? Jeffs mengklaim sebagai putri hilang Mansfield. Untuk mendukung ini, ia mengubah catatan medisnya sendiri agar menyebut Mansfield sebagai ayahnya, bahkan mengirim surat kepada sepupunya, Terry Mansfield, dengan secara palsu menyatakan bahwa tes DNA telah mengonfirmasi hubungan biologis mereka—dengan keakuratan 99%. Jeffs, yang kini tidak lagi bekerja di rumah tersebut, kini menghadapi delapan tuduhan penipuan dan dua tuduhan pencurian. Bersama putrinya dan dua orang lainnya, ia juga membantah tuduhan terkait pencucian uang dari transfer sebuah mobil. Sidang masih berlangsung.

article_content: Early Thursday, students at Florida State University huddled in the aisles of the packed Strozier Library after a gunman opened fire, injuring three students. Two of the victims were transported to Tallahassee Memorial Healthcare—one in critical condition, the other stable—while the third was treated and released at the scene. Campus police fatally shot the gunman after he fired at officers following commands to drop his handgun, authorities said. Tallahassee Police Chief Michael DeLeo stated, 'This is an isolated incident involving one person acting alone. There’s no indication of any further threat.' He added, 'Obviously, everyone wants to know why—that’s the hard question we’ll continue to investigate.' Officials did not confirm whether the gunman was a student. The five officers involved were placed on routine paid administrative leave. The shooting began shortly after midnight inside or near Strozier Library, which is open 24 hours and was reportedly filled with 300–400 students studying for final exams. Mary Coburn, FSU’s vice president of student affairs, confirmed the high volume of students present. Mayor-elect Andrew Gillum noted, 'If there’s any positive takeaway, it’s that the victim count wasn’t higher.' FSU issued emergency alerts instructing students to seek shelter away from doors and windows. Students barricaded themselves using tables and bookshelves. A cell phone video circulating online showed students listening to an announcement: 'There has been a shooting in the library. Stay where you are. We will be coming to each floor to clear and assist everyone.' Perry Kostidakis, sports editor of the campus newspaper, told CNN the campus was largely evacuated and under lockdown. 'The entire campus is empty,' he said. 'Everyone in campus buildings is locked down. Police are still surrounding the library.' Graduate student Alex Lauren described being escorted to a nearby building, where gunshots continued to echo. Armed officers stood nearby as students waited for buses to leave campus. 'It was very scary... I’m more heartbroken than anything else,' she said. 'My heart goes out to those affected.' FSU canceled all classes and exams for Thursday. University President John Thrasher said, 'The Florida State University community is extremely saddened by the shootings that took place early this morning at Strozier Library, in the very heart of campus. Our thoughts and prayers are with the families and loved ones of all those affected.' CNN contributors Rick Martin, Anjali Tsui, Ed Payne, and Tina Burnside reported on the incident.

Petugas kampus menembak mati penembak itu setelah ia menembaki petugas setelah diperintahkan untuk meletakkan senapannya, menurut otoritas setempat. Kepala Kepolisian Tallahassee Michael DeLeo menyatakan, 'Ini adalah insiden terpisah yang dilakukan oleh satu orang. Tidak ada indikasi ancaman lebih lanjut.' Dia menambahkan, 'Jelas, semua orang ingin tahu mengapa—pertanyaan sulit ini akan terus kami selidiki.' Otoritas tidak mengonfirmasi apakah penembak itu mahasiswa. Lima petugas yang terlibat ditempatkan pada cuti administratif berbayar rutin. Penembakan dimulai tak lama setelah tengah malam di dalam atau dekat Perpustakaan Strozier, yang buka 24 jam dan dilaporkan dipadati 300–400 mahasiswa yang sedang belajar untuk ujian akhir. Mary Coburn, Wakil Presiden Urusan Mahasiswa FSU, mengonfirmasi jumlah besar mahasiswa yang hadir. Wali Kota Terpilih Andrew Gillum mencatat, 'Jika ada pelajaran positif, jumlah korban tidak lebih tinggi.' FSU mengeluarkan peringatan darurat yang menginstruksikan mahasiswa untuk berlindung jauh dari pintu dan jendela. Mahasiswa memblokir diri mereka dengan meja dan rak buku. Sebuah video ponsel yang beredar menunjukkan mahasiswa mendengarkan pengumuman: 'Ada penembakan di perpustakaan. Tetap di tempat Anda. Kami akan datang ke setiap lantai untuk membersihkan dan membantu semua orang.' Perry Kostidakis, editor olahraga surat kabar kampus, memberi tahu CNN bahwa kampus sebagian besar telah dievakuasi dan dalam keadaan lockdown. 'Seluruh kampus kosong,' katanya. 'Semua orang di bangunan kampus sedang dikunci. Polisi masih mengelilingi perpustakaan.' Mahasiswa pascasarjana Alex Lauren menggambarkan bagaimana mereka diantar ke gedung terdekat, di mana tembakan terus terdengar. Petugas bersenjata berdiri di dekatnya sementara mahasiswa menunggu bus untuk meninggalkan kampus. 'Sangat menakutkan... Saya lebih hancur daripada apa pun,' katanya. 'Hati saya ikut berduka atas mereka yang terdampak.' FSU membatalkan semua kelas dan ujian pada hari Kamis. Presiden Universitas John Thrasher berkata, 'Komunitas Florida State University sangat berduka atas penembakan yang terjadi dini hari tadi di Perpustakaan Strozier, di jantung kampus. Pikiran dan doa kami menyertai keluarga dan orang-orang tercinta dari semua yang terdampak.' Kontributor CNN Rick Martin, Anjali Tsui, Ed Payne, dan Tina Burnside melaporkan insiden ini.

article_content: Brett Anderson, father of 16-year-old Hannah Anderson, has resigned from his job in Nashville to move to San Diego — the city where Hannah lived with her mother and brother before their tragic deaths. He made the decision to prioritize his daughter’s emotional stability after she was rescued from suspected kidnapper and murderer James DiMaggio, who killed her mother Christina and 8-year-old brother Ethan before fleeing into the wilderness. In an interview with People Magazine, Anderson explained, 'I’d hoped Hannah could return to Nashville with me, but I agreed it was vital not to uproot her from the people and places she still associates with safety and comfort.' He emphasized that he would not relinquish guardianship: 'She needs her father, and I need my daughter.' DiMaggio, known to Hannah as 'Uncle Jim,' was shot and killed by FBI agents on August 10 after a six-day manhunt across the western U.S., Canada, and Mexico. His home, where the murders occurred, was set on fire using a timer, giving him a 20-hour head start. Yet, in a controversial interview on CNN’s Piers Morgan Live, DiMaggio’s sister Lora vehemently defended him, asserting there is no conclusive evidence tying him to the murders. She claimed DiMaggio 'gave his life to protect' Hannah and questioned the reliability of a 16-year-old’s account. Lora recalled Hannah visiting her home three weeks prior, describing her as 'not very gracious' and wearing 'heavy eye makeup.' However, law enforcement officials confirmed they had collected physical evidence linking DiMaggio to the crime scene, including DNA and arson patterns — contradicting Lora’s claim of 'no evidence.' The San Diego Sheriff’s Office also stated they made multiple attempts to contact Lora, who did not respond until after the interview aired. Meanwhile, Hannah and her father have begun healing together. They attended a public memorial service at Guardian Angels Roman Catholic Church in Santee, California, where over 1,000 mourners gathered. Reverend Kevin Casey said the community was 'touched by this evil and can never be the same again.' Hannah, visibly emotional, placed photos of her mother and brother on an easel and wept during the service. Hannah later spoke on NBC’s Today Show, tearfully explaining that letters and text messages exchanged with DiMaggio — often cited as suspicious — were written months earlier when she was struggling with her mother and seeking advice. She described Ethan as having 'a really big heart' and her mother as 'strong-hearted and very tough.' Authorities have not disclosed a motive, nor confirmed whether DiMaggio fathered the children. DiMaggio named Hannah’s grandmother, Bernice Anderson, as the sole beneficiary of his $112,000 life insurance policy — a detail that has drawn public scrutiny.

article_content: While history celebrates the male scientists behind the atomic bomb, the tens of thousands of women who made it possible have largely been erased from the narrative. In 1942, a secretive government project—the Clinton Engineer Works—brought women from every corner of America—rich and poor, educated and self-taught, Black and white—to a remote corner of Tennessee known colloquially as Oak Ridge. Their mission? To enrich uranium, though none were told why. They operated massive electromagnetic separators at the Y-12 plant, welded pipes, monitored radiation with Geiger counters, and crunched numbers for uranium output—all jobs once considered too difficult or inappropriate for women. Many came from impoverished towns, lured by wages that lifted them out of the Depression’s grip. For some, it was their first taste of financial independence. But the cost was steep. Black women were confined to overcrowded, segregated housing known as 'hutments,' forbidden to live with their husbands or bring their children onto the compound. White women lived in dormitories but still answered to male supervisors who rarely explained the gravity of their work. Signs everywhere warned: 'What you see here, what you do here, what you hear here—when you leave here, let it stay here.' Workers were told not to ask questions. The only safe topic? 'Where are you from?' Among them was Celia Szapka, a Polish immigrant who became a secretary to top officials. Kattie Strickland, a Black mother from Alabama, sent money home while separated from her children. Jane Greer, denied entry to an engineering program, became a statistical leader in uranium tracking. Toni Peters, displaced from her family’s land, struggled to understand her boss’s Northern accent—and he struggled to understand hers. It wasn’t until August 6, 1945, after Hiroshima was destroyed, that the truth finally broke through: they had built the bomb. One woman shouted, 'It’s a bomb!' Others wept. They had worked for years without knowing they were helping end a world war—and start a new age of destruction. Denise Kiernan’s book, 'The Girls of Atomic City,' gives voice to these women—not as footnotes, but as the backbone of one of history’s most consequential secrets.

Pada tahun 1942, sebuah proyek rahasia pemerintah—Clinton Engineer Works—membawa perempuan dari seluruh penjuru Amerika—kaya dan miskin, terdidik dan tidak terdidik, kulit hitam dan putih—ke sudut terpencil Tennessee yang dikenal secara kolektif sebagai Oak Ridge. Misi mereka? Memperkaya uranium, meskipun tak seorang pun diberi tahu alasannya. Mereka mengoperasikan separator elektromagnetik besar di pabrik Y-12, mengelas pipa, memantau radiasi dengan penghitung Geiger, dan mengolah angka untuk produksi uranium—semua pekerjaan yang dahulu dianggap terlalu sulit atau tidak pantas bagi perempuan. Banyak yang datang dari kota-kota miskin, tertarik oleh gaji yang menolong mereka keluar dari jurang Depresi. Bagi sebagian, ini adalah pertama kalinya mereka merasakan kemandirian finansial. Tetapi harganya sangat mahal. Perempuan kulit hitam dikurung di perumahan terpisah yang penuh sesak, disebut 'hutments,' dilarang tinggal bersama suami atau membawa anak-anak mereka ke kompleks. Perempuan kulit putih tinggal di asrama tetapi tetap menjawab kepada supervisor laki-laki yang jarang menjelaskan betapa seriusnya pekerjaan mereka. Tanda-tanda di mana-mana memperingatkan: 'Apa yang kalian lihat di sini, apa yang kalian lakukan di sini, apa yang kalian dengar di sini—ketika kalian pergi dari sini, biarkan tetap di sini.' Para pekerja dilarang bertanya. Satu-satunya topik aman? 'Kamu dari mana?' Di antara mereka ada Celia Szapka, imigran Polandia yang menjadi sekretaris para pemimpin atas. Kattie Strickland, seorang ibu kulit hitam dari Alabama, mengirim uang ke rumah sambil terpisah dari anak-anaknya. Jane Greer, yang ditolak masuk ke program teknik, menjadi pemimpin statistik dalam pelacakan uranium. Toni Peters, yang terusir dari tanah keluarganya, kesulitan memahami aksen Utara bosnya—dan bosnya juga kesulitan memahaminya. Baru pada 6 Agustus 1945, setelah Hiroshima hancur, kebenaran akhirnya terungkap: mereka telah membuat bom itu. Seorang perempuan berteriak, 'Ini bom!' Yang lain menangis. Mereka telah bekerja bertahun-tahun tanpa tahu bahwa mereka membantu mengakhiri perang dunia—dan memulai era baru kehancuran. Buku Denise Kiernan, 'The Girls of Atomic City,' memberikan suara kepada perempuan-perempuan ini—bukan sebagai catatan kaki, tetapi sebagai tulang punggung dari salah satu rahasia paling penting dalam sejarah.

article_content: Just two weeks after being released from prison, former footballer Ched Evans proposed to Natasha Massey, his long-term partner who has steadfastly maintained his innocence since his 2012 conviction for raping a 19-year-old woman in Rhyl, Wales. Evans spent 30 months at HMP Wymott in Lancashire before his early release, having served half of a five-year sentence. In a recent video posted online, Evans apologized to Massey for his act of infidelity, describing it as the only wrongdoing he accepts — firmly denying the rape charge for which he was imprisoned. He called Massey 'the woman I love with all my heart,' crediting her unwavering support for helping him endure his time behind bars. Massey, who appeared wearing what was initially thought to be an engagement ring, clarified it was a commitment ring given to her while Evans was incarcerated. According to reports, Evans intentionally waited until after his release to propose, wanting the moment to feel more meaningful. Massey, speaking on ITV's This Morning, said she immediately stood by Evans after learning of the allegations, choosing to believe in his character over the court’s verdict. She continues to lead a public campaign to overturn his conviction, asserting he was wrongly judged. Meanwhile, Evans’s own aunt, Nina Evans, condemned his silence toward the victim, stating he 'deserved to go down' for the crime. The victim’s father has publicly pleaded for Evans to apologize, warning that ongoing media attention endangers his daughter’s safety, as she was forced into hiding after threats from the public. The Criminal Cases Review Commission is currently assessing whether to grant Evans a retrial. To date, no professional football club has re-signed him.

article_content: Former Chelsea goalkeeper Mark Schwarzer has issued a stark warning about the dangers of hosting the 2022 World Cup in Qatar during its scorching summer months. Speaking at the Leaders in Sport summit in London, he said it would likely take two or three players dying from extreme heat before FIFA takes meaningful action. Schwarzer, who has experienced match conditions above 40°C in the region—including a game in Oman where temperatures hit 43°C—called the current scheduling 'ridiculous' and questioned why there's still debate over moving the tournament to cooler months. The European Club Association has already proposed shifting the event to January or February, a move supported by many for player safety. Yet, despite prior warnings from safety committees and ongoing corruption allegations tied to Qatar’s 2010 bid selection, FIFA has resisted change. Schwarzer also condemned FIFA President Sepp Blatter’s refusal to publish the Michael Garcia report investigating bribery in the host selection process. He argued that withholding the report undermines all efforts to rebuild trust in the organization. 'If you want credibility,' he said, 'open the report. Let the world see how things are run. If there’s wrongdoing, fix it. But silence just breeds more doubt.' For Schwarzer, the situation isn't just flawed—it's a profound betrayal of the sport’s values.

Asosiasi Klub Eropa wis ngusulake ngalihke acara menyang Januari utawa Februari, langkah sing didukung sawetara kanggo keselamatan pemain. Nanging, sadurunge peringatan saka komite keselamatan lan tuduhan korupsi sing nyambung karo pemilihan Qatar dina 2010, FIFA tetep nolak perubahan. Schwarzer uga ngkritik Presiden FIFA Sepp Blatter sing nolak ngumumke laporan Michael Garcia sing nyelidiki suap nang proses pemilihan tuan rumah. Dheweke nglarang yen nggawe laporan iki rahasia mbuwang usaha kanggo ngembalike kepercayan marang organisasi. 'Yen sampeyan pengin kredibilitas,' dheweke ngomong, 'bukak laporan iki. Tonton dunya ngendi carane manajemen dijalankan. Yen ana kesalahan, perbaiki. Nanging keheningan mung mbuwang keraguan liyane.' Kanggo Schwarzer, situasi iki ora mung salah—iku sawiji pengkhianatan gedhe marang nilai-nilai sepak bola.

article_content: During a live broadcast on Sky News, political editor Adam Boulton was mid-sentence describing David Cameron’s sweeping cabinet reshuffle — one that saw at least 13 ministers removed or resigning — when a fly suddenly flew into his mouth. Caught off guard, he gagged briefly before swallowing it whole. With remarkable poise, he continued reporting, calmly assuring colleagues he was fine. 'I swallowed a fly,' he said with a smile, 'but that’s alright.' His composure drew praise, even as viewers erupted online. Later, Boulton joked on Twitter that the fly likely came from one of Whitehall’s notoriously grim public restrooms, quipping, 'At 50p a time, you’d think CityWestminster could keep them clean.' The moment quickly became a viral sensation, with fellow journalists like James Chapman calling it the most memorable moment of the entire reshuffle. Boulton, a veteran broadcaster since Sky News launched in 1989, isn’t new to controversy; his fiery 2010 clash with Tony Blair’s former spin doctor Alastair Campbell — where he snapped, 'I’m fed up with you telling me what I think' — remains legendary in UK political media circles.

Kacampakan, dia geus batuk sejeneng terus nywallow lalat éta. Nalika tetep tenang, dia ngeusi siaran sambil ngomong kana temen ka rekan-rekanna: 'Aya lalat anu kawas kahawa, tapi aya-aya wae.' Reaksi warga net jadi viral. Nanti, Boulton ngajak ngobrol di Twitter yén lalat éta mungkin datang ti WC umum Whitehall sing kotor, jeung ngeceng: 'Kadua 50p, teu bisa CityWestminster jaga kebersihan?' Moment éta jadi sorotan utama, jeung jurnalis séjén saperti James Chapman nyebut éta momen paling berkesan dina reshuffle ieu. Boulton, jurnalis veteran sejak Sky News didirikeun taun 1989, henteu anyar kana kontroversi; konflik érakna taun 2010 jeung Alastair Campbell, mantan spin doctor Tony Blair — di mana dia ngamuk, 'Aya-aya wae kau ngajelaskeun kana pikiran ku!' — masih jadi legenda di dunia media politik Inggris.
