Abdi kahiji dianggo ngirimkeun jam tangan ieu tanggal 23 Januari—langsun ka para pendukung anu percaya kana produk ieu ti dina unggulan. Apa anu ngajadikeun Pebble jadi luar biasa? Henteu gancang, tapi loba gunana. Nyambungkeun ku lancar ka iPhone jeung ponsel Android lewat Bluetooth, jam tangan ieu ngirimkan notifikasi langsung keur pesan, email, jeung telepon—bahkan nyayogikeun pangaran anu menelepon. Pamaké bisa ngunduh aplikasi pihak katilu pikeun ngalengkepan fungsina, sarta ngarobah wajahe jam pikeun cocok jeung suasana atawa pakaian. Layar e-paper-na, sarua jeung Amazon Kindle, ngajadikeun éta gampang dibaca bahkan di bawah cahaya mentari, sambil lampu latar ngajadikeun éta gampang dipikacaya dina waktos malam. Baterainya tahan leuwih ti sabulan dina hiji pangisian, diisi ulang ngagunakeun kabel USB. Dibangun kuat, éta tahan air jeung tahan pecah, ngajadikeun éta pas pikeun para pelari, wisatawan, jeung warga anu selawasna ngalalakon. Samentara raksasa teknologi sapertos Apple jeung Google kabaraya lagi ngembangkeun jam tangan pintar méreka sorangan, Pebble leuwih leutik ngajadikeun pasar—henteu ngagunakeun dana korporat, tapi ku kakuatan warga biasa anu ngarengsekeun hal anu béda. Diharga kira-kira $150, éta geus jadi favorit kalompok awal.

article_content: Amid a struggling economy, many American families are reconsidering their vacation plans — and for some, Hawaii is suddenly within reach. Karl Stetson of Seattle originally planned to skip his family’s annual trip to the islands, but when he saw airfares dip below $450 per person — down from $600 the year before — he couldn’t resist. He snagged a deal at the Hanalei Colony Resort on Kauai, getting 25% off and even a free night. 'We could’ve stayed closer to home,' he said, 'but the price made all the difference.' Stetson isn’t alone. Across the U.S., travelers are embracing Hawaii like never before — not because it’s trendy, but because it’s cheap. Flights from major cities like Los Angeles and Boston are now 30% cheaper than last year. Some luxury resorts are listing rooms for under $150 a night, and package deals from companies like Pleasant Holidays start at just $299 for flights and three nights in Oahu. But behind the bargain signs lies a deepening crisis. Hawaii’s tourism industry, which supports one in six jobs on the islands, has seen its visitor numbers fall by over 12% in January 2009 — the steepest drop since the Great Depression. Spending has fallen even further, by 13.6%. Remote islands like Lana‘i and Moloka‘i are hit hardest, with visitor counts down nearly a third. The collapse began last year, triggered by airline bankruptcies, soaring fuel prices, and cruise lines pulling out. Companies like Hawaii Forest & Trail reported losing thousands of customers overnight. Even the state’s famed natural beauty hasn’t been enough to draw crowds in a time when budgets are tight. Still, tourism agencies are fighting back. Hotels are throwing in free nights, room upgrades, and dining vouchers. For instance, Outrigger Hotels offered third-night-free deals in Waikiki at $159/night in early 2009 — a steep drop from over $250 a year earlier. Travel experts say this is the best time in decades to visit — but warn the deals won’t last. With recovery not expected until 2011, officials are racing to reshape the public’s perception: Hawaii doesn’t have to be a luxury splurge. It can be an affordable escape — if you book now.

article_content: Los Angeles (CNN) — Actor Ryan O'Neal testified in court that he is the rightful owner of an Andy Warhol portrait of Farrah Fawcett — the woman he calls the love of his life. The black-and-white print, featuring ruby-red lips and turquoise eyes, currently hangs above his bed in his Malibu home — just as it did from 1980 to 1998. Fawcett, who died of cancer in 2009, left her art collection to the University of Texas at Austin. The university now alleges that O'Neal took the portrait without permission about a week after her death. O'Neal admits removing it but insists it was always his — a gift from Warhol, given to him and Fawcett jointly in 1980. Their relationship, once a symbol of Hollywood glamour, fractured in 1997 after Fawcett discovered O'Neal with a younger woman. Though O'Neal claimed she was 'hurt and in shock,' not furious, he later asked her to store the portrait because the young woman felt uncomfortable with Fawcett’s gaze. Fawcett reportedly replied: 'I’d like you to leave it there because I want to make her uncomfortable.' After the breakup, the portrait remained with Fawcett until her death. O'Neal maintains that the Warhols were never intended for inclusion in her bequest to UT Austin. He says he suggested she donate her collection to the university — but only after excluding the portraits he considered personal gifts. The university countersued, seeking the return of the portrait to display alongside its twin, which hangs in the Blanton Museum. O'Neal, meanwhile, is fighting for legal rights to a Warhol-decorated tablecloth with painted hearts — also part of Fawcett’s estate — which he claims was meant for both of them. The most moving moment came when O'Neal read aloud a Christmas 2007 letter from Fawcett to their son, Redmond, written after her cancer diagnosis. 'You, sweet boy, are the love of my life,' she wrote. 'Life is a miraculous gift... I don’t want any regrets because I waited too long.' The courtroom fell silent. The trial continues with testimony from movers, producers, and video evidence of memorabilia, including Fawcett’s iconic red swimsuit. While a different Andy Warhol portrait — 'Silver Car Crash' — sold for $105.4 million, the value of these Fawcett portraits remains subject to legal and emotional significance.

Fawcett, sing meninggal akibat kanker ing 2009, mewariskan koleksi senine menyang Universitas Texas di Austin. Universitas nganggep O'Neal nyolong potret iki sawise kematiané, kurang lebihe seminggu. article_content: After more than six years behind bars, former Philippine senator Leila de Lima walked out of jail on bail — a move hailed by global human rights groups as long overdue. Charged with drug-related crimes she insists were invented to crush her investigations into President Rodrigo Duterte’s violent anti-drug campaign, de Lima’s detention became a global symbol of political repression. On Monday, Judge Gener Gito overturned a prior ruling and granted bail to de Lima and four others facing a final remaining drug case, following the dismissal of two earlier charges. Outside the courtroom in Muntinlupa, supporters erupted in cheers as armored police vehicles transported her away from detention. ‘I’m starting from zero,’ de Lima told AP, her voice trembling with emotion. ‘This is freedom — and it’s priceless.’ The European Union, U.S. State Department, and United Nations all welcomed the decision, calling it a step toward restoring the rule of law. De Lima immediately called her 91-year-old mother, tears streaming as she said she was coming home. In a public statement, she thanked her family, legal team, supporters, and even President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. for upholding judicial independence. ‘It hurts to be locked up when you’re innocent,’ she said, ‘but today, I choose joy over bitterness.’ After posting a ₱300,000 bond and clearing administrative hurdles, she was officially freed. Though asked if she’d pursue legal action against Duterte, she declined, saying simply, ‘God bless him — he knows what he did.’ Her ordeal began in 2009, when, as head of the Commission on Human Rights, she investigated killings linked to Duterte’s time as Davao mayor — a probe that found no public witnesses. When Duterte became president in 2016, de Lima was elected to the Senate and reopened the investigation. In response, authorities arrested her using testimony from incarcerated drug lords. Over 6,000 people died in the government’s drug war, according to official figures; rights groups believe the true number is far higher. The ICC is now examining whether these killings constitute crimes against humanity. Even while imprisoned in a high-security facility, de Lima wrote hundreds of handwritten statements criticizing the regime and advocating for human rights. Last year, she ran for re-election from jail — forced to use a life-sized cardboard cutout as her campaign symbol. She lost. She blames Duterte for smearing her reputation and launching vicious gender-based attacks she couldn’t defend against from behind bars. Her suffering deepened in October 2023, when three Islamist militants stormed her cell, tied her up, blindfolded her, and held a gun to her chest, demanding a plane and media access. One threatened to kill her before police snipers shot him dead. ‘It’s over,’ said Father Robert Reyes, a longtime ally. ‘But the work isn’t. We still need justice for what was done to her.’
translated_content: Setelah lebih dari enam tahun di balik jeruji, mantan senator Filipina Leila de Lima dibebaskan dengan jaminan — sebuah langkah yang dipuji oleh kelompok hak asasi manusia global sebagai hal yang terlambat. Dia didakwa dengan tuduhan narkoba yang menurutnya dibuat-buat untuk menghentikan penyelidikannya terhadap kampanye anti-narkoba kejam Presiden Rodrigo Duterte. Penahanannya menjadi simbol global represi politik. Pada hari Senin, Hakim Gener Gito membatalkan keputusan sebelumnya dan memberikan jaminan kepada de Lima dan empat terdakwa lainnya yang menghadapi kasus narkoba terakhir, menyusul pencabutan dua dakwaan sebelumnya. Di luar pengadilan di Muntinlupa, para pendukung bersorak sorai saat kendaraan polisi berlapis baja membawanya keluar dari penjara. ‘Saya mulai dari nol,’ kata de Lima kepada AP, suaranya gemetar penuh emosi. ‘Ini adalah kebebasan — dan sangat berharga.’ Uni Eropa, Departemen Luar Negeri AS, dan PBB semuanya menyambut keputusan ini, menyebutnya sebagai langkah menuju pemulihan supremasi hukum. De Lima langsung menelepon ibunya yang berusia 91 tahun, air mata mengalir saat dia berkata bahwa dia akan pulang. Dalam pernyataan publik, dia berterima kasih kepada keluarga, tim hukum, pendukung, dan bahkan Presiden Ferdinand Marcos Jr. karena menjunjung tinggi independensi yudisial. ‘Sakit rasanya dipenjara ketika kamu tidak bersalah,’ katanya, ‘tapi hari ini, saya memilih kebahagiaan daripada kepahitan.’ Setelah membayar jaminan ₱300.000 dan menyelesaikan prosedur administratif, dia secara resmi dibebaskan. Meski ditanya apakah dia akan mengambil tindakan hukum terhadap Duterte, dia menolak, hanya berkata, ‘Semoga Tuhan memberkati dia — dia tahu apa yang telah dia lakukan padaku.’ Penderitaannya dimulai pada 2009, ketika, sebagai kepala Komisi Hak Asasi Manusia, dia menyelidiki pembunuhan yang terkait dengan masa jabatan Duterte sebagai wali kota Davao — sebuah penyelidikan yang tidak menemukan saksi publik. Ketika Duterte menjadi presiden pada 2016, de Lima terpilih ke Senat dan membuka kembali penyelidikan itu. Sebagai respons, otoritas menangkapnya menggunakan kesaksian dari para bandar narkoba yang dipenjara. Lebih dari 6.000 orang tewas dalam perang narkoba pemerintah, menurut angka resmi; kelompok hak asasi manusia percaya angka sebenarnya jauh lebih tinggi. ICC kini sedang menyelidiki apakah pembunuhan-pembunuhan ini merupakan kejahatan terhadap kemanusiaan. Bahkan saat dipenjara di fasilitas keamanan maksimum, de Lima menulis ratusan pernyataan tulisan tangan yang mengkritik rezim dan memperjuangkan hak asasi manusia. Tahun lalu, dia mencalonkan diri lagi dari dalam penjara — terpaksa menggunakan potret karton berukuran tubuh nyata sebagai simbol kampanyenya. Dia kalah. Dia menyalahkan Duterte karena mencemarkan reputasinya dan melancarkan serangan seksis yang tidak bisa dia tanggapi dari balik jeruji. Penderitaannya memburuk pada Oktober 2023, ketika tiga militan Islamis menyerbu selnya, mengikat tangan dan kakinya, menutup matanya, dan menekankan senjata ke dadanya, menuntut pesawat dan akses media. Salah satu dari mereka mengancam akan membunuhnya sebelum petugas polisi menembaknya mati. ‘Ini sudah berakhir,’ kata Pastor Robert Reyes, sekutu lama. ‘Tapi pekerjaannya belum selesai. Kita masih butuh keadilan atas apa yang telah dilakukan padanya.’

article_content: The family of seven-year-old Luke Jenkins has expressed profound anger after a hospital investigation found that staff shortages over the Easter Bank Holiday weekend contributed to his death following heart surgery. Luke, who had been expected to make a full recovery after his third corrective procedure at Bristol Children’s Hospital, suffered a cardiac arrest on Good Friday. Despite a rapid response — the cardiac surgeon arrived within 19 minutes of being called from home — Luke’s heart stopped for 43 minutes before resuscitation efforts began. He died the next day. A 40-page Root Cause Analysis (RCA) report revealed a series of avoidable failures: junior staff did not know where resuscitation equipment was stored on Ward 32; emergency teams were unfamiliar with the unit’s protocols; and nursing staff repeatedly lowered the alarm thresholds on Luke’s monitoring equipment to silence frequent alerts — without triggering medical reviews. Compounding these issues, the hospital had long struggled with chronic understaffing. A risk assessment from October 2010 warning of unsafe nurse-to-patient ratios on the ward remained unaddressed. Since January 2012, there have been eight patient safety incidents on Ward 32, all linked to staffing problems. Luke’s parents, Stephen Jenkins and Faye Valentine, reject the report’s conclusions, citing factual inaccuracies. They deny that Luke received an X-ray the day before his death — a claim included in the report — and insist that had such a test been performed, his condition might have been detected earlier. They also say staff ignored their urgent pleas for help during Luke’s deterioration. While the RCA acknowledged that failing to listen to families is a known risk in patient safety, it stopped short of determining whether doing so in Luke’s case would have changed the outcome. The parents are demanding a full, transparent investigation and intend to continue their fight for accountability — not just for Luke, but for every child at risk in similar circumstances.

Luke, sing diharapake bakal pulih sawise operasi jantung kaping telu neng Bristol Children’s Hospital, ngalami serangan jantung dina Jumat Agung. Sadurunge respons cepet — dokter jantung sampai ing 19 menit sawise dipanggil saka omah — jantung Luke berhenti selama 43 menit sadurunge bisa diselamatke. Dheweke wafat dina sesudhene. Panggawe masalah iki, rumah sakit wis lama ngalami krisis tenaga kerja. Laporan risiko saka Oktober 2010 sing nandha masalah rasio perawat-pasien sing ora aman neng ward iki tetep ora ditindakake. Sawise Januari 2012, ana delapan insiden keselamatan pasien neng Ward 32, kabeh linked karo masalah tenaga kerja. Orang tuane Luke, Stephen Jenkins lan Faye Valentine, nolak kesimpulan laporan, nglebu kesalahan fakta. article_content: Retired Lt. Gen. Ricardo Sanchez, who once commanded U.S. forces in Iraq during the Abu Ghraib prison scandal, is urging the creation of a national truth commission to examine the Bush-era policies that enabled detainee abuse and controversial interrogation methods. In an interview with CNN’s 'Newsroom,' Sanchez said that existing accountability mechanisms have lost public trust, making a truth commission the only viable path forward. 'I’ve lived with the association of Abu Ghraib for years,' he said. 'It doesn’t bother me anymore — but I’ve never compromised my honor.' He described the Iraq War as riddled with institutional and individual failures — from flawed policies in Washington to poor oversight on the ground. While lower-ranking personnel like guards and interrogators were disciplined, senior leaders, including Sanchez himself, were cleared by federal investigations in 2005. Sanchez pointed to recently released Justice Department memos that legally sanctioned extreme tactics — such as waterboarding, prolonged sleep deprivation, nudity, and sensory deprivation — arguing these were not isolated acts but authorized practices. He cited then-Defense Secretary Donald Rumsfeld’s December 2002 approval of aggressive techniques at Guantanamo Bay, which quickly spread to Iraq and Afghanistan. A 2009 Senate Armed Forces Committee report confirmed that senior officials knowingly authorized these methods despite warnings from military psychologists and legal advisors. Sanchez blamed this breakdown on a failure of leadership: 'We were abandoned on the battlefield,' he said. Though he retired in 2006 after 30 years of service, Sanchez continues to speak out. His 2008 memoir, 'Wiser in Battle: A Soldier’s Story,' reflects his enduring belief that America must confront its past honestly — or remain trapped by it. 'Until we face the truth,' he warned, 'we’ll keep repeating the same mistakes.'

Dalam wawancara dengan CNN ‘Newsroom,’ Sanchez mengatakan bahwa mekanisme akuntabilitas yang ada telah kehilangan kepercayaan publik, sehingga komisi kebenaran adalah satu-satunya jalan yang layak. 'Saya telah hidup dengan keterkaitan saya terhadap Abu Ghraib selama bertahun-tahun,' katanya. 'Tidak lagi mengganggu saya — tetapi saya tidak pernah mengorbankan kehormatan saya.' Dia menggambarkan Perang Irak sebagai penuh dengan kegagalan institusional dan individu — mulai dari kebijakan cacat di Washington hingga pengawasan buruk di lapangan. Sementara personel tingkat rendah seperti penjaga dan interogator dihukum, para pemimpin senior, termasuk Sanchez sendiri, dibebaskan oleh investigasi federal pada tahun 2005. Sanchez menunjuk pada memo Departemen Kehakiman yang baru dirilis yang secara hukum mensahkan taktik ekstrem — seperti penyiksaan air, kurang tidur berkepanjangan, ketelanjangan, dan deprivasi sensorik — dengan berargumen bahwa ini bukan tindakan terpisah, melainkan praktik yang disetujui. Ia menyebut persetujuan Menteri Pertahanan Donald Rumsfeld pada Desember 2002 terhadap teknik agresif di Guantanamo Bay, yang dengan cepat menyebar ke Irak dan Afghanistan. Laporan Komite Angkatan Bersenjata Senat tahun 2009 mengonfirmasi bahwa pejabat senior sengaja mensahkan metode-metode ini meskipun ada peringatan dari psikolog militer dan penasihat hukum. Sanchez menyalahkan kegagalan ini pada kegagalan kepemimpinan: 'Kami ditinggalkan di medan perang,' katanya. Meskipun ia pensiun pada tahun 2006 setelah 30 tahun dinas, Sanchez terus bersuara. Memoarnya tahun 2008, 'Wiser in Battle: A Soldier’s Story,' mencerminkan keyakinannya bahwa Amerika harus menghadapi masa lalunya secara jujur — atau tetap terperangkap di dalamnya. 'Sampai kita menghadapi kebenaran,' dia memperingatkan, 'kita akan terus mengulangi kesalahan yang sama.'

article_content: Mary Barra, the newly appointed CEO of General Motors, is a quiet yet determined leader — a mother of two teenagers who regularly tests GM’s latest vehicles on the track. A lifelong employee of the automaker, she joined the company at 18, following in the footsteps of her father, Ray Makela, who spent 39 years as a die maker at GM’s Pontiac plant. Barra, 51, holds an MBA from Stanford University and has spent 33 years rising through GM’s ranks, serving as global product chief before becoming CEO. Known for her hands-on approach, she frequently visits test tracks and even sent engineers to work at local dealerships to better understand customer needs. Her leadership helped transform GM after its 2009 bankruptcy. Under her guidance, the company launched successful models like the Chevrolet Silverado, GMC Sierra, and Chevrolet Impala — all praised for quality and performance. J.D. Power and Consumer Reports consistently rated GM’s vehicles higher during her tenure. Barra also restructured GM’s engineering teams, assigning one lead engineer per vehicle model and cutting redundant roles. Her calm demeanor, strong work ethic, and collaborative style earned respect across the organization. She arrives at work by 6 a.m. and is deeply competitive about making GM the best in the industry. She met her husband, Tony, a management consultant, while studying engineering at GM-sponsored Kettering University. On January 15, 2014, she succeeded Dan Akerson as GM’s first female CEO — a milestone in a traditionally male-dominated field. Akerson, who stepped down earlier than planned due to his wife’s illness, said the board chose Barra unanimously for her deep operational knowledge, leadership record, and interpersonal skills. 'It was almost like watching your daughter graduate from college,' he told the New York Times. He emphasized she was selected for her talent, not her gender. Though GM has repaid its government bailout and shed the nickname 'Government Motors,' Barra still faces challenges: reducing costs and gaining traction in international markets like India and South America. Industry experts, including retired GM vice chairman Bob Lutz and professor Erik Gordon, praise her as the most qualified candidate — possessing unmatched 'car-guy' credentials and a rare blend of technical insight and people skills. 'She’s the one to do the breakthrough,' Gordon said.

article_content: A social worker who assisted elderly clients by day and performed a burlesque act dressed as a pensioner by night has been disciplined by her employer, Bromley Council. Amy Spilsbury-Butler, 39, used the stage names Molly Marmalade and Old Molly for performances featuring a hairnet, slippers, and an oversized coat. An online video of her act was seen by a relative of one of her clients, prompting a formal complaint. Following this, Ms. Spilsbury-Butler posted what the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC) deemed 'inappropriate' comments about the relative on Facebook. At an HCPC hearing, the panel concluded she had breached the expected standard of personal conduct for social workers, which requires high ethical behavior both inside and outside work. She was ordered to remove all videos of her Molly Marmalade performances, refrain from portraying vulnerable individuals in future acts, and obtain prior approval from her employer before performing any new routines. The panel affirmed that her professional competence as a social worker was not in question and imposed a three-year caution, which will appear on her public registration record. Despite these restrictions, Ms. Spilsbury-Butler continues to perform burlesque under the new stage name Alabama Breeze. Recent videos show her performing routines involving suggestive movements and revealing attire, including corsets and wigs, at venues such as Infinitease. On her personal website, she describes her act as including 'sensual fan dances, balloon-popping routines, and cheeky little routines performed only after midnight,' identifying herself as an accomplished actress and pin-up model. She characterizes her current performances as 'a little more dark and daring.' Bromley Council stated it would not comment further on individual cases, noting that appropriate action had already been taken. Ms. Spilsbury-Butler has previously acknowledged to the HCPC that her behavior was 'silly' and 'highly inappropriate' and expressed regret.

article_content: Adam Scott, 21, from Exmouth, Devon, was sentenced for violently assaulting his ex-girlfriend and repeatedly breaching a lifelong restraining order. During a terrifying incident, Scott punched his ex-girlfriend, pulled her hair, and dangled her over the railing of a pedestrian bridge above the A379 dual carriageway, threatening to drop her — an act that could have caused serious injury or death. Witnesses in a passing vehicle were horrified and alerted police. Within days of his arrest, Scott sent multiple letters from prison to his ex-girlfriend, violating the court-ordered no-contact directive. One letter explicitly threatened to stab her new partner 'in the face,' while others claimed enduring affection, stating she was 'still the one I miss, love and think about.' The prosecution argued these messages constituted severe harassment, while the defence claimed they reflected remorse and love. Judge Francis Gilbert QC rejected the defence's interpretation, emphasizing that Scott acted 'regardless of her wishes' and that the letters caused 'considerable harassment.' Scott has 27 convictions for 44 offences, many involving violence while intoxicated. The court imposed an eight-month suspended jail sentence, to be served over two years, along with a £100 victim surcharge. Judge Gilbert warned that any future contact with his ex-girlfriend will result in immediate imprisonment.

article_content: After spending six months without a single appearance for Manchester City, defender Matija Nastasic has agreed to a season-long loan move to Schalke 04, with the German side holding an option to buy him permanently. The 21-year-old Serbian centre-back, who once starred under former manager Roberto Mancini, says his decision to leave was purely about getting back on the pitch — not any fallout with current boss Manuel Pellegrini. 'Everything was fine between us,' Nastasic told Sky Sports News HQ. 'It was tough sitting out for half a year. Playing regularly is crucial for my development, and Schalke offered me that chance.' Nastasic’s fall from grace at the Etihad began after a series of calf and knee injuries disrupted his 2012–13 campaign. Once a key starter following his 2012 transfer from Fiorentina, he gradually slipped behind Martin Demichelis, then lost ground entirely after the arrival of Eliaquim Mangala and the emergence of Dedryck Boyata. His last game for City was the Community Shield against Arsenal in August. Schalke, who are also competing in this season’s Champions League, see Nastasic as a strategic addition and have included a purchase clause in the agreement. He’ll be working under former Chelsea manager Roberto di Matteo, whom he’s already spoken to. 'He gave me a clear picture of the club and the team,' Nastasic said. 'I’m hopeful we’ll build something good together.' Though his time at City didn’t end as planned, Nastasic remains grateful for his early success there — including being named one of their Players of the Season in 2011–12 — and insists the move is the right step for his future.

Pemain tengah Serbia berusia 21 tahun, yang pernah menjadi andalan di bawah pelatih mantan Roberto Mancini, menyatakan bahwa keputusannya pindah murni demi bisa kembali bermain — bukan karena konflik dengan manajer saat ini, Manuel Pellegrini. Bermain rutin sangat penting bagi perkembanganku, dan Schalke memberiku kesempatan itu.' Dulu ia menjadi pilihan utama setelah pindah dari Fiorentina pada 2012, tetapi perlahan tersingkir oleh Martin Demichelis, lalu semakin tertinggal setelah kedatangan Eliaquim Mangala dan munculnya Dedryck Boyata. article_content: The trial of Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, accused in the 2013 Boston Marathon bombing, is set to begin Monday in Boston after a federal appeals court declined to intervene. The 1st U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals ruled Saturday that Tsarnaev’s defense team did not meet the exceptionally high legal bar needed to delay the proceedings or move them out of Massachusetts. His lawyers had argued that the intense local trauma made a fair trial impossible in the region — but the court, in a 2-1 decision, found no sufficient grounds to alter the schedule. One dissenting judge said he hadn’t had enough time to fully review the petition filed Wednesday. Meanwhile, presiding Judge George O'Toole reiterated that postponing jury selection would disrupt over 1,200 summoned potential jurors and strain court operations. Tsarnaev, who has pleaded not guilty to 30 charges — including several carrying the death penalty — is accused of orchestrating the attack that killed three people and injured more than 260. His lead attorney, Miriam Conrad, declined to comment on the ruling.

Para pengacara membela bahwa trauma mendalam di komunitas lokal membuat sidang yang adil sulit dijalankan di wilayah itu — namun, dalam keputusan 2-1, pengadilan menyatakan tidak ada alasan yang cukup kuat untuk mengubah jadwal atau lokasi. Satu hakim menyampaikan pendapat berbeda, menyatakan ia tidak memiliki waktu memadai untuk menelaah petisi yang diajukan pada Rabu. Sementara itu, Hakim George O'Toole, yang memimpin persidangan, menekankan bahwa penundaan pemilihan juri akan mengganggu lebih dari 1.200 calon juri yang telah dipanggil serta mengganggu operasional pengadilan. Pengacara utamanya, Miriam Conrad, menolak memberikan pernyataan terkait putusan ini.

article_content: New research reveals that regular physical activity can significantly reduce the risk of developing high blood pressure. Just over half an hour of exercise daily — totaling four hours per week — may lower your risk by nearly 19%, according to scientists. A comprehensive analysis of 13 studies, involving 136,846 adults from the U.S., Europe, and East Asia, found that those who engaged in more than four hours of leisure-time physical activity per week had a substantially lower chance of developing hypertension compared to those who exercised less than an hour weekly. Those with one to three hours of weekly activity saw an 11% reduction in risk. The findings, published in the journal Hypertension and supported by the American Heart Association, underscore the powerful protective effect of recreational exercise. Researchers believe this may be due to improved weight management, better insulin sensitivity, and reduced resistance in blood vessels. In the UK, an estimated 16 million people live with high blood pressure — one-third of whom are unaware they have it. This silent condition contributes to around 350 preventable heart attacks or strokes every day. While current health advice encourages 150 minutes of moderate activity (like brisk walking or gardening) or 75 minutes of vigorous exercise (such as running or cycling) per week, three out of four Britons fall short. Importantly, the study found no clear link between physically demanding jobs — such as farming or factory work — and reduced hypertension risk. Researchers suggest future guidelines may need to distinguish between occupational exertion and intentional leisure exercise. Dr. Wei Ma of Shandong University noted, 'Preventing hypertension is critical to avoiding heart and kidney disease.' Dr. Bo Xi added that while exercise helps, people who exercise recreationally often have other healthy habits, so causation isn't proven. Still, experts agree: every bit counts. Doireann Maddock of the British Heart Foundation says even short bursts — like a 10-minute walk or getting off the bus early — can make a meaningful difference. You don’t need a gym membership to stay heart-healthy.

Wong kang ngelakoni 1–3 jam aktivitas saben minggu nemokang pengurangan risiko 11%. article_content: A powerful car bomb exploded near the Danish Embassy in Islamabad on Monday, killing at least six people and injuring up to 18, according to Pakistani authorities. The blast, heard over two miles away, ripped through the embassy’s facade, shattered windows, and left a four-foot-deep crater in the street. While police initially described the incident as a suicide attack, senior officer Ahmad Latif later said confirmation was still pending. Medical staff reported eight deaths, including a child and a foreign national — but Latif clarified only six died, all Pakistani citizens, with one Brazilian-Pakistani individual among the injured. The attack came amid lingering global tensions tied to the 2005–2006 publication of satirical cartoons of Prophet Muhammad by Denmark’s Jyllands-Posten newspaper. Those images, which many Muslims viewed as deeply offensive, sparked worldwide protests and led to the temporary closure of Denmark’s embassy in Islamabad. Although no group claimed responsibility for Monday’s bombing, past incidents in Pakistan have often been linked to extremist factions. The country had enjoyed a brief calm since March, following the formation of a new government that sought dialogue with militant groups — but violence has since resurged. Danish Foreign Minister Per Stig Moeller condemned the attack, calling it ‘completely unacceptable’ and stressing that embassies exist to foster mutual understanding, not to become targets of hatred. Pakistani officials vowed to strengthen security around all foreign missions. Debris-littered streets, overturned cars, and bloodied blankets carried by rescuers painted a grim picture of the aftermath. The embassy’s flags, torn from their poles, hung limp on the balcony — a silent symbol of the rupture.
translated_content: Sébuah bom mobil kuat meledak di dekat Kedutaan Besar Denmark di Islamabad pada Senin, menewaskan setidaknya enam orang dan melukai hingga 18 orang, menurut otoritas Pakistan. Ledakan itu, terdengar lebih dari dua mil jauhnya, menghancurkan dinding depan kedutaan, memecahkan jendela-jendela, dan meninggalkan kawah setebal empat kaki di jalan. Meskipun polisi awalnya menggambarkan insiden itu sebagai serangan bunuh diri, petugas senior Ahmad Latif kemudian mengatakan konfirmasi masih belum pasti. Petugas medis melaporkan delapan korban tewas, termasuk seorang anak dan warga asing — tetapi Latif menjelaskan hanya enam orang tewas, semuanya warga Pakistan, dengan satu warga Brasil keturunan Pakistan di antara yang terluka. Serangan ini terjadi di tengah ketegangan global yang masih berlanjut terkait penerbitan kartun satir Nabi Muhammad oleh surat kabar Denmark Jyllands-Posten pada 2005–2006. Gambar-gambar itu, yang dianggap sangat menyinggung oleh banyak umat Muslim, memicu protes di seluruh dunia dan menyebabkan penutupan sementara Kedutaan Besar Denmark di Islamabad. Meskipun tidak ada kelompok yang mengklaim tanggung jawab atas serangan Senin ini, insiden-insiden sebelumnya di Pakistan sering dikaitkan dengan faksi ekstremis. Negara ini sempat menikmati masa tenang singkat sejak Maret, menyusul terbentuknya pemerintahan baru yang berusaha melakukan dialog dengan kelompok militan — tetapi kekerasan telah kembali meningkat. article_content: HANCOCK, Massachusetts (CNN) — Imagine climbing 276 steps just to change a light bulb. For Rian Harford, a mountain operations mechanic at Jiminy Peak Mountain Resort, that’s just another day on the job. But this isn’t any ordinary bulb — it’s part of an air-traffic warning light perched 253 feet above ground on top of Zephyr, a massive wind turbine that dominates the skyline of this ski resort. Jiminy Peak, located in Hancock, Massachusetts, claims to be the first ski resort in North America to install such a turbine. The idea originated with CEO Brian Fairbank, who sought to combat soaring snowmaking costs. 'Someone suggested we harness the wind,' Fairbank recalls. 'And that’s when the wind blows hardest — in winter, when we need energy most.' But turning vision into reality took more than three years. Before ordering the turbine, the resort had to navigate complex federal regulations, assess impacts on aviation, birds, and endangered species, and plan the transport of 500 tons of equipment up a two-mile gravel road. 'Getting everything to the top was the real challenge,' Fairbank says. 'Putting it together? Just a couple days.' In fall 2007, the $4 million project was complete. Named Zephyr after the Greek god of the west wind, the turbine stands 386 feet tall — including its 123-foot blades. It generates roughly one-third of the resort’s electricity, cutting $450,000 off its annual energy bill. That’s enough power for more than 600 homes. Visitors like Louise Pinho see it as a model for sustainable innovation. 'When you realize it cuts nearly a third of their energy costs, you understand why we need more of this,' she says. 'We have to explore alternatives.' Yet Zephyr isn’t without controversy. Studies indicate wind turbines contribute to significant bat mortality — not from direct blade strikes, but from barotrauma: internal bleeding caused by sudden pressure changes as blades rotate. According to Dr. Thomas Kunz of Boston University, up to 80% of bat deaths near turbines occur this way, especially during fall migration. At Jiminy Peak, Zephyr operates year-round, but over 60% of its output occurs in winter. While some locals objected to the turbine’s visual impact, Fairbank notes few complaints remain — especially since surplus electricity flows downhill to power nearby homes and businesses. 'When we’re not using it, the whole community goes green,' he says. And Zephyr is just the latest step in a decades-long environmental journey. Since 1985, Jiminy Peak has recycled motor oil, heated lodges with renewable sources, and installed waterless urinals. 'We’ve always looked for ways to conserve,' Fairbank says. In a time when many businesses shutter, Jiminy Peak is 12% ahead of its best year ever.

article_content: Before Germany faced Argentina in a friendly at the Esprit Arena in Düsseldorf, the nation bid a heartfelt farewell to three icons of its golden generation: Miroslav Klose, Philipp Lahm, and Per Mertesacker. Each had helped lead Germany to its 2014 World Cup triumph—and then stepped away from international duty, leaving behind legacies etched in history. Klose, the man who scored more goals in World Cups than anyone else ever has, retired after netting 71 times in 137 appearances for his country. Lahm, the calm and brilliant captain who lifted the trophy in Rio, earned 113 caps and became synonymous with leadership. Mertesacker, the towering 198cm defender, brought grit and composure across 104 games. As the crowd cheered, they were presented with custom plaques: one honoring Klose’s signature somersault celebration, another calling Lahm a 'four-star captain,' and a third noting Mertesacker’s height and championship status. Even assistant coach Hansi Flick wasn’t forgotten, receiving a plaque reading 'System team player'—a nod to his quiet but vital role. With their departure, Bastian Schweinsteiger now carries the armband for a new-look German squad. Together, the trio amassed 354 international appearances and 80 goals, embodying the discipline and spirit that defined German football at its peak.

Kabehé ndhukung Jerman menang Piala Dunia 2014—kajabaé dheweke mundur saka tim nasional, nglakoni warisan sing diukir ing sejarah. article_content: Mike Ashley, owner of Newcastle United, is obligated to pay £5 million to dismiss manager Alan Pardew, as stipulated in the eight-year contract signed in September 2012. This financial penalty arises amid mounting pressure from fans and persistent poor performance, with Newcastle languishing at the bottom of the Premier League. Earlier, Ashley sparked controversy by publicly stating during a drink at The Golden Lion pub in London’s Soho district that Pardew would be sacked if Newcastle lost to Stoke City. He reportedly said: 'One more game — if we lose against Stoke City on Monday night then he’s gone. I have had enough. Dead. Finished. Over.' However, Ashley’s legal team later clarified that his remarks were made 'tongue in cheek,' insisting he was merely humorously responding to media speculation that Pardew had two games left before dismissal. The club emphasized that no formal decision had been made. Despite this clarification, many view the comments as reckless, especially given the high stakes involved. Pardew, who had endured a six-game winless run, had recently earned temporary reprieve after draws against Hull City and a cup win at Crystal Palace. Ashley, known for frugal management and unpredictable public behavior — including a televised pint chug at an Arsenal match — has faced sustained criticism since buying the club for £55 million in 2007. His reluctance to invest consistently in the squad, despite spending £25 million in the summer 2013 transfer window (including £12m for Remy Cabella and £6m for Siem de Jong), has further alienated supporters. Though Ashley claims he has 'had enough' and won't tolerate continued failure, his mixed messaging — from threats to jokes — has only deepened instability at the club. Fans continue to protest with banners calling for Pardew’s removal, while the manager struggles to restore confidence both on and off the pitch.

article_content: In his debut podcast appearance, Woody Allen opened up with surprising honesty — but not about the controversy surrounding him. Speaking with MTV News’ Josh Horowitz, the filmmaker admitted he’s never been satisfied with any of his full-length movies. Still, he found joy in scattered moments: the explosive emotional breakdown by Cate Blanchett in 'Blue Jasmine', and the playful ping-pong flirtation between Jonathan Rhys Meyers and a teenage Scarlett Johansson in 'Match Point'. Allen explained that his creative vision always outpaces reality. What looks perfect on paper — imagine Emma Stone nailing a complex line — often crumbles under real-world pressures: bad lighting, stubborn weather, or actors who simply can’t deliver a line the way he imagined. 'It’s fantasy versus the messy truth of filmmaking,' he said. He also reflected on his casting habits: for decades, he starred in his own films, then shifted focus to writing strong roles for women. While he’s worked with stars like Joaquin Phoenix and Sean Penn, he lamented never collaborating with icons like De Niro, Nicholson, or Pacino — not because he didn’t want to, but because they were always booked. He even admitted he once almost cast Jack Nicholson in 'Hannah and Her Sisters' — before considering Michael Caine. Perhaps most startling: Allen revealed that film backers have zero insight into what they’re funding. No script, no synopsis, no preview — just a bank transfer. 'It’s not a smart investment,' he bluntly admitted. 'Only one in a few ever turns a profit.' Throughout the conversation, he sidestepped all questions about Dylan Farrow’s public allegations of childhood sexual abuse — allegations he has consistently denied. The topic remained untouched, leaving listeners to wonder whether silence was strategy, sorrow, or something else entirely.

Namun, ia menemukan kegembiraan dalam momen-momen terpisah: ledakan emosional Cate Blanchett di 'Blue Jasmine', dan percakapan ringan di meja pingpong antara Jonathan Rhys Meyers dan Scarlett Johansson yang masih remaja di 'Match Point'. Allen menjelaskan bahwa visi kreatifnya selalu melampaui kenyataan. Apa yang tampak sempurna di atas kertas — bayangkan Emma Stone menyampaikan baris dialog rumit — sering runtuh karena tekanan dunia nyata: cahaya buruk, cuaca buruk, atau aktor yang tak bisa menyampaikan dialog seperti yang ia bayangkan. 'Ini adalah fantasi versus kekacauan nyata dari pembuatan film,' katanya. Ia juga merefleksikan pilihan castingnya: selama puluhan tahun, ia membintangi film-filmnya sendiri, lalu beralih fokus pada menulis peran-peran kuat untuk perempuan. article_content: AS Roma have confirmed their interest in Ashley Cole, with the 33-year-old set to travel to Rome for negotiations over a potential two-year contract. The veteran left-back became a free agent after departing Chelsea at the end of the 2013–14 Premier League season. Cole, who spent eight years at Stamford Bridge following his transfer from Arsenal, has attracted interest from several clubs including Monaco, MLS teams, Barcelona, AC Milan, and Liverpool. Rumors also suggested a possible return to Arsenal. He officially retired from international football in early 2014 after earning 107 caps for England. His final appearance came in a friendly against Denmark on March 5, following his omission from Roy Hodgson’s 2014 World Cup squad. Hodgson selected Leighton Baines of Everton as his first-choice left-back, with Southampton’s young talent Luke Shaw as backup. Since then, Cole has taken time off from professional football.

article_content: Last week, Canadian special forces engaged in their first recorded firefight with Islamic State (ISIS) fighters in Iraq — a historic moment in Western military involvement against the militant group. The soldiers, embedded with Kurdish Peshmerga units near the front lines, came under heavy mortar and machine gun fire. Brigadier General Michael Rouleau confirmed the incident, stating that Canadian troops returned fire with precision sniper shots to neutralize the threat — suffering no casualties. Rouleau emphasized that the soldiers’ primary mission remains training and advising Iraqi and Kurdish forces, not direct combat. The engagement occurred after a planning session with Iraqi leaders several kilometers behind the front lines. When the team moved forward to visually verify the battlefield layout, they were immediately targeted. While officially non-combatant, Canadian forces retain the right to defend themselves — a principle Rouleau called 'wholly consistent with the inherent right of self-defense.' He declined to disclose the exact location of the clash, citing operational security. In a notable revelation, Rouleau acknowledged for the first time that Canadian troops are actively directing coalition air strikes from the ground — a tactical role beyond previous public descriptions. Canada contributes six CF-18 fighter jets, a refueling tanker, and two surveillance aircraft to the U.S.-led coalition, alongside approximately 600 aircrew. Of its 69 special forces personnel on the ground, about 80% operate well behind the front lines, with 20% working directly alongside frontline units. The incident coincides with a chilling ISIS video threatening to execute two Japanese hostages — journalist Kenji Goto and private contractor Haruna Yukawa — unless Japan pays $200 million within 72 hours. The video features 'Jihadi John,' the British-accented militant linked to prior beheadings, who directly accuses Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe of funding 'crusader' efforts to kill Muslim civilians. Japan had pledged $200 million in non-military aid to anti-ISIS coalitions just two days earlier, heightening the stakes of the ransom demand. The video underscores the complex intersection of military action, diplomacy, and terrorist propaganda in the global fight against ISIS.
translated_content: Minggu kemarin, pasukan khusus Kanada terlibat dalam pertempuran pertama yang tercatat melawan pejuang Islamic State (ISIS) di Irak — momen bersejarah dalam keterlibatan militer Barat melawan kelompok militan tersebut. Para prajurit, yang ditempatkan bersama pasukan Peshmerga Kurdi dekat garis depan, diserang dengan tembakan mortir dan senapan mesin berat. Brigadir Jenderal Michael Rouleau mengonfirmasi insiden tersebut, menyatakan bahwa pasukan Kanada membalas dengan tembakan penembak jitu untuk menetralkan ancaman — tanpa korban jiwa. Rouleau menekankan bahwa misi utama para prajurit tetap pelatihan dan penasihat bagi pasukan Irak dan Kurdi, bukan pertempuran langsung. Pertempuran itu terjadi setelah sesi perencanaan dengan pemimpin Irak beberapa kilometer di belakang garis depan. Ketika tim maju untuk memverifikasi secara visual peta medan tempur, mereka segera diserang. Meskipun secara resmi bukan pasukan tempur, pasukan Kanada memiliki hak untuk membela diri — prinsip yang Rouleau sebut 'sepenuhnya konsisten dengan hak alami untuk membela diri.' Ia menolak mengungkap lokasi pasti pertempuran, dengan alasan keamanan operasional. Dalam pengakuan penting, Rouleau mengakui untuk pertama kalinya bahwa pasukan Kanada secara aktif mengarahkan serangan udara koalisi dari darat — peran taktis yang lebih luas daripada yang sebelumnya dijelaskan publik. Kanada memberikan enam pesawat tempur CF-18, pesawat pengisi bahan bakar, dan dua pesawat pengawasan kepada koalisi pimpinan AS, bersama sekitar 600 awak udara. Dari 69 personel pasukan khususnya di lapangan, sekitar 80% beroperasi jauh di belakang garis depan, dengan 20% bekerja langsung bersama unit garis depan. Insiden ini bertepatan dengan video mengerikan dari ISIS yang mengancam akan mengeksekusi dua sandera Jepang — jurnalis Kenji Goto dan kontraktor swasta Haruna Yukawa — kecuali Jepang membayar $200 juta dalam waktu 72 jam. article_content: More than 60 years after it was recorded, a rare, intimate audio recording of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. has surfaced — found tucked away in a dusty attic in Tennessee. The reel-to-reel tape, captured on December 21, 1960, features King in a quiet, conversational mood, speaking not as a national icon delivering a sermon, but as a thoughtful man reflecting on justice, love, and the global weight of America’s racial divide. Illusionist David Copperfield, moved by the raw humanity in King’s voice, bought the recording and donated it to the National Civil Rights Museum in Memphis — the very site where King was assassinated in 1968. The museum plans to play the audio in Room 306, the bedroom where King slept during his final days. What makes this find extraordinary isn’t just its age, but its tone: King speaks openly about nonviolence not as a strategy, but as a spiritual commitment rooted in love. 'If you’re truly nonviolent,' he says, 'you refuse to hurt your opponent because you love them.' He also shares insights from a recent trip to Africa, emphasizing how deeply Africans were watching — and hoping — for progress in the U.S., warning that America’s moral authority on the world stage depends on solving its own injustices. The tape was unearthed by Stephon Tull, who discovered it among his late father’s belongings. His father, a Tennessee native who lived under Jim Crow, had hoped to write a book on the era but never completed it after falling seriously ill. Historians, including Stanford’s Clayborne Carson, say this may be one of the few surviving recordings from King’s pivotal 1960 visit to Nigeria — a moment largely absent from official archives. Reverend Joseph Lowery, a close colleague of King, hopes the recording reignites the idea that nonviolence isn’t just a protest tactic — it’s a lifelong practice. For many who’ve listened, hearing King’s voice, calm and human, feels less like listening to history — and more like having a conversation with a friend who still has something vital to say.

Illusionist David Copperfield, kaget dening kemanunggalan mentah ing suara King, mbeli rekaman iki lan ngarepke marang National Civil Rights Museum ing Memphis — tempat di mana King dibunuh dina 1968. Museum rencanane bakal menehi rekaman iki ing Kamar 306, kamar tidur di mana King nginep ing waktune pungkasan. Sing nggawe temuan iki luar biasa ora mung umure, tapi tonenye: King ngomong nganti open babagan nonkekerasan ora minangka strategi, nanging komitmen rohani sing didasarken marang cinta. article_content: Outside White Hart Lane, Tottenham Hotspur merchandise vendors sold satirical T-shirts mocking Manchester United, portraying Louis van Gaal, Wayne Rooney, and Angel di Maria as characters from the BBC comedy 'Only Fools and Horses'. The shirts featured a twisted version of the show’s iconic line: 'This time next year, we’ll be champions'—a reference to Del Boy and Rodney Trotter’s delusional ambition. The mockery emerged ahead of United’s Capital One Cup match against Nottingham Forest, capitalizing on the club’s poor start under Van Gaal. Di Maria had been signed for a record £60 million as United’s marquee signing, while Rooney was named captain in hopes he could turn things around. Tottenham defeated Forest 3–1 to reach the last 16, while Manchester United were eliminated after a humiliating 4–0 loss to MK Dons. Ironically, the joke may have had the last laugh—just as Del Boy eventually became a millionaire, United’s situation might still improve despite early setbacks.

article_content: By Daily Mail Reporter. Published: 13:53 EST, 20 November 2013. Updated: 14:11 EST, 20 November 2013. Bloc Party's Kele Okereke and vocalist Bobbie Gordon are set to become the world’s first artists to release an original music track on 3D-printed vinyl. The release coincides with the opening of the world’s first 3D-printed record store in London in December. The musical duo met through the BACARDI Beginnings music mentoring program, which provides emerging artists with a platform to showcase their sound. Together, they created 'Down Boy'—a track heavily influenced by Bloc Party’s dance-rock style, featuring classic garage beats and ambient vocals from Bobbie Gordon. Each limited-edition vinyl will come in one of four unique sleeve designs, allowing fans to choose their favorite. Kele Okereke, who rose to fame in the UK in 2005 with Bloc Party’s Mercury Prize-nominated album 'Silent Alarm', said: 'I’m really excited to be part of this year’s project and work with Bobbie. She has a lovely quality and fresh energy in her voice that complements our up-tempo dance track perfectly. I hope this project brings her the attention she deserves.' Bobbie Gordon, who began her career providing backing vocals for artists including Adele, CeeLo Green, and the Noisettes, added: 'I’m proud to have delivered the lead vocals on this track—and to see my name on it. Releasing it on 3D-printed vinyl? That’s just brilliant. It’s incredibly hard to break through in this industry, so having this opportunity means a lot.' The custom 3D-printing technology was developed by technologist Amanda Ghassaei, who created software capable of converting digital audio files into 3D-printable record grooves. She explained: 'I designed this project to explore the limits of 3D printers. They can print a highly complex fractal in the same time it takes to print a solid cube—complexity is trivial to them. This was an experiment in writing code that leverages that capability by packing immense detail into a single 3D model.' All proceeds from the sale of the vinyl will support Nordoff Robbins, the UK’s national music charity dedicated to transforming the lives of vulnerable adults through music therapy and services. A launch party celebrating the release will take place on Thursday, December 12, at the Vinyl Factory in Soho, where Kele and Bobbie will perform 'Down Boy' live for the first time.

article_content: In the wake of Haiti’s catastrophic 2010 earthquake, a group of resilient amputees united by their passion for soccer became a powerful symbol of recovery and hope. Team Zaryen — Haiti’s first all-amputee soccer team — is embarking on its inaugural U.S. tour this week. The team will visit Washington, D.C., and New York City to host soccer clinics and hold demonstration matches as part of the 'Haitian Inspiration Tour.' Sponsored by the Knights of Columbus and Project Medishare, Team Zaryen was founded in September 2010 by Capitan Wilfred Macena, who regained mobility after receiving a prosthetic limb through the Healing Haiti’s Children Program. Inspired by his own recovery, Macena gathered other amputee patients to form the team. They chose the name 'Zaryen' — meaning 'tarantula' in Haitian Creole — because the spider persists in attacking despite its wounds. All ten members received prosthetic limbs and a full year of physical therapy through the same program. The team’s mission is to challenge societal stigma surrounding disability and to inspire others who have lost limbs. Their U.S. tour begins Monday with a soccer clinic at Walter Reed National Military Medical Center, where they will engage with wounded American service members — a gesture of gratitude for U.S. military relief efforts after the quake. The team will also practice at RFK Stadium, formerly home of D.C. United, and perform brief demonstrations during professional soccer games in both cities.

Karena kagem pengalamané dhewe, Macena ngumpulake wong-wong liyane sing amputasi kanggo mbentuk tim iki. Mereka nyebut 'Zaryen' — sing artine 'tarantula' ing bahasa Kreol Haiti — amarga laba-laba iku tetep serangan meski ana luka. Kabeh sepuluh anggota menerima prostetik lan terapi fisik siji taun kanthi program sing padha. Misi tim iki yaiku ngalahake stigma sosial ngenani disabilitas lan ngajak orang liyane sing kekeh kehilangan anggota tubuh. Tur AS mulai Senin karo klinik sepak bola ing Walter Reed National Military Medical Center, kahanan dheweke bakal ngobrol karo prajurit Amerika sing luka — minangka tanda syukur kanggo upaya bantuan militer AS pasca gempa. Tim iki uga bakal latihan ing RFK Stadium, sing dulu dadi markas D.C. United, lan njalari pertunjukan sing singkat ing pertandingan sepak bola profesional ing loro kutha iki.

article_content: Germany didn’t just win the 2014 World Cup — they broke the internet. Their 1-0 triumph over Argentina in the final sent social media into overdrive, racking up a staggering 280 million interactions on Facebook alone. At the exact moment the final whistle blew at Rio’s Maracanã Stadium, Twitter exploded with 618,725 tweets in a single minute — the highest ever recorded for any sporting event. That’s nearly 40,000 more tweets per minute than during Germany’s jaw-dropping 7-1 win over Brazil in the semis. In total, fans posted 32.1 million tweets about the final. While Mario Götze, the hero who netted the decisive goal in extra time, topped Twitter’s trending list, Lionel Messi stole the spotlight on Facebook, where he was mentioned over 4 million times. Even though Brazil lost badly to Germany in the semifinals, that match still holds the crown for most tweets ever — 35.6 million — proving the world couldn’t look away. One of the most-shared moments? German forward Lukas Podolski’s candid selfie with teammate Bastian Schweinsteiger planting a kiss on his cheek. It racked up over 90,000 retweets and 80,000 likes. Another viral hit? His photo with German Chancellor Angela Merkel — shared more than 26,000 times. Despite missing the knockout rounds due to injury, Brazil’s Neymar was the most discussed player across the entire tournament on Facebook. His account gained over 15 million new followers, and his picture with Thiago Silva became the most-liked image of the whole World Cup — beating out even Cristiano Ronaldo’s famous melon-carving pose. Adidas was the big winner off the pitch too, dominating brand conversations with 1.59 million mentions and the hashtag #allin appearing nearly a million times. Meanwhile, the official match ball, Brazuca, grew its Twitter following by almost 3 million — a 603% surge. The final drew 88 million active Facebook users globally — part of the 350 million total interactions across the entire month-long tournament. The biggest chatter came from young men aged 18–24. Countries like Brazil, Argentina, Costa Rica, and Uruguay saw over half their online populations actively discussing the match, making it a true global spectacle.

Negara-negara seperti Brasil, Argentina, Kosta Rika, dan Uruguay melihat lebih dari separuh populasi daring mereka aktif membahas pertandingan, menjadikannya spektakel global sejati.

article_content: Britain could send military reinforcements to the Gulf if the dispute with Iran escalates, the Defence Secretary has revealed. Philip Hammond said the deployment of HMS Argyll as part of an international flotilla of warships through the sensitive Strait of Hormuz on Sunday sent a 'clear signal' to Tehran. He warned that further reinforcements would be available if needed. Iran has threatened to close the Strait — through which 35% of the world's tanker-borne oil exports pass — in retaliation for Western sanctions on its oil exports. This comes after Prime Minister David Cameron stated that Britain 'will not accept' Iran’s pursuit of a nuclear weapon. The flotilla included the Nimitz-class aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln, which took over from the USS John C. Stennis in the Arabian Sea and later led the passage through the Strait. HMS Argyll, a Type 23 frigate, joined U.S. and French vessels in the transit. Hammond made these remarks during a press conference in London following annual talks between UK and Australian foreign and defence ministers. Australia’s Foreign Minister Kevin Rudd confirmed his country would enforce the same ban on Iranian crude oil imports recently adopted by the European Union. In a rare joint statement, German Chancellor Angela Merkel, French President Nicolas Sarkozy, and Prime Minister Cameron warned Tehran it would face economic isolation unless it immediately abandoned its nuclear ambitions. They emphasized: 'We have no quarrel with the Iranian people. But the Iranian leadership has failed to restore international confidence in the exclusively peaceful nature of its nuclear programme. We will not accept Iran acquiring a nuclear weapon.' The statement was backed by an unprecedented package of EU sanctions, including a ban on importing Iranian oil into Europe, restrictions on gold and precious metal exports, and targeted travel and economic sanctions against hardline regime officials. Tehran responded defiantly, with senior officials stating that closing the Strait of Hormuz would be a legitimate response to any threat to Iran’s oil exports. However, British and international analysts believe a full closure is unlikely due to the severe economic and military consequences it would trigger for Iran. The United States has warned that blocking the Strait — which carries about one-fifth of the world’s oil exports — would provoke a massive Western military response. The recent passage of six warships from the US, UK, and France underscored this deterrence posture. British Foreign Secretary William Hague asserted there was 'no plausible civilian explanation' for Iran’s uranium enrichment programme and pledged to escalate pressure until Iran returns to negotiations. He noted that EU member states collectively import nearly 600,000 barrels of Iranian oil daily — though the UK’s share is minimal. Australia’s Rudd confirmed that oil imports from Iran were now 'negligible,' calling the sanctions a necessary cost for global security. He stressed: 'This is not idle philanthropy — it is a cost worth paying.' Experts such as Professor Paul Stevens of Chatham House argue that Iran could bypass an oil embargo by exporting via pipelines to Turkey and Egypt, making a blockade ineffective. He cautioned that such pressure might instead embolden hardliners to launch terrorist attacks rather than return to talks. HMS Argyll, based in Plymouth and commissioned in 1991 after a £20 million refit in 2009–2010, is one of the Royal Navy’s most advanced frigates. It is currently operating as part of the Combined Maritime Forces — a 25-nation coalition promoting security across 2.5 million square miles of international waters, including the critical chokepoints of the Strait of Hormuz, Bab-el-Mandeb, and the Suez Canal. Its missions include counter-terrorism, counter-piracy, and strengthening regional partnerships.

Ini menyusul pernyataan Perdana Menteri David Cameron bahwa Britania 'tidak akan menerima' upaya Iran untuk mengembangkan senjata nuklir. Armada tersebut mencakup kapal induk kelas Nimitz USS Abraham Lincoln, yang menggantikan USS John C. Stennis di Laut Arab dan kemudian memimpin penerobosan melalui Selat. HMS Argyll, frigat tipe 23, bergabung dengan kapal-kapal AS dan Prancis dalam perjalanan tersebut. Hammond membuat pernyataan ini selama konferensi pers di London setelah pembicaraan tahunan antara menteri luar negeri dan pertahanan Inggris dan Australia. Menteri Luar Negeri Australia Kevin Rudd mengonfirmasi negaranya akan memberlakukan larangan yang sama terhadap impor minyak mentah Iran yang baru saja diadopsi oleh Uni Eropa. Dalam pernyataan bersama yang langka, Kanselir Jerman Angela Merkel, Presiden Prancis Nicolas Sarkozy, dan Perdana Menteri Cameron memperingatkan Teheran bahwa mereka akan menghadapi isolasi ekonomi kecuali segera meninggalkan ambisi nuklirnya. Mereka menekankan: 'Kami tidak memiliki perselisihan dengan rakyat Iran. Tetapi kepemimpinan Iran gagal memulihkan kepercayaan internasional terhadap sifat eksklusif damai dari program nuklirnya. Kami tidak akan menerima Iran mendapatkan senjata nuklir.' Pernyataan itu didukung oleh paket sanksi UE yang belum pernah terjadi sebelumnya, termasuk larangan impor minyak Iran ke Eropa, pembatasan ekspor emas dan logam mulia, serta sanksi perjalanan dan ekonomi yang ditargetkan terhadap pejabat rezim garis keras. Teheran merespons dengan menantang, dengan pejabat senior menyatakan bahwa penutupan Selat Hormuz akan menjadi respons yang sah terhadap ancaman apa pun terhadap ekspor minyak Iran. Namun, analis Inggris dan internasional percaya penutupan penuh tidak mungkin terjadi karena konsekuensi ekonomi dan militer serius yang akan memicunya bagi Iran. Amerika Serikat telah memperingatkan bahwa pemblokiran Selat — yang membawa sekitar seperlima ekspor minyak dunia — akan memicu respons militer besar-besaran dari Barat. Penerobosan enam kapal perang dari AS, Inggris, dan Prancis baru-baru ini menegaskan postur pencegahan ini. Menteri Luar Negeri Inggris William Hague menegaskan tidak ada penjelasan sipil yang masuk akal untuk program pengayaan uranium Iran dan berjanji untuk meningkatkan tekanan hingga Iran kembali ke negosiasi. Ia mencatat bahwa negara-negara anggota UE secara kolektif mengimpor hampir 600.000 barel minyak Iran per hari — meskipun pangsa Inggris sangat kecil. Rudd dari Australia mengonfirmasi bahwa impor minyak dari Iran sekarang 'nyaris nol', menyebut sanksi sebagai biaya yang diperlukan untuk keamanan global. Ia menekankan: 'Ini bukan filantropi kosong — ini adalah biaya yang patut dibayar.' Para ahli seperti Profesor Paul Stevens dari Chatham House berpendapat bahwa Iran dapat melewati embargo minyak dengan mengekspor melalui pipa ke Turki dan Mesir, sehingga blokade menjadi tidak efektif. Ia memperingatkan bahwa tekanan semacam ini justru bisa memperkuat garis keras untuk melakukan serangan teroris daripada kembali ke meja negosiasi. HMS Argyll, yang berbasis di Plymouth dan dikomandani pada 1991 setelah refit £20 juta pada 2009–2010, adalah salah satu frigat paling canggih di Angkatan Laut Kerajaan. Saat ini ia beroperasi sebagai bagian dari Combined Maritime Forces — koalisi 25 negara yang mempromosikan keamanan di 2,5 juta mil persegi perairan internasional, termasuk titik-titik penting Selat Hormuz, Bab-el-Mandeb, dan Terusan Suez. Misinya mencakup anti-terorisme, anti-pembajakan, dan memperkuat kemitraan regional.

article_content: Stars of the new BBC Three documentary 'People Like Us' have accused the producers of portraying them as 'fat, drunk, and destitute'—reinforcing damaging stereotypes of working-class communities in Harpurhey, Manchester. Once labeled Britain’s most deprived neighborhood a decade ago, Harpurhey is now the focus of a six-part series that residents say misrepresents their lives. Many locals feel they were deceived into participating, believing the documentary would highlight improvements in their community. Instead, they allege they were manipulated into appearing like caricatures from 'The Jeremy Kyle Show'—a tabloid-style program notorious for confrontational guests, profanity, and paternity tests. Over 300 residents gathered at a public meeting to express outrage. One father, Richard Searle, claimed his 21-year-old daughter Rosie was given alcohol before filming began. Another resident, Toni Callan, who did not appear in the final cut, said film crews supplied alcohol and egged on fights to create 'good TV.' Callan and others assert the entire documentary was manufactured. Campaigners are now planning a protest outside BBC Media City in Salford unless the remaining three episodes are pulled. Local Labour MP Graham Stringer intends to write to BBC Trust chairman Lord Patten demanding accountability. In response, the BBC defended the series as a 'warm and unflinching' portrayal of youth in Harpurhey, emphasizing that many participants are resilient, ambitious, and articulate—running businesses, planning careers, and sharing their stories with humor and heart. Production company Dragonfly denied all allegations of misconduct. A spokesperson confirmed that no participant was encouraged to fight, and that Toni Callan was never selected for inclusion in the final series. The team stated they followed BBC Editorial Guidelines throughout production and offered only reasonable hospitality during initial outreach. Featured resident Amber Wakefield, 18, who helps run her family’s local launderette, exemplifies the positive narratives the BBC says the documentary aims to showcase.

Luwih saka 300 wong kumpul ing pertemuan umum kanggo ngombe marah. Sawijining bapak, Richard Searle, nyawang putrining sing umure 21 taun, Rosie, kena minum alkohol sadurunge rekaman. article_content: At a high-profile Labour fundraiser in London, actor and activist Stephen Fry sparked controversy by openly challenging Operation Yewtree — the police initiative launched after the Jimmy Savile scandal to investigate historical sexual abuse allegations. Hosting the event at the Roundhouse, where tickets cost up to £15,000 per table, Fry expressed concern that less than half of those investigated under Yewtree had been convicted. He specifically pointed to Sir Keir Starmer, then Director of Public Prosecutions and now a Labour MP, who was seated in the audience, calling him the architect behind many of the operation’s prosecutions — including those against Rolf Harris and Max Clifford. Fry also highlighted cases where charges were dropped after intense media scrutiny, such as those involving comedians Freddie Starr and Jim Davidson, and actor William Roache. He emphasized the personal toll on individuals like his friend, BBC radio host Paul Gambaccini, who was arrested but never charged, yet still endured lasting reputational damage. Fry urged the crowd to uphold core democratic values — notably, the presumption of innocence — invoking the 800-year-old Magna Carta as a reminder of Britain’s legal foundations. His remarks, described by attendees as a 'rant,' left the room in stunned silence. One guest recalled Ed Miliband looking 'as if he’d swallowed a wasp.' While Fry called for harsher penalties for false accusations, Labour quickly responded: Miliband’s team stated unequivocally that the party stands firmly behind Operation Yewtree and that its focus remains on supporting survivors. Critics of the operation have long debated whether its broad scope led to overreach, while defenders argue it gave voice to victims who had long been ignored by institutions. Meanwhile, Scotland Yard’s broader investigations — including the £30 million probe into phone hacking — have also drawn scrutiny, with dozens of journalists still awaiting trial years after their arrests. Fry declined to comment further after the event.

Nggawe acara ing Roundhouse, nanging tiket e nandang dhuwit luhur saking £15.000 per meja, Fry nyebutake kekhawatiranipun yen kurang saka setengah saka wong-wong sing diselidiki ing Yewtree wis katon bersalah. Dheweke njlentrehaké Sir Keir Starmer, Direktur Publik Prosekusi ing wektu iku lan saiki anggota Partai Buruh, sing lagi duduk ing pendhapa, nganggep dheweke minangka arsitek saka proses penuntutan sing gedhe — kalebu penuntutan marang Rolf Harris lan Max Clifford. Fry uga nyebut kasus-kasus sing dihentike sawise pambanyangan media sing intens, kalebu komedian Freddie Starr lan Jim Davidson, lan aktor William Roache. Dheweke nyebut beban pribadi sing dialami dening wong-wong kaya sahabate, host radio BBC Paul Gambaccini, sing ditangkap nanging ora kena tuntutan, nanging tetep nemokake kerusakan reputasi. Fry munggahaken para tamu kanggo nglaksanaké nilai-nilai demokratis inti — kalebu prinsip tak bersalah sawise dibuktikake bersalah — ngajak Magna Carta sing umure 800 taun minangka pengingat babagan landasan hukum Britania. Pernyataanipun, sing digambarake dening para tamu minangka 'rant', mbuat ruangan iki gumantung ing kelungan. Sawijining tamu ngelingake Ed Miliband katon 'kaya wis nyithak semut.' Sadurunge Fry ngluwehi hukuman sing luwih berat kanggo penuduh palsu, Partai Buruh cepet-cepet nanggap: tim Miliband nyatake yen partai iki ngamani Operation Yewtree lan fokusipun tetep ing dukungan marang korban. Kritikus operasi iki wis lama manggala apakah cakupan sing luwih luas mbawa overreach, nanging panggiro malah nganggep yen operasi iki mbantu korban sing wis lama diabaikan déning institusi. Samentara iku, investigasi luwih luas Scotland Yard — kalebu penyelidikan £30 juta ngenani hacking telepon — uga wis ngrasakake kritik, karo puluhan jurnalis sing tetep nampa sidang taun-taun sawise tangkap. Fry ora ngomong apa-apa sawise acara.

article_content: A NATO airstrike killed at least 11 children and one woman in Shigal District, Kunar Province, near the Pakistani border, on April 6, 2013, during an operation targeting Taliban commanders. The Afghan Interior Ministry reported six insurgents killed, including two senior Taliban leaders—Ali Khan and Gul Raouf—but made no mention of civilian casualties. Wasefullah Wasefi, a spokesman for the provincial governor, confirmed that civilian homes were struck: 'Eleven children and a woman were killed when an air strike hit their houses.' Mohammad Zahir Safai, the district chief, said the victims died when their homes collapsed during the bombardment. NATO’s International Security Assistance Force (ISAF) acknowledged receiving reports of civilian casualties but stated it had no evidence of deaths, claiming its air support targeted insurgents in open areas away from structures. A Reuters journalist reported seeing the bodies of 11 children brought to Safai’s office by grieving families; the body of the woman was not publicly displayed, consistent with local customs. Tribal elder Haji Malika Jan told the BBC that fighting lasted over seven hours, beginning early Saturday. A U.S. civilian adviser attached to Afghanistan’s National Directorate of Security (NDS) was also killed in the operation. Afghan President Hamid Karzai had previously banned Afghan forces from requesting air strikes due to recurring civilian deaths, including a similar incident in the same region in February 2012. On the same day as the airstrike, a car bomb in Zabul Province killed five Americans—including three U.S. soldiers, a diplomat, and a Defense Department contractor.

Kementrian Dalem Afghanistan ngabari 6 insurgen weruak, kalebu dua pimpinan Taliban senior—Ali Khan lan Gul Raouf—nanging ora nyebutaké korban sipil. Wasefullah Wasefi, juru bicara gubernur propinsi, ngonfirmasi rumah sipil kena serangan: 'Kapindho belas anak lan sasuwene wani weruak neng waktu serangan udara nyerang rumah mereka.' Mohammad Zahir Safai, kepala distrik, nyebutaké korban weruak neng waktu rumah mereka runtuh akibat bom. Pasukan Internasional untuk Keamanan (ISAF) NATO ngakui menerima laporan korban sipil tapi nyebutaké ora ana bukti kematian sipil, nyebutaké dukungan udara dipaké neng wilayah terbuka jauh saka struktur. Jurnalis Reuters ngadegaké jenazah 11 anak sing dibawa ka kantor Safai ku keluarga lan warga sing kagung; jenazah wani ora ditampilaké publik, sesuai adat setempat. Tokoh suku Haji Malika Jan ngabari BBC bahwa pertempuran berlangsung lewih saka tujuh jam, mulai dini hari Sabtu. Seorang penasihat sipil Amerika Serikat kanggo National Directorate of Security (NDS) Afghanistan uga weruak neng operasi iki. Presiden Afghanistan Hamid Karzai gelem larang pasukan Afghanistan njaluk serangan udara amarga seringé korban sipil, kalebu insiden serupa neng wilayah iki ing Februari 2012. Dina sing same, bom mobil neng Kabupatén Zabul ngweruaké lima warga Amerika—kalebu tiga prajurit AS, seorang diplomat, lan kontraktor Departemen Pertahanan AS.

article_content: In a remarkable turn of events, all 18 individuals aboard a Super Puma helicopter that ditched in the North Sea have been safely pulled from the water. The aircraft, which was transporting personnel to an offshore oil rig roughly 120 miles east of Aberdeen, went down during its final approach — but thanks to a swift and coordinated rescue effort, no lives were lost. According to James Lyon of the RAF’s Rescue Coordination Center in Kinloss, Scotland, rescuers located emergency beacons activated by lifejackets and deployed five helicopters alongside rescue boats from nearby platforms. While the exact condition of those rescued remains unknown, officials believe there are no serious injuries. The operation, initiated after a distress call at 6:43 p.m. local time, involved collaboration between the Royal Air Force and Aberdeen Coast Guard. BP, the company operating the platform, confirmed that the 16 passengers and two crew members are accounted for: three are currently on the ETAP Platform, and the remaining 15 are aboard the Caledonian Victory rescue ship. Though light fog reduced visibility, weather conditions overall were favorable. The Super Puma, a workhorse of North Sea oil transport, is known for its reliability, and this incident appears to be an isolated event rather than a systemic issue.

Menurut James Lyon saka Pusat Koordinasi Penyelamatan RAF ing Kinloss, Skotlandia, petugas selamatake nemokake beacon darurat sing diaktifake dening jaket pelampung lan ngirimake lima helikopter sareng perahu penyelamat saka platform ngarep. Nalika kondisi pasti para korban sing diselamatkean ora diketahui, pejabat percaya ora ana luka serius. Operasi iki, kang diawali sawise panggilan darurat jam 6:43 p.m. waktu setempat, melibatke kolaborasi antar RAF lan Aberdeen Coast Guard. BP, perusahaan sing ngoperasikake rig, ngonfirmasi yen 16 penumpang lan 2 awak kapal wis ditemokake: telu ana ing ETAP Platform, lan 15 liyané ana ing perahu penyelamat Caledonian Victory. Nalika kabut tipis ngrintangi pandangan, kondisi cuaca umume apik. Super Puma, helikopter utama transportasi minyak Laut Utara, dikenal karo kehandalane, lan insiden iki tampaké minangka peristiwa isolate tinimbang masalah sistemik.
