article_content: A powerful gas explosion tore through two homes on Cloes Lane in Clacton-on-Sea, Essex, early yesterday morning, leaving nine people injured but thankfully none dead. The blast, which occurred at 8:30 a.m., was so forceful that neighbors compared it to a bomb detonating — debris was hurled up to 150 yards down the street. David Davies, 65, and his wife Hela, 56, were inside their home when it collapsed. Rescued from the rubble still wearing their pajamas, both suffered severe burns and were rushed to Broomfield Hospital — David by air ambulance after being sedated on-site. Their neighbor Gary Curtis, 27, said he heard screams coming from the wreckage and helped pull Hela from a makeshift tunnel formed by fallen beams. Elsewhere, Jack Whitby, 69, his son Ray, 47, and daughter-in-law Kim, 56, were also injured and taken to Colchester General Hospital. Their stepson Craig Stagg, 23, narrowly avoided disaster after switching his night shift as a care worker at the last minute — a decision that likely saved his life. 'It doesn't bear thinking about,' said family member John Clitheroe. Seven other locals sustained injuries ranging from burns to broken bones, with emergency teams responding swiftly: four fire engines, five ambulances, and two air ambulances arrived within minutes. Paramedics reached the scene in just over three minutes after the first 999 call was placed at 8:27 a.m. St Clare's Roman Catholic Primary School, located just 100 yards away, was evacuated as a precaution. Residents across the town reported feeling the ground shake and hearing the blast from miles away — some even thought it was an earthquake or nearby construction gone wrong. Fire officials suspect a poorly installed gas appliance or boiler as the trigger. The gas company is now inspecting the site, while investigators comb through the ruins. Despite the devastation, survivors expressed profound relief. 'I've lost everything,' said Kim Whitby, 'but I’m just glad I'm still here.'

article_content: Documents released by the Clinton Presidential Library in Little Rock, Arkansas, reveal that Hillary Clinton’s advisers in the 1990s proposed a range of media strategies to soften her image as a stern, schoolmarm-like first lady. In August 1995, her press secretary, Lisa Caputo, suggested she appear on the popular sitcom Home Improvement alongside comedian Tim Allen, participate in a wedding anniversary photo spread for People magazine, and grant a joint interview with President Bill Clinton to Barbara Walters. Caputo argued that timing such efforts around the Clintons’ anniversary would make them seem less political. She also recommended reaching young women through the Internet—an early recognition of digital outreach. She urged Clinton to 'own the women’s media' by securing features in publications like Family Circle and sharing candid photos from throughout their marriage, including images from a large anniversary celebration. Caputo acknowledged concerns that appearing on a sitcom might diminish the dignity of the First Lady role but believed the potential political and image benefits outweighed the risks. Meanwhile, adviser Mandy Grunwald advised Clinton in 1999 to appear more humorous and authentic during public appearances as she prepared to run for the U.S. Senate in New York, warning her to 'be careful to be real.' The documents also highlight Clinton’s central role in the controversial 1993–1994 healthcare reform effort known as 'Hillarycare' and her involvement in the 1996 'Travelgate' scandal, in which the entire White House Travel Office staff was dismissed and replaced with Clinton associates. A separate controversy involved Craig Livingstone, appointed head of White House personnel security despite lacking proper clearance; his office failed to conduct background checks on hundreds of employees and improperly accessed FBI files from previous administrations. Billy Dale, the fired Travel Office director, was later acquitted of embezzlement charges after testifying that funds were used for unofficial presidential travel expenses. The release of over 4,000 pages followed pressure from journalists and the conservative watchdog group Judicial Watch, which had pursued these records through multiple FOIA lawsuits. The Obama administration declined to invoke executive privilege, permitting full disclosure—raising questions about whether this decision was politically motivated. Historians have rated Clinton poorly on integrity, ranking her 21st out of 39 former first ladies in honesty, according to a Siena College poll. While critics point to these documents as evidence of ethical lapses, some Republicans, including Senator John McCain, acknowledge her likely path to the presidency if she runs in 2016.

Ing Agustus 1995, juru bicarane, Lisa Caputo, nyaranake dheweke muncul ing acara komedi televisi Home Improvement karo Tim Allen, nggawe liputan foto ulang taun perkawinan ing People magazine, lan nggawe wawancara gabungan karo Presiden Bill Clinton karo Barbara Walters. Caputo nglakoni yen njaluk iki dadi pita ulang taun bakal nggawa kesan kurang politis. Dheweke uga nyaranake kanggo nggawe hubungan karo wong-wong wadon munggah liwat Internet—pamahaman awal ngenani jalan digital. Dheweke nyuruh Hillary kanggo 'manggoni media wadon' karo nggawa liputan ing majalah kaya Family Circle lan mbagike foto-foto pribadi saka kabeh masa perkawinané, kalebu foto saka pesta besar ulang taun. Dokumen-dokumen iki uga nandhang peran sentral Hillary ing usaha reformasi kesehatan 1993–1994 sing dikenal minangka 'Hillarycare' lan keterlibatane ing skandal 'Travelgate' 1996, ing ngendi seluruh staf Kantor Perjalanan Gedung Putih diputer lan diganti karo teman-teman Clintons. Kontroversi liyane meliputi Craig Livingstone, sing ditunjuk minangka kepala keamanan personel Gedung Putih tanpa izin sing apik; kantornya gagal nglakoni pemeriksaan latar belakang ing ratusan pegawai lan ngakses file FBI saka administrasi Reagan lan Bush. Pemerintahan Obama nyerah kanggo nggunakake hak eksekutif, ngijini rilis purna—nandhang pitakonan apa iki dadi motivasi politik. Para sejarawan nganggep Clinton kurang percaya, nglakoni pangkat 21 saka 39 istri presiden ing kategori kejujuran, menurut polling Siena College. Samentara kritikus nganggep dokumen iki minangka bukti kelalaian etis, sawetara Republikan, kalebu Senator John McCain, ngakoni jalur kemungkinan dheweke dadi presiden yen dheweke njaluk.

article_content: The average American is 20 pounds heavier today than they were in the 1990s, a new report shows. According to the annual Gallup Health and Healthcare Survey, American men now report an average weight of 196 pounds, while women report 160 pounds — both nearly 20 pounds higher than figures from 20 years ago. As actual weight has increased, so too has the perceived ideal weight: for men, it is now 181 pounds (up from 177), and for women, 138 pounds (up from 137). Researchers note that Americans are not only heavier but also further from their ideal weight. Today, the average man weighs 15 pounds more than his ideal, compared to 9 pounds in 1990. The average woman weighs 22 pounds more than her ideal, up from 13 pounds. These are the highest recorded levels in Gallup’s history of tracking weight since 2001, with earlier data collected in 1990 and 1999. The survey found that 64% of men and 68% of women exceed their ideal weight. Separately, Gallup and Healthways reported that 62% of Americans were overweight or obese in the third quarter of 2023. Yet only 39% of Americans describe themselves as overweight — the majority (56%) say their weight is 'about right,' consistent with trends over the past two decades. Researchers suggest this disconnect stems from reluctance to use the term 'overweight,' even when medically warranted. Many individuals between one and 10 pounds above their ideal weight may perceive themselves as 'about right.' Results are based on telephone interviews conducted November 3–6 with a random sample of 1,012 U.S. adults aged 18 and older, living in all 50 states.

article_content: After spending 69 days trapped underground in Chile’s San Jose mine, miner Victor Antonio Segovia has returned home to the dusty town of Paipote — not as a celebrity, but as a quiet man eager to resume his life. He’s not writing a memoir. He won’t sue anyone. And despite everything, he plans to go back to mining — just not in that mine. 'Just not that one,' he says with a shrug. His family spent Friday preparing his home for his return, hanging signs and waiting under the blazing Atacama sun. All 33 rescued miners had undergone intense medical evaluations, and most were discharged by day’s end. Segovia’s family bore extra pain: two of the trapped men were his cousins. Neighbors held up handmade banners reading, 'Welcome home, Victor.' One woman whispered, 'If God gave you a second chance, hold onto it tightly.' A mysterious gift arrived: a brand-new Sony media player, left for Victor by an unknown well-wisher. His brother Pedro, standing guard in the heat, says Victor is unfazed. 'He’s just like he came off a regular shift,' Pedro says. 'We missed him, but he doesn’t talk about it yet. He will — when he’s ready.' Inside the house, symbols of survival quietly adorn the walls: two Chilean flags, gifted for their mother’s 50th wedding anniversary and lowered into the mine via the 'paloma' supply tube. On each, Victor drew a miner with a drill above the number 33, and every trapped man signed his name beneath in neat rows. One message to his mother read: 'For you with all my heart.' Blanca Segovia beams as she recalls her son’s musical talents — self-taught on guitar, accordion, and organ. A small celebration is planned. But the moment he steps from the van, chaos erupts. Reporters swarm, tripods block the driveway, and a single photographer breaks an agreed-upon protocol, triggering a shoving match. Police barely escort Victor inside as tempers flare. Later, the noise shifts to joyful chanting: 'Chi Chi Chi, Le Le Le, los mineros de Chile!' Even journalists are invited in. Victor, visibly drained, speaks softly. 'That was quite something,' he says of the collapse. 'Very ugly.' He visited Camp Hope, but won’t return. 'I miss my family more than anything,' he admits. 'And I think about God more now.' Of the 33 men, he says they became a family — with friction, yes, but also resolution. 'We were a team.' He also reveals a haunting truth: 'Down there, you were always tired. No nightmares. Here? You have them… until you remember you’re out.'

'Dan saya sekarang lebih sering memikirkan Tuhan.' Dari 33 orang, ia mengatakan mereka menjadi seperti keluarga — dengan konflik, ya, tapi juga penyelesaian. 'Kami tim.' Ia juga mengungkap kebenaran yang mengganggu: 'Di bawah sana, kamu selalu lelah. Tidak ada mimpi buruk. Di sini? Kamu punya mimpi buruk… sampai kamu ingat kamu sudah keluar.'

article_content: By James Rush. Published: 06:57 EST, 22 October 2013. Updated: 08:12 EST, 22 October 2013. A law-abiding family man was forced to quit his job after a criminal records check mistakenly labeled him a hardened criminal with a decade-long history of offenses. David Reay was wrongly identified as having convictions for burglary, theft, possession of cocaine, and drink-driving—crimes committed by someone else with a similar name. The erroneous information was provided to his new employer following a request for an Enhanced Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check. Mr. Reay, who lives in South Benwell, Newcastle, with his wife Stephanie and six-year-old son Robert, had just begun training for a new role as a child and adult welfare helpline advisor with the National Citizen Service when the error surfaced. He was told to leave his position immediately, despite clear discrepancies between his personal details and those on the fraudulent record. He has been unemployed and without income since early September while appealing the decision. 'I'd got the job and started my two weeks of training when my wife rang and said, 'Your DBS check has arrived—and there seems to be a problem with it,''' Reay said. 'I told my employers right away. They apologized but said I had to leave while they kept the position open pending my appeal.' Reay, 33, emphasized that he has never held a driver’s license—making the charge of drink-driving particularly absurd. The family had to cancel a planned birthday trip to Cadbury World for his son due to financial strain. Northumbria Police admitted that a human error led to Mr. Reay’s details being incorrectly matched with another individual in their database. They have apologized unreservedly, informed his employer of the mistake, and assured him a corrected certificate will be issued promptly. Nick Pickles of Big Brother Watch noted: 'This highlights why people must be able to review their disclosure reports before they’re sent to employers. Delays in correcting errors can cause serious harm to livelihoods.' Mr. Reay hopes to resume his training on 2 November.

article_content: For the Evans family, firearm proficiency isn’t just a hobby — it’s a way of life. At just six years old, sisters Charlisse and Raealonie Evans handle .22 rifles with the same ease most children play with dolls. Their older siblings — Verenise, 14; Roberto, 12; and Celeste, 10 — each have their own weapons and practice regularly at their local shooting range. Their father, Treves Evans, a 37-year-old truck driver from Kent, Washington, keeps 15 firearms at home and teaches his children how to use them — not out of aggression, but as preparation. 'In case someone tries to take them away,' he says. He believes armed citizens are the best defense against crime and, ultimately, government overreach. Celeste, who favors Taylor Swift, prefers her semi-automatic rifle because 'you can shoot ten at a time.' Verenise, a One Direction fan, is eager to learn how to fire a 12-gauge shotgun. 'When you pull the trigger, I like the rush you get,' she says. 'It’s just adrenaline.' Despite national tragedies like the Sandy Hook shooting, Treves insists more guns lead to less crime. 'Most shooters either surrender or turn the gun on themselves,' he argues. 'More guns, less crime.' He views the Second Amendment as both a shield against foreign invasion and a final safeguard against tyranny — aligning himself with the militia movement. His wife, Rosanna, shares these beliefs. Together, they’re preppers: ready to flee into the wilderness at a moment’s notice. Crucially, Treves emphasizes education over secrecy. 'The first thing is gun safety. Then, let them handle it. There’s no mystery — it’s not forbidden. They won’t sneak guns when I’m not home.' Treves also holds a concealed carry permit and proudly displays his family’s collection — including a pink hunting rifle for six-year-old Raealonie. 'Freedom is being eroded,' he warns. 'I won’t give an inch on the Second Amendment. It’s our right — and we’re going to exercise it.'

article_content: A routine easyJet flight from Bristol to Barcelona encountered a dramatic but non-dangerous event today when it was struck by lightning during its approach to the Spanish coast. The Airbus A319, carrying 154 passengers, was rocked by a powerful flash and deafening boom as a thunderstorm suddenly intensified — prompting widespread alarm among travelers, some of whom cried out in shock. Despite the frightening experience, the aircraft remained fully operational. Pilots safely diverted the plane to Reus Airport, about 70 kilometers from Barcelona, due to unsafe weather conditions in the destination zone. After landing without incident, passengers exited normally and were transported by coach to their final destination. Several passengers shared their experiences online, describing the moment as surreal and terrifying — one even said they believed they saw lightning encircle the fuselage. easyJet emphasized that modern commercial aircraft are engineered to absorb lightning strikes without risk to safety, and that such events, while rare and startling, are well within design specifications. A full technical inspection of the plane is scheduled for later. No injuries were reported, and all travelers are now en route to Barcelona by ground transport.

article_content: At just 14 years old, Andrea Rubio from Guadalajara, Mexico, spent a year in England improving her English — and it paid off in the most unforgettable way. During a charity polo match at Beaufort Polo Club in Gloucestershire, she spotted Princes William and Harry walking across the field. Without hesitation, she sprinted over, raised her iPhone, and politely asked, 'Could you please smile for my picture?' To her delight, both princes turned, grinned, and burst into laughter. The moment was captured on her phone — and later, in a MailOnline feature showing Andrea mid-run, beaming as she snapped the shot. Andrea, who’s studying at Westonbirt School, says this was the most thrilling event of her entire exchange year. 'I wasn’t shy at all,' she told MailOnline. 'I just ran up and asked. They smiled, laughed, and I said thank you before running off. I didn’t even know what a curtsey was!' She sent the photo to her family back home, who found it hilarious — and now she plans to print it and hang it on her bedroom wall. A longtime admirer of the young royals, Andrea called them 'quite important for England, and really smart-looking.' But when asked if she’d do the same for the Queen? 'I don’t think I’d run up to the Queen. She’s a bit too important.' In a sweet, innocent twist, she also offered royal advice: 'Kate is so pretty. If they have a girl, maybe name her Diana — it would be nice.' As she prepares to return to Mexico, Andrea carries more than fluent English — she carries a memory she’ll treasure forever.

article_content: Seventeen-year-old Sheila Eddy pleaded not guilty to first-degree murder, conspiracy, and kidnapping in connection with the 2012 killing of her former best friend, Skylar Neese. The hearing took place in Monongalia County Court in Morgantown, West Virginia, on Tuesday. Prosecutors allege that Eddy and Rachel Shoaf — now a convicted accomplice — lured the 16-year-old Neese out of her home on July 6, 2012, stabbed her to death, and concealed her body beneath branches in the woods across the Pennsylvania border. Neese’s body was discovered six months later, after Shoaf confessed to the crime. Shoaf has already pleaded guilty to second-degree murder and is awaiting sentencing; prosecutors plan to recommend a 20-year sentence, though she could face up to 40 years. The motive for the murder remains unclear. According to Neese’s father, Dave Neese, the only explanation offered was that 'they didn’t like her anymore.' He expressed anguish over the lack of deeper reasoning: 'There is no reason... I don’t care if you have the best reason in the world, but there’s no reason this should have happened.' Eddy’s case was transferred from juvenile to adult court earlier in September 2013, making her eligible for adult penalties. Judge Russell M. Clawges, Jr., set the trial date for October 22. The case shocked the tight-knit community of Star City, West Virginia, where Neese was last seen on surveillance video walking calmly to a car with no signs of struggle. Locals described both girls as seemingly ordinary teenagers. Shoaf’s family issued a public apology through their attorney, calling her actions 'unforgivable and inexcusable' and expressing deep sorrow to the Neese family. In the aftermath, Neese’s parents successfully advocated for 'Skylar’s Law,' enacted in April 2013 to improve how authorities respond to missing teenager cases in West Virginia. Dave Neese has declined to hear graphic details of his daughter’s death. 'I don’t want to hear how she screamed and cried,' he said. 'But I do want these girls to get what they deserve.'

Sidangé digawekaké ing Pengadilan Kabupatén Monongalia, Morgantown, West Virginia, dina Selasa. Penuntut umum nganggep yèn Eddy lan Rachel Shoaf — sing wis ngajukake plede guilty — nyeret Skylar Neese, umur 16 taun, keluar saka omahé ing 6 Juli 2012, ngerusaké dheweke nganggo pisau, lan mbuang jenazahé ing ngisor cabang-cabang pohon ing tepi perbatasan Pennsylvania. Jenazahé ditemokaké pitung buwana kemudian, sawise Shoaf ngaku karo kawruh. Shoaf wis ngajukake plede guilty marang pembunuhan tingkat loro lan lagi nunggu penentuan hukuman; penuntut umum rencanane menganjuraké hukuman 20 taun, nanging dheweke bisa dihukum nganti 40 taun. Kasus Eddy dialihaké saka pengadilan remaja menyang pengadilan wong dewasa ing awal September 2013, nggawa dheweke bisa dihukum minangka wong dewasa. Hakim Russell M. Clawges, Jr., njupuk tanggal sidang ing 22 Oktober. Kasus iki nyebabaké geger ing komunitas cilik Star City, West Virginia, nalika Neese dipirangake ing video pengawasan lunga tenang menyang mobil tanpa tanda-tanda perlawanan. Warga lokal nganggep kaping dua remaja iki kaya remaja biasa. Keluarga Shoaf ngajukake permintaan maaf publik lewat pengacarane, nyebut tindakané 'ora bisa dimaafaké lan ora bisa dibeneraké' lan nyatakaké kesedihan sing mendalam menyang keluarga Neese. Sawise kasus iki, orang tua Neese berhasil ngajak undang-undang 'Skylar’s Law,' sing ditandatangani ing April 2013 kanggo nyempurnaké cara otoritas nanggapi kasus remaja ilang. Dave Neese nolak ngelingi rincian kejam saka kematian putrinya. 'Aku ora pengin dengar carane dheweke mriksa lan nangis,' ujare. 'Nanging aku pengin kaping dua remaja iki nemu apa sing mereka layak.'

article_content: Matt Kuchar didn’t just win the Players Championship — he captured one of golf’s most coveted prizes: $1.7 million. But for him, the real reward wasn’t the money. It was watching his wife and two young boys sprint across the green the moment he sank the winning putt — all while celebrating Mother’s Day right beside his parents, who live just down the road in Ponte Vedra Beach. 'It felt like magic,' he said. 'Playing against the best, doing it on this day, with everyone I love right there… it doesn’t get better than this.' Kuchar isn’t the flashiest name on the tour. He doesn’t dominate headlines with explosive drives or dramatic comebacks. Instead, he’s the quiet force — steady, reliable, and always smiling. He’s made the cut in his last 17 tournaments. He tied for third at the Masters just weeks earlier. And on Sunday, he stayed calm even when paired with Kevin Na, whose slow pace drew boos from the crowd. Kuchar didn’t roll his eyes. He understood. 'He’s trying to cope,' Kuchar explained. 'Walking fast helps him manage his nerves. It’s not laziness — it’s survival.' Na, a naturalized American born in South Korea, shot a disappointing 76 in the final round and finished five shots back. He admitted the crowd’s reaction was deserved — but not fair. 'If you put any regular person out there, they’d freeze too,' he said. Tiger Woods, who’s seen it all, wasn’t buying it. 'One stroke equals one dollar,' he insisted. 'Time lost is money lost.' Even the world’s best weren’t immune to TPC Sawgrass’s brutal layout. Rory McIlroy missed the cut — again. Luke Donald, still ranked No. 1, could only manage sixth despite a brilliant closing 66. Meanwhile, names like Fowler, Curtis, Johnson, and Laird all hovered near the top — but none could overtake Kuchar. As Kuchar walked through the champions’ tunnel after his win, he paused — like so many before him — to stare at the photos of Nicklaus, Trevino, Mickelson, Woods, and others. 'I’m going to be in that gallery soon,' he thought. 'My face, up there with the legends.' For a man who’s spent years quietly building his legacy, that moment meant everything.

'Rasanya kayak ajaib,' dia ngomong. 'Main lawan para pemain paling apik, nang hari iki, karo sageda sing kucen... henteu bisa leuwih apik saka iki.' Kuchar bukan nama sané paling mencolok nang tur. article_content: British intelligence officials have warned that chemical weapons stockpiled by the Assad regime in Syria could fall into the hands of extremist groups linked to Al-Qaeda, with potentially catastrophic consequences. According to the Parliamentary Intelligence and Security Committee (ISC), the vast arsenals of sarin, ricin, mustard gas, and VX — the deadliest nerve agent ever developed — are at serious risk of proliferation as the Syrian regime weakens. MI6 chief Sir John Sawers told the ISC there is a 'highly worrying' risk of these weapons being seized during or after the regime’s collapse. The ISC expressed deep concern that terrorists within Syria — or abroad — could gain access to these materials, enabling devastating attacks. UK Foreign Secretary William Hague has warned that British citizens who travel to Syria to fight with rebel groups may return radicalized and pose a direct threat to national security. Prime Minister David Cameron confirmed that Al-Qaeda-affiliated factions within the Syrian opposition have attempted to acquire chemical weapons for potential use. The ISC also highlighted the rising threat of 'lone actor' terrorism, citing the 2010 stabbing of Labour MP Stephen Timms as an example of how isolated attackers are far harder to detect than organized cells. One Home Office official noted that Al-Qaeda leadership increasingly sees lone attacks as more effective than traditional group-based operations, making them a preferred tactic moving forward.

article_content: One of Britain’s oldest continuously operating shops, The Famous menswear store in Cheltenham, is closing its doors after 126 years. Founded in 1886, the family-run business has served generations of customers, offering tailored suits, trousers, and overcoats — priced as low as 13 shillings in its early days. It is one of the last remaining shops in the UK still using a vintage Lamson vacuum cash transport system, installed in 1930, which sends money capsules through tubes to a central cashier office. The Cole family has rented the property since the shop’s inception, but rising costs and an unaffordable lease renewal have forced the decision to close at the end of 2012. Ross Cole, the great-grandson of the shop’s 1896 owner and chairman for over half a century, said the building’s maintenance and rent have become unsustainable. 'We’ve felt the pinch,' he said. 'The business is still thriving, but we simply can’t recreate this experience in a modern space.' Hundreds of customers have expressed their sorrow through letters and calls. 'It’s a very sad day,' added Ross. 'We’re deeply grateful for the loyalty we’ve received.' Richard Cole, the 36-year-old menswear director, echoed the sentiment: 'Our longest-standing customers will miss us dearly.' The shop will hold a closing-down sale starting November 1, while its children’s clothing division will relocate to new premises within the spa town. Martin Quantock, Cheltenham’s town centre manager, noted, 'Few who grew up here haven’t bought school uniforms from The Famous.' Established in the same year as Coca-Cola, Arsenal FC, and the publication of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde, The Famous stands as a living relic of Victorian Britain — a symbol of enduring craftsmanship, community, and quiet resilience.

Ross Cole, cucu cangkang saking pemilik toko warsa 1896 lan direktur kang gelem nganggo 50 taun, ngomong karo biaya pemeliharaan lan sewa wis ora bisa ditindakke. 'Kami rasane tekan batas,' ujaré. article_content: In a chilling discovery that shocked a quiet neighborhood in Thurston County, Washington, a 93-year-old man named Bill Flowers returned home to find a human leg lying in his front yard — carried there by his loyal dog, Liberty. The leg, reportedly intact from the knee down and severed cleanly about four inches above the buttock, had been dragged from nearby land belonging to the Nisqually Reservation. Initially frightened and unsure what to do, Bill considered burying the limb himself, fearing legal trouble. But after four days, his daughter Cheryl urged him to contact authorities. What followed was a large-scale search involving police, K-9 units, and volunteers, who uncovered further remains: a pelvis, ribcage, fragments of a skull, and a jawbone with teeth. Investigators believe the body may have been dismembered and scattered by wildlife. Authorities are now working to identify the victim and determine how the death occurred, cross-referencing local missing persons reports. Liberty, the dog, was fitted with a GPS tracker in hopes she might lead officers to the original site. Bill, still shaken, recalled examining the leg closely: 'Nothing was damaged from the knee down,' he told Komo News. The case remains open as the community grapples with the grim mystery.

Kaki itu, menurut laporan, utuh dari lutut ke bawah dan dipotong bersih sekitar empat inci di atas pantat, ditarik dari tanah di dekat Reservasi Nisqually. Awalnya takut dan bingung, Bill sempat ingin menguburnya sendiri karena khawatir ditangkap. Namun setelah empat hari, putrinya, Cheryl, meyakinkannya untuk melapor ke polisi. Otoritas kini sedang berupaya mengidentifikasi korban dan menentukan penyebab kematiannya, dengan membandingkan laporan orang hilang di daerah itu. Liberty, si anjing, dipasangi pelacak GPS dalam harapan ia bisa menunjukkan lokasi awal penemuan. Bill, yang masih terguncang, mengingat saat ia memeriksa kaki itu: 'Tidak ada kerusakan dari lutut ke bawah,' katanya kepada Komo News. Kasus ini masih dalam penyelidikan sementara komunitas berusaha memahami misteri yang suram ini.

article_content: In Iran, two Christian pastors are caught in a dangerous legal battle over their faith. Youcef Nadarkhani, a 32-year-old minister from Rasht, has been sentenced to death for allegedly leaving Islam — a charge he strongly denies. He says he was never Muslim to begin with, and that authorities pressured him into signing a false confession during interrogation. Meanwhile, in Shiraz, 35-year-old Behrouz Sadegh-Khanjani is facing similar charges, despite being born to Christian parents — his mother an immigrant from the Congo, his father a convert. His lawyer argues the apostasy charge is legally baseless under both Iranian law and Islamic scholarship. Yet, judges are relying on interpretations by religious scholars rather than written statutes, bypassing constitutional guarantees that protect Christians' right to worship. This pattern reflects a wider crackdown: Christians are being targeted across the Middle East, from Iraq to Pakistan, where blasphemy laws can lead to execution. International human rights organizations warn that Iran’s courts are drifting further from rule-of-law principles, substituting personal religious views for legal procedure. Even four senior clerics, including the late Grand Ayatollah Montazeri, have stated that converting to Christianity isn’t apostasy under Islam. Still, Nadarkhani’s sentence was upheld by Iran’s appeals court, and his lawyer has appealed to the Supreme Court. With no clear timeline for resolution, activists fear the worst — especially since the last known execution of a Christian for apostasy in Iran occurred 30 years ago. The world is watching, and voices from the U.S. and beyond are demanding immediate action.

Ia mengatakan ia tidak pernah menjadi Muslim sejak awal, dan bahwa otoritas memaksa dirinya menandatangani pengakuan palsu selama interogasi. Sementara itu, di Shiraz, Behrouz Sadegh-Khanjani, berusia 35 tahun, menghadapi tuduhan serupa, meskipun ia lahir dari orang tua Kristen — ibunya imigran dari Kongo, ayahnya seorang mualaf. Pengacaranya berargumen bahwa tuduhan murtad tidak memiliki dasar hukum baik menurut hukum Iran maupun ilmu teologi Islam. Namun, hakim justru mengandalkan interpretasi para ulama, bukan undang-undang tertulis, sehingga mengabaikan jaminan konstitusional yang melindungi hak Kristen untuk beribadah. Pola ini mencerminkan tekanan lebih luas: umat Kristen sedang ditargetkan di seluruh Timur Tengah, dari Irak hingga Pakistan, di mana hukum penghinaan bisa berujung pada hukuman mati. Organisasi hak asasi manusia internasional memperingatkan bahwa pengadilan Iran semakin menjauh dari prinsip hukum, mengganti prosedur hukum dengan pandangan pribadi agama. Bahkan empat ulama senior, termasuk Grand Ayatollah Montazeri yang telah wafat, menyatakan bahwa pindah ke Kristen bukanlah murtad menurut Islam. Namun, hukuman Nadarkhani tetap dipertahankan oleh pengadilan banding Iran, dan pengacaranya telah mengajukan banding ke Mahkamah Agung. Dengan tidak adanya jadwal jelas, aktivis khawatir yang terburuk akan terjadi — terutama karena eksekusi terakhir seorang Kristen karena murtad di Iran terjadi 30 tahun lalu. article_content: In early 2013, a disturbing incident came to light in a suburb outside Moscow, where a two-year-old girl named Sasha was allegedly subjected to repeated abuse by her nanny, Larisa Zhulitskaya. The child’s parents, deeply troubled by a sudden shift in Sasha’s behavior — including uncharacteristic aggression toward toys — decided to install a hidden camera to monitor her daily routine. What they captured horrified them: footage showed Zhulitskaya physically striking Sasha, yelling at her during meals, threatening to shove her face into a bowl of soup, and locking her alone in the kitchen while she lounged on the sofa watching television. The parents, who have another daughter studying in London and chose to remain anonymous, shared a carefully edited version of the video online as a cautionary message to other families. They stated that more severe clips had been submitted to law enforcement as part of an active investigation. Zhulitskaya, a certified educator with years of experience, responded by claiming she was merely in a bad mood due to personal family struggles, insisting that children generally adored her more than their own parents. Her adult son, Anton, acknowledged that his mother could be overly strict but described the episode as an emotional breakdown rather than habitual cruelty. He criticized the parents for publishing the video publicly, accusing them of attempting to ruin his mother’s reputation by contacting his girlfriend’s family and questioning their readiness to entrust their future grandchildren to her. Despite these defenses, the video evidence painted a chilling picture of neglect and emotional violence. The parents emphasized that Zhulitskaya had worked for them for a full year, presenting herself as cheerful and attentive — making the betrayal all the more devastating. They warned others: 'We thought monsters only existed in movies — but ours looked just like a kind, caring woman.' The case ignited widespread debate about trust in caregivers, the ethics of surveillance, and the urgent need for better child protection systems.

Orang tua anak itu, yang sangat khawatir dengan perubahan mendadak perilaku Sasha — termasuk agresi tidak biasa terhadap mainan — memutuskan memasang kamera tersembunyi untuk memantau rutinitas harian anaknya. Yang mereka rekam membuat mereka terkejut: rekaman menunjukkan Zhulitskaya memukul Sasha, berteriak padanya saat makan, mengancam akan menekan wajahnya ke dalam mangkuk sup, dan mengurungnya sendirian di dapur sementara dia bersantai di sofa menonton televisi. Orang tua itu, yang memiliki seorang putri lain yang sedang belajar di London dan memilih tetap anonim, membagikan versi diedit dari video tersebut secara daring sebagai pesan peringatan bagi keluarga lain. Mereka menyatakan bahwa klip yang lebih parah telah diserahkan kepada aparat hukum sebagai bagian dari penyelidikan aktif. Zhulitskaya, seorang pendidik bersertifikat dengan pengalaman bertahun-tahun, merespons dengan mengklaim bahwa ia hanya dalam suasana hati buruk karena masalah pribadi, menegaskan bahwa anak-anak umumnya lebih menyukainya daripada orang tua mereka sendiri. Putra dewasanya, Anton, mengakui bahwa ibunya bisa sangat ketat tetapi menggambarkan kejadian itu sebagai kegagalan emosional, bukan kekejaman berkelanjutan. Ia mengkritik orang tua itu karena mempublikasikan video tersebut secara terbuka, menuduh mereka berusaha merusak reputasi ibunya dengan menghubungi keluarga pacarnya dan mempertanyakan kesediaan mereka untuk mempercayakan cucu masa depan mereka kepadanya. Meskipun ada pembelaan ini, bukti video menggambarkan gambaran menyeramkan tentang kelalaian dan kekerasan emosional. Orang tua itu menekankan bahwa Zhulitskaya telah bekerja untuk mereka selama satu tahun penuh, menampilkan dirinya sebagai ceria dan perhatian — menjadikan pengkhianatan ini semakin menyakitkan. Mereka memperingatkan orang lain: 'Kami pikir monster hanya ada di film — tapi milik kami tampak seperti wanita baik dan penuh perhatian.' Kasus ini memicu perdebatan luas tentang kepercayaan pada pengasuh, etika pengawasan, dan kebutuhan mendesak akan sistem perlindungan anak yang lebih baik.

article_content: New York (CNN) — Twelve firefighters from Ladder Company 3, who lost their lives attempting to rescue people in the North Tower of the World Trade Center on September 11, 2001, were honored Wednesday in a ceremony at the 9/11 Memorial and Museum. Mayor Michael Bloomberg, Fire Department of New York Commissioner Salvatore J. Cassano, firefighters, family members, and friends watched as the company’s truck — covered in a white sheet — was permanently returned to the site where the Twin Towers once stood. The 60,000-pound truck had been preserved in a climate-controlled room by the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey, according to a press release from the 9/11 Memorial Museum. It was escorted to the former World Trade Center site by the current Ladder 3 fire truck. As the vehicle was lowered to its permanent location, 70 feet below ground, the FDNY Emerald Society Pipes and Drums played 'America the Beautiful.' 'We will never forget the heroism of the hundreds of firefighters and other first responders who rushed into those burning towers on September 11,' Bloomberg said in a statement. 'The sacrifice of Ladder Company 3 and the FDNY is something we must all honor. Their names, along with those of other courageous first responders who perished, will be permanently etched in bronze on the memorial, and their truck will be preserved in the museum as a testament to their bravery.' 'All the memories come back — all the emotions,' said Robert Sweeney, Chief of Operations for the FDNY, speaking to CNN. 'Some anger. Some pride in the department.' The firefighters from the East Village-based company were conducting search-and-rescue operations in the North Tower when it collapsed, Sweeney said. The completed memorial features two large reflecting pools surrounded by more than 400 trees and bronze panels inscribed with the names of all 9/11 victims. The memorial opened to families of the victims on the 10th anniversary of the attacks, September 11, 2011, and to the general public the following day.
translated_content: New York (CNN) — Dua belas petugas pemadam kebakaran dari Ladder Company 3, yang meninggal dalam upaya menyelamatkan orang-orang di Menara Utara World Trade Center pada 11 September 2001, dihormati pada Rabu dalam sebuah upacara di 9/11 Memorial dan Museum. Wali Kota Michael Bloomberg, Komisaris Departemen Pemadam Kebakaran New York Salvatore J. Cassano, para petugas pemadam kebakaran, anggota keluarga, dan teman-teman menyaksikan truk perusahaan itu — yang ditutupi selembar kain putih — dikembalikan secara permanen ke lokasi tempat Menara Kembar berdiri. Truk seberat 60.000 pon itu dipertahankan dalam ruangan beriklim terkendali oleh Otoritas Pelabuhan New York dan New Jersey, menurut rilis pers dari 9/11 Memorial Museum. Truk itu diiringi ke lokasi bekas World Trade Center oleh truk Ladder 3 saat ini. Saat kendaraan diturunkan ke lokasi permanennya, 70 kaki di bawah tanah, band pipa dan drum FDNY Emerald Society memainkan 'America the Beautiful.' 'Kami tidak akan pernah melupakan keberanian ratusan petugas pemadam kebakaran dan responder pertama lainnya yang bergegas masuk ke menara-menara yang terbakar pada 11 September,' kata Bloomberg dalam pernyataannya. 'Pengorbanan Ladder Company 3 dan FDNY adalah sesuatu yang harus kita semua hormati. Nama-nama mereka, bersama dengan nama responder pertama pemberani lainnya yang gugur, akan terukir selamanya dalam perunggu di monumen, dan truk mereka akan diawetkan di museum sebagai bukti keberanian mereka.' 'Semua kenangan kembali — semua emosi,' kata Robert Sweeney, Kepala Operasi FDNY, kepada CNN. 'Beberapa kemarahan. Beberapa kebanggaan pada departemen.' Petugas pemadam kebakaran dari perusahaan berbasis East Village sedang melakukan operasi pencarian dan penyelamatan di Menara Utara ketika bangunan itu runtuh, kata Sweeney. Monumen yang telah selesai menampilkan dua kolam refleksi besar yang dikelilingi lebih dari 400 pohon dan panel perunggu yang bertuliskan nama-nama semua korban serangan 9/11. Monumen dibuka untuk keluarga korban pada peringatan 10 tahun serangan, 11 September 2011, dan untuk umum pada hari berikutnya.

article_content: (CNN) -- Udinese have moved to the top of the Italian Serie A table on goal difference from Lazio after captain Antonio Di Natale scored again in a 2-1 victory over Siena on Sunday. With previous leaders Juventus seeing their match against Napoli called off due to torrential rain, Udinese, Lazio, and Milan all secured wins, pushing Juve down to fourth place. Udinese took the lead after just 54 seconds against Siena, when Dusan Basta prodded the ball home from close range. Di Natale, the prolific scorer, doubled the advantage in the 64th minute, cutting inside a defender to finish Pablo Armero's long pass. Siena pulled one back 13 minutes from time when Francesco Bolzoni fired home Emanuele Calaio's half-volley header, but the home side held on to reach 21 points from 10 games. Lazio are level on points but trail on goal difference after a 1-0 home win over Parma. Giuseppe Sculli poked home the winner with just five minutes left, leaving Edy Reja's side firmly in the title race. However, the standout performance of the day came from Milan, who sit ominously just one point behind in third after thrashing Catania 4-0. Zlatan Ibrahimovic opened the scoring in the seventh minute with a penalty after Davide Lanzafame fouled Robinho in the box. Robinho then doubled Milan's lead in the 24th minute, curling the ball home after Ibrahimovic sent him clear down the left wing. The pair combined again for the third goal in the 69th minute, with Robinho's shot being bundled over the line by defender Francesco Lodi. Gianluca Zambrotta added the fourth three minutes later, finishing off a fumbled free-kick from Alberto Aquilani.

Dengan juara sebelumnya Juventus yang pertandingannya melawan Napoli dibatalkan akibat hujan lebat, Udinese, Lazio, dan Milan semuanya meraih kemenangan, sehingga Juve turun ke peringkat empat. Udinese unggul setelah hanya 54 detik melawan Siena, ketika Dusan Basta menendang bola masuk dari jarak dekat. Di Natale, pencetak gol produktif, memperbesar keunggulan di menit ke-64, memotong masuk melewati seorang bek untuk menyelesaikan umpan panjang Pablo Armero. Siena memperkecil kedudukan 13 menit menjelang akhir, ketika Francesco Bolzoni menembakkan bola setelah menyundul setengah voli dari Emanuele Calaio, tetapi tim tuan rumah bertahan untuk meraih 21 poin dari 10 pertandingan. Lazio sama-sama mengumpulkan poin, tetapi tertinggal dalam selisih gol setelah menang 1-0 di kandang melawan Parma. Giuseppe Sculli mencetak gol kemenangan hanya lima menit menjelang akhir, membuat tim asuhan Edy Reja tetap bersaing ketat di gelar juara. Namun, performa terbaik hari ini datang dari Milan, yang berada hanya satu poin di belakang di posisi tiga setelah menghancurkan Catania 4-0. Zlatan Ibrahimovic membuka skor di menit ketujuh dengan tendangan penalti setelah Davide Lanzafame melakukan pelanggaran terhadap Robinho di kotak penalti. Penyerang Brasil Robinho kemudian mencetak gol kedua di menit ke-24, menendang bola melengkung masuk setelah Ibrahimovic mengirimnya lewat sayap kiri. Keduanya kembali bekerja sama untuk gol ketiga di menit ke-69, dengan tembakan Robinho dibawa masuk oleh bek yang mundur, Francesco Lodi. Gianluca Zambrotta menambahkan gol keempat tiga menit kemudian, memanfaatkan sundulan bola hasil tendangan bebas Alberto Aquilani yang gagal diselamatkan kiper.

article_content: A company set up and operated by Darren Flood — Victoria Beckham’s brother-in-law — is at the center of a fraud investigation after an 83-year-old widow was deceived out of her life savings of £235,000. Investigators allege that staff members used the Beckham name in their sales pitch, claiming, 'If Victoria Beckham’s relative is investing with us, it must be fine.' Flood, 35, was a director of one of the companies involved in the alleged fraud. However, there is no suggestion he knew about or participated in the misconduct. The victim, a childless widow from Woking, Surrey, was picked up from her home and taken on a tour of a rented mailbox in Canary Wharf, presented as a 'virtual office.' She was also treated to an expensive lunch. She was convinced to invest after being told the company used Coutts Bank and had ties to the Beckhams. Her bank manager flagged the unusual transactions, prompting police intervention. Five people connected to the company have been arrested and questioned about the scheme, which involved fake investments in gold, diamonds, and land in Brazil. Flood has not been arrested. When contacted, his wife said he would not comment. The investigation continues, with all suspects due to return on police bail in April.

Penyelidik ngakungaken yen staf kumpani iki nyebut nama Beckham neng pangajén jualan, ngomong, 'Yen relasi Victoria Beckham njaluk investasi karo kita, pasti aman.' Flood, 35 taun, mangkana direktur saking salah siji kumpani sané keterlibatan neng penipuan sané diduga. Nanging, teu ana petunjuk yen dia tahu utawi terlibat neng kelakuan salah. Lima orang sané keterlibatan karo kumpani iki ditangkap lan diinterogasi ngenani skema sané melibatkan investasi palsu neng emas, berlian, lan tanah neng Brasil. Flood teu ditangkap. article_content: Every holiday needs a song — and National Unfriend Day is no exception. On 'Jimmy Kimmel Live,' country singers Brad Paisley and Darius Rucker premiered 'The National Unfriend Day Soundtrack' to kick off the satirical celebration. Lyrics mock persistent social media annoyances: 'To all the friends I've unfriended before / Who sent me quizzes about Jersey Shore / You made my life a hell with your stupid LOL.' Kimmel declared November 11 as National Unfriend Day (NUD), encouraging Facebook users to remove contacts who aren’t genuine friends. 'NUD is the international day when all Facebook users shall protect the sacred nature of friendship by cutting out any 'friend fat' on their pages occupied by people who are not truly their friends,' according to the show’s website. The campaign ignited viral momentum: '#unfriend' trended on Twitter, and numerous articles surfaced offering advice on how and why to unfriend. Users shared reactions like: 'It’s easier to deactivate my profile than unfriend 463 people.' and 'Taking five minutes to unfriend everyone I don’t know — long overdue!' Ironically, some users responded by unfollowing Kimmel himself, with one tweeting: 'In honor of National Unfriend Day, I’m removing you from Twitter.' Common unfriending rationales include: being friends with your mom, not knowing the person, hiding their posts due to annoyance, receiving endless invites to quizzes or events, or remaining connected to high school acquaintances with whom you’ve lost touch. Unfriending on Facebook is simple: visit the profile, scroll to the bottom of the left sidebar, and click 'Remove from Friends.' On Twitter, select 'Unfollow' beneath the user’s name.

article_content: In one of the most harrowing cases of violence ever recorded in Miami, 65-year-old Ronald Poppo endured a nightmarish assault that left him permanently blind and with devastating facial injuries. On May 26, 2012, he was attacked by 31-year-old Rudy Eugene, who tore away chunks of his face and gouged out his eyes. Police arrived to find Eugene still attacking and fatally shot him to stop the rampage. Though early reports suggested Eugene was high on synthetic drugs known as bath salts, toxicology results later confirmed only marijuana was present. Poppo, who had been sleeping near a highway, had never met his attacker and insists he did nothing to provoke the assault — contradicting rumors that they’d met at a shelter or that he stole Eugene’s Bible. In a chilling interview with police, Poppo described how Eugene screamed he would die, smashed his face into the pavement, and held him in wrestling holds while removing his eyes. He credits the responding officers with saving his life, saying he would be far worse off without their intervention. Despite his trauma, Poppo’s memory of the event contained gaps and distortions: he believed Eugene emerged from a passing car and was wearing clothes, but surveillance footage showed the attacker was completely naked and approached on foot. A New York native, Poppo had lived on Florida’s streets for three decades, cut off from his family, who had long assumed he died by suicide. After undergoing multiple surgeries at Jackson Memorial Hospital, he now resides in a long-term rehabilitation center, learning to live without sight.

Pada 26 Mei 2012, dheweke diserang dening Rudy Eugene, 31 taun, sing nyobek-nyobek wajahé lan nyabut mataé. Polisi teka nemu Eugene lagi nyerang lan nembaké mati kanggo ngenteni serangané. Sadurunge dadi kabar, Eugene lagi kena efek obat sintetis sing disebut bath salts, tapi hasil toksikologi mbuktekake mung mariyuana sing ditemokake. Poppo, sing lagi tidur ngarep jalan raya, ora kenal pelaku lan yakin ora ngajak ribut — nyelakake desas-desus yen mereka ketemu ing penampungan tunawisma utawa dheweke nyolong Alkitab Eugene. Dalam wawancara karo polisi, Poppo njelaske yen Eugene nyeru ‘aku bakal mati’, nyebabake wajahé karo aspal, lan nggandhengé karo pegangan gulat sambil nyabut mataé. Dheweke ngucapke trima kasih marang petugas polisi sing nyelametake uripé, ngombe yen dheweke bakal luwih parah tanpa bantuané. Nanging, ing tengah trauma, inggih punika ingatan Poppo ana kesalahan: dheweke nyangka Eugene muncul saka mobil lan ngenakan pakaian, nanging rekaman CCTV mbuktekake pelaku telanjang lan nyerang karo ngeling. Asli saka New York, Poppo wis ngemban hidup ing jalanan Florida selama 30 taun, dipisahake saka keluargane, sing wis lama nyangka dheweke mati bunuh diri. Sawise operasi berkali-kali ing Jackson Memorial Hospital, saiki dheweke tinggal ing pusat rehabilitasi jangka panjang, belajar hidup tanpa penglihatan.

article_content: While commuting from Charlbury in Oxfordshire to London each Monday morning, former Justice Secretary Jack Straw would often share a train carriage with Rebekah Brooks — then a top newspaper editor. They’d chat about what was trending in the press and the latest political gossip, but not constantly. 'There were people all around,' Straw explained, 'so you didn’t say everything.' Straw, now reflecting on those days at the Leveson Inquiry, admitted that during Tony Blair’s era, Labour’s ties with the media had grown uncomfortably intimate. He described the dynamic as 'incestuous' — a term he used to capture how certain journalists were given privileged access, feeding off insider stories while others were shut out. He clarified that this wasn’t unique to government: the closeness began when Labour was in opposition, fueled by a desire to win back media favor after losing the 1992 election. Once in power, Downing Street never broke the habit. 'It suited us. It suited them,' he said. 'But I didn’t like it.' Straw also weighed in on Rupert Murdoch, whom he’d met only briefly but observed closely. He didn’t claim there was a direct deal — no written agreement, no explicit exchange. But he believed Murdoch understood that keeping his newspapers politically flexible could unlock doors — on licensing, media regulation, even football broadcasting rights. 'He thought there was something in it,' Straw said, adding that Murdoch seemed to relish wielding influence for its own sake. Their train chats ended in 2009, when Brooks took over as CEO of News International. That same year, the phone-hacking scandal began to unravel — leading to criminal charges against Brooks and her husband, among others. Straw, who attended their wedding, now sees those friendships as part of a larger, flawed system — one where proximity to power blurred lines between journalism and politics.

article_content: After six years, Accenture made the rare move of severing ties with golf superstar Tiger Woods—becoming the first major sponsor to do so after Woods publicly acknowledged extramarital affairs and stepped away from competitive play. William D. Green, the company’s chairman and CEO, spoke candidly to The New York Times about the weight of leadership: as a man who once struggled with personal accountability, he now shoulders responsibility for 177,000 employees. ‘The spiritual duty to those people,’ he said, ‘is something I’m still learning to carry.’ In Italy, Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi was hospitalized after a man hurled a miniature cathedral model at his face during a campaign rally. The 73-year-old leader suffered a fractured nose and broken teeth and is being treated with painkillers and antibiotics. This incident adds to a year filled with legal battles—including tax fraud allegations—public protests, rumors of escort hires, and a bitter divorce from his wife of 19 years. Meanwhile, in Washington D.C., schools chancellor Michelle Rhee sparked national conversation after her district posted the only significant gains in math scores among 11 major urban school systems. Her controversial decision to dismiss around 250 teachers—some tenured—for underperformance drew praise from reform advocates and criticism from unions. A Wall Street Journal editorial pressed the Obama administration: Why isn’t more federal support being extended to her bold vision? On a more hopeful note, bestselling author Stephen King and his wife, Tabitha, covered the $12,999 cost to send 150 Maine National Guard soldiers home for the holidays by bus before their January deployment to Afghanistan. The gesture, reported by the Bangor Daily News, touched hearts across the state. Robert G. Heft, a 17-year-old Ohio student in 1958, stitched together a 50-star American flag as a history class project. His design was chosen by President Eisenhower as the official flag after Alaska and Hawaii joined the Union. Heft, who passed away this weekend at age 67, never sought fame—but his creation became a permanent symbol of American identity. What makes someone unforgettable in the news? It’s rarely just the act—it’s the story behind it. Was it courage? Contradiction? Redemption? A quiet act of kindness amid chaos? The people who stick with us aren’t always the powerful—they’re the ones whose humanity, however messy, forces us to pause, wonder, and ask: Why did they do that?

William D. article_content: Before Lance Armstrong sat down with Oprah Winfrey, many assumed he was finished — a fallen icon buried under scandal, accusations, and broken trust. Once celebrated as a cycling legend who conquered the Tour de France seven times, he’d become the face of sport’s darkest secrets. But beneath the hype, he was never just a symbol. He was a man who pushed boundaries, embraced cheating as routine, and let the system protect him because it benefited everyone — from sponsors to fans to officials who looked away. The sport loved his swagger, his wins, his American grit — until it didn’t. Then, suddenly, they wanted justice. And when the truth came out, Armstrong didn’t play the victim. No blaming teammates. No crying over bad advice. He owned it. That alone stunned the world. While others denied, deflected, or whispered ‘everyone did it,’ Armstrong said plainly: ‘I did this.’ It wasn’t pretty, but it was real. For a sport drowning in lies, his honesty felt revolutionary. He even acknowledged that new anti-doping measures are working — a sign that change is possible. Yes, he betrayed millions. Yes, he damaged the credibility of cancer survivors who trusted his Livestrong brand. And yes, he’ll carry this for life. But for the first time, he’s not hiding behind the myth. Maybe that’s where healing begins — not with forgiveness, but with truth.

Dhuwuré dipérkarakna minangka legenda balap sepeda sing ngalahake Tour de France pitu kali, dia wis dadi wajah rahasia paling kelam ing olahraga. Nanging ing ngendi ngendié, dia ora mung simbol. Dia kuwatir kang njalari batas, mangan nyelak saling nggawe, lan biyasa sistem mbela dheweke amarga nguntungke kabèh — saka sponsor nganti panggemar nganti pejabat sing munggah. Olahraga seneng gayane, kemenangane, semangat Amerikane — ngati ora lagi. Banjur, tiba-tiba, padha pengin keadilan. Lan nalika kebenaran keluar, Armstrong ora muter dadi korban. Ora nyalahake rekan tim. Ora nangis amarga nasihat sing salah. Dheweke njanjurake. Iki nggawa kaget dunya. Sambi liyané nolak, nyeret, utawa mbiyantu ‘kabeh padha melu’, Armstrong ngomong kanthi klir: ‘Aku sing nggawe iki.’ Iki ora apik, tapi asli. Kanggo olahraga sing tenggelam ing kebohongan, kejujurané dirasakna revolusioner. Dheweke uga ngakui bahwa langkah anyar anti-doping wis ana — tanda yen perubahan bisa. Ya, dheweke ngebali ratusan ribu. Ya, dheweke nyebabake kredibilitas para penyintas kanker sing percaya marang merek Livestrongé. Lan ya, dheweke bakal ngangkut iki sabanjure. Nanging kanggo pertama kaline, dheweke ora nyembunyike mitos. Mungkin iki tempat mulainé kesembuhan — ora karo pengampunan, nanging karo kebenaran.

article_content: A vast database system, known as Capita One, is collecting highly detailed personal information on around eight million schoolchildren across the UK—often without the knowledge or consent of their parents. Teachers are uploading data on pupils up to six times a day, including academic performance, attendance, behavioral records, and special educational needs. This information is stored on local council servers and can be accessed by multiple public agencies, including the police, NHS, youth offending teams, and charities. According to The Sunday Times, approximately 22,000 schools and 100 local authorities are already using the system to build a continuous digital profile of each child. While Capita provides the software infrastructure, it does not store the data centrally. Instead, each local authority manages its own database and controls who can access it. A separate tool called API allows authorized external staff—such as social workers—to retrieve specific child records. Swindon Borough Council, for example, shares data on over 48,000 pupils with youth offending teams and NHS Swindon, asserting compliance with data protection regulations. However, most parents remain unaware that their children’s information is being collected, stored, and shared. Nick Pickles of the civil liberties group Big Brother Watch said, 'Parents will be shocked that they are being kept in the dark about how their child's information is being gathered and exactly what it is used for.' The Information Commissioner’s Office has confirmed it will investigate whether the Capita One system complies with UK data protection laws. Capita maintains that only a small number of councils enable external access, and all data handling follows legal requirements. The Department for Education has stated there are no current plans to centralize this data nationally.

Guru-guru ngunggah data babagan murid sawetara kaping enem saben dinten, kalebu prestasi akademik, kehadiran, catatan perilaku, lan kebutuhan pendidikan khusus. Kabupaten Swindon, contone, mbagi data babagan luwih saka 48.000 murid karo tim penindakan pemuda lan NHS Swindon, ngaku patuh karo peraturan perlindungan data. Nanging, kabeh orang tua ora tahu yen informasi anaké dikumpulake, disimpen, lan dibagike. Nick Pickles saka kelompok hak sipil Big Brother Watch nyebut, 'Orang tuane bakal kaget yen mereka dijupuk ing dheweke ngenani carane informasi anaké dikumpulake lan digunakake.' article_content: This week, Iran is welcoming over 120 developing nations to the Non-Aligned Movement summit — a bloc formed in 1961 to balance power during the Cold War. As the current three-year president of the group, Iran is putting Western sanctions at the center of discussions, urging member states to deepen economic cooperation despite international pressure. Can nations that identify as non-aligned actually build resilient trade networks among themselves? Meanwhile, in a surprising twist in the luxury food world, the global caviar market is shifting. Once dominated by Iran, Azerbaijan, and Russia thanks to wild sturgeon from the Caspian Sea, the industry is collapsing under overfishing and strict bans on wild harvesting. Enter Kibbutz Dan in northern Israel: a small agricultural community now farming nearly 70,000 sturgeon in controlled environments. Each fish yields caviar worth thousands of dollars — turning a once-endangered delicacy into a thriving aquaculture innovation.

Minangka presidén tiga taun saiki, Irán nggawa sanksi Barat dadi inti diskusi, mendorong anggota kanggo nggandhèngake kerja sama ekonomi nanging tetep tekan tekanan internasional. Bisakah negara-negara sing nganggep dirié ora berpihak mbangun jaringan perdagangan sing tangguh antaré wongé dhewe? Samentara iku, ing panggonan sing anyar ing dunya pangan mewah, pasar kaviar global lagi ganti. article_content: When Julita Echeverria Abalsamo passed away in 1993 from complications after heart surgery, her husband Rocky 'Roque' Abalsamo didn’t just lose a spouse—he lost the center of his world. For the next three decades, he made St. Joseph Cemetery in West Roxbury his second home. Every day, rain or shine, he arrived at opening and stayed until closing, rarely eating or drinking—not out of neglect, but as a quiet act of reverence. He brought photos, small mementos, and a blue chair, greeting her each morning with, 'I am here!' On her birthday, December 20, he’d toast her with sparkling cider. At night, he’d scatter crumbs for chipmunks, believing they’d keep her company after he left. His devotion caught the eye of The Boston Globe in 2000, when he was 84. The story went viral, drawing strangers who brought food, warm clothes, flowers, and even ceramic angels to decorate her grave. Among them were Linda Handley, a local math teacher, and John Tobin, the cemetery groundskeeper. Rocky noticed they were both unmarried and middle-aged. On the 61st anniversary of his first kiss with Julita, he invited them to meet together. A year later, they married—and in their wedding program, they credited Rocky and Julita for the miracle of their union. After his son Roque Jr. died in a car accident in California in 2005, Rocky began spending more time with his remaining family. Still, he never abandoned his daily ritual—until July 2023, when he fell ill. He died peacefully on January 22, 2024, at age 97. His daughter Angela Arai said his greatest gift was living fully, one day at a time, without regret. 'He lived his life his way,' she said. 'And now, finally, he’s with her again.' As he requested, Rocky was laid to rest beside Julita—on her left, just as they walked through life, side by side.
translated_content: Saat Julita Echeverria Abalsamo wafat ing 1993 akibat komplikasi sawise operasi jantung, suaminya Rocky 'Roque' Abalsamo ora cuma kehilangan pasangane—tapi kehilangan pusat duniane. Selama tiga dekade, ia njadikan Kebun Raya St. Joseph ing West Roxbury minangka rumah keduane. Setiap dinten, hujan utawa cerah, iya dateng saiki buka lan tetep nganti tutup, jarang mangan utawa minum—ora amarga lalai, nanging minangka bentuk panghormatan tenang. Ia mbawa foto, kenangan cilik, lan kursi biru, nyapa istine tiap pagi kanthi, 'Aku nengen!' Ing dina ulang taune, 20 Desember, iya bersulang kanggo karo cider berkarbonasi. Ing ndalu, iya ngrampungake remah-remah kanggo tupai, percaya yen wong-wong mau bakal nemani istine sawise iya weruh. Kesetiaane ngrampungake perhatian The Boston Globe ing 2000, nalika iya umure 84 taun. Ceritane dadi viral, ngrampungake wong-wong asing sing mbawa mangan, pakaian hangat, bunga, bahkan patung malaikat keramik kanggo nghiasi makame. Di antarane ana Linda Handley, seorang guru matematika lokal, lan John Tobin, petugas pemelihara kuburan. Rocky ngelingi merek berdua durung nikah lan umure paruh bayi. Ing pangingetan 61 taun ciuman pertamane karo Julita, iya ngundang merek metu bareng. Sawise setaun, merek nikah—lan ing program perkawinan loro, merek ngilangi Rocky lan Julita amarga keajaiban perkawinan loro. Sawise putrane, Roque Jr., meninggal ing kecelakaan mobil ing California ing 2005, Rocky mulai luwih becik ngabekti wektu karo keluargane sing wis ana. Nanging, iya ora pernah ninggalake ritual hariane—sampai Juli 2023, nalika iya sakit. Iya wafat kanthi tenang ing 22 Januari 2024, ing umur 97 taun. Putrinya, Angela Arai, ngomong hadiah paling gedhe iku hidup sepenuhe, siji dinten karo siji, tanpa penyesalan. 'Ia njalari hidupne sesuai carane dhewe,' ujaré. 'Lan saiki, akhire, iya karo dheweke maneh.' Sapertos permintaane, Rocky dimakamake ing samping Julita—ing sebelah kirine, kaya dulu loro padha melintas bareng, berdampingan.

article_content: A police helicopter that crashed into a busy Glasgow pub, killing 10 people, suffered a dual engine failure, according to an interim report. The Eurocopter EC135 plunged into the roof of the Clutha Bar in November 2013, claiming the lives of all three crew members and seven patrons. The Air Accidents Investigation Branch (AAIB) found that both engines 'flamed out' during the final stages of the flight. However, the cause of the failure remains unknown — 76kg (168lb) of fuel remained in the main tank at impact. Investigators are also examining why no Mayday call was made and why the aircraft could not execute a controlled landing. The helicopter departed Glasgow City Heliport at 8:45 p.m. on November 29 with 400kg (882lb) of fuel — sufficient for approximately 1 hour and 35 minutes of flight. At 10:18 p.m., the pilot requested clearance to re-enter the Glasgow control zone to return to the heliport. This was approved, and no further radio transmissions were received. Recorded data indicates the right engine flamed out first, followed shortly by the left engine. The helicopter then descended rapidly in an upright attitude and struck the roof of the Clutha Vaults bar. Evidence shows neither the main rotor nor the Fenestron tail rotor was rotating at impact. The last recorded radar position, at 10:22 p.m., showed the aircraft at approximately 400ft (122m) above mean sea level. Examination of the fuel system revealed no leaks, blockages, or failures in pipework or valves, all of which were found in the 'open' position. More than 100 people were inside the bar at the time of impact. Among the dead were pilot David Traill, 51, and police officers Kirsty Nelis, 36, and Tony Collins, 43. Six patrons also perished: Robert Jenkins, 61; Mark O'Prey, 44; Colin Gibson, 33; John McGarrigle, 57; Gary Arthur, 48; and Samuel McGhee, 56. Customer Joe Cusker, 59, was pulled alive from the wreckage but died in hospital nearly two weeks later. Thirty-two others were injured, 12 seriously. Bond Air Services, the operator, has begun making interim payments to victims’ families through Thomsons Solicitors. The AAIB emphasized that this interim report — labeled a 'special bulletin' — provides factual updates but does not include analysis or conclusions. A book of condolences signed by UK MPs was presented to Glasgow’s Lord Provost, Sadie Docherty, by Commons Speaker John Bercow. The Prince of Wales also signed the council’s condolence book during a visit to the city. BALPA and other stakeholders continue to support the investigation, urging thorough examination of the fuel system to determine the root cause.

Eurocopter EC135 njlajah ing atap Clutha Bar ing November 2013, nyebabak tewas kaping telu anggota awak lan pitu pelanggan. Air Accidents Investigation Branch (AAIB) nemokaké yen kaping loro mesin 'flamed out' dina tahap akhir penerbangan. Nanging, penyebab kegagalan tetep ora jelas — 76kg (168lb) bahan bakar masih ana ing tangki utama sajrone krash. Penyelidik uga nyelidiki ngapa ora ana panggilan Mayday lan ngapa pesawat ora bisa laksanakaké pendaratan terkendali. Helikopter iki berangkat saka Glasgow City Heliport ing jam 8:45 p.m. ing November 29 karo 400kg (882lb) bahan bakar — cukup kanggo sawetara 1 jam 35 menit penerbangan. Ing jam 10:18 p.m., pilot menehaké permintaan kanggo masuk maneh ing zona kontrol Glasgow kanggo balik menyang heliport. Permintaan iku disetujui, lan ora ana transmisi radio liyane sing ditampa. Data sing direkam nemokaké yen mesin kanan mati pertama, diiringi sawetara saat kemudian mesin kiwa. Helikopter padha turun cepet ing posisi tegak lan nyerang atap Clutha Vaults bar. Bukti nglalekaké yen baling-baling utama lan baling-baling ekor Fenestron ora muter sajrone dampak. Posisi radar pungkasan sing direkam, ing jam 10:22 p.m., nuduhaké pesawat ing ketinggian sawetara 400 kaki (122m) ing ndhuwur permukaan laut rata-rata. Pemeriksaan sistem bahan bakar nemokaké ora ana kebocoran, sumbatan, utawa kegagalan ing pipa utawa katup, kabeh sing ditemokaké ing posisi 'buka'. Luwih saka 100 wong ana ing dalam bar sajrone krash. Kanggo korban tewas yaiku pilot David Traill, 51, lan petugas polisi Kirsty Nelis, 36, lan Tony Collins, 43. Pitu pelanggan uga tewas: Robert Jenkins, 61; Mark O'Prey, 44; Colin Gibson, 33; John McGarrigle, 57; Gary Arthur, 48; lan Samuel McGhee, 56. Pelanggan Joe Cusker, 59, diarani hidup saka reruntuhan nanging tewas ing rumah sakit hampir dua minggu kemudian. Tiga puluh loro wong liyane luka, 12 ing kondisi serius. Bond Air Services, operator, wis mulai mbayar kompensasi antara marang keluarga korban nglalui Thomsons Solicitors. AAIB ngedegaké laporan antara iki — sing diarani 'special bulletin' — mung ngrangkum informasi fakta tanpa analisis utawa kesimpulan. Buku rasa sedih sing ditandatangani anggota parlemen Inggris diserahkan marang Lord Provost Glasgow, Sadie Docherty, dening Commons Speaker John Bercow. Pangeran Wales uga nandatangani buku sedih dewan kota nalika mlayang menyang kutha kanggo ketemu para selamat lan petugas darurat. BALPA lan stakeholder liyane terus mendukung penyelidikan, mohon pemeriksaan menyeluruh saka sistem bahan bakar kanggo nemokaké akar penyebab.

article_content: Five ex-Royal Netherlands Air Force F-16s have arrived at Romania’s 86th Air Base near Fetești, marking the operational launch of the European F-16 Training Center (EFTC). While the jets remain Dutch property, the training mission is led by a coalition of U.S. and European private contractors—not official military personnel. Lockheed Martin organizes the center, but day-to-day instruction and maintenance are outsourced. Draken International and GFD GmbH provide experienced F-16 instructor pilots with recent frontline combat experience from U.S. and European air forces. Draken, backed by private equity firm Blackstone, has longstanding ties to both Dutch and Norwegian governments and Lockheed Martin, positioning it as a natural partner for this effort. GFD, a German firm with 250 staff—including 100 retired German Air Force and Navy personnel—will offer advanced flight simulation using its fleet of 15 specially equipped Learjet 35/36 aircraft. These jets simulate enemy threats during live training exercises. Daedalus Aviation Group, based in the Netherlands, will oversee maintenance, repair, and overhaul of the growing F-16 fleet—expected to reach 12–18 aircraft. Meanwhile, Belgium’s ILIAS Solutions will manage logistics, flight scheduling, and training data systems using software developed for the Belgian and Australian air forces. This multi-national contractor model enables the U.S. to support Ukraine’s air force development while maintaining diplomatic distance from direct involvement near Russia’s border. It also mirrors NATO’s collaborative spirit, aligning with Romania’s alliance membership and Ukraine’s long-term goal of integration. The EFTC represents a critical milestone in equipping Ukrainian pilots with Western fourth-generation fighters—a necessary step before potential deployment against Russian forces. Whether these trained pilots and aircraft will ultimately see combat in Ukraine remains uncertain, but the foundation for their readiness is now firmly in place.

Sambil pesawat tetap milik Belanda, misi pelatihan dipimpin ku koleksi kontraktor swasta Amerika Serikat jeung Eropa—bukan personel militer resmi. Lockheed Martin ngatur pusat iki, tapi latihan jeung pemeliharaan harian diserahkan ka pihak ketiga. Draken International jeung GFD GmbH nyadiakeun instruktur F-16 berpengalaman sareng pangalaman tempur anyar ti angkatan udara AS jeung Eropa. Draken, didukung ku perusahaan modal ventura Blackstone, ngagaduhan hubungan panjang jeung pamarentah Belanda jeung Norwegia jeung Lockheed Martin, ngajadikeunna mitra alami pikeun usaha iki. GFD, perusahaan Jerman aranjeunna 250 pegawai—termasuk 100 mantan tentara Angkatan Udara jeung Angkatan Laut Jerman—akan nyadiakeun simulasi penerbangan tingkat lanjut ngagunakeun armada 15 pesawat Learjet 35/36 sing diadaptasi. Pesawat-pesawat ieu ngasimulasikan ancaman lawan dina latihan langsung. Daedalus Aviation Group, anu based di Belanda, bakal ngawasai pemeliharaan, perbaikan, jeung overhaul armada F-16 sing terus berkembang—diprediksi bakal capai 12–18 pesawat. Sambil itu, ILIAS Solutions asal Belgia bakal ngatur logistik, jadwal penerbangan, jeung sistem data pelatihan ngagunakeun perangkat lunak sing dikembangkeun pikeun angkatan udara Belgia jeung Australia. Model kontraktor multinasional ieu nyababkeun AS bisa mendukung pengembangan angkatan udara Ukraina sambil mimiti jarak diplomatik ti partisipasi langsung dekat perbatasan Rusia. Iki ogé ngamiripikeun semangat NATO, sejajar jeung keanggotaan Romania dina aliansi jeung tujuan jangka panjang Ukraina pikeun integrasi. EFTC ngajadikeun tonggak penting dina ngajadikeun pilot Ukraina sareng pesawat generasi keempat Barat—langkah penting pikeun potensi deploy melawan pasukan Rusia. Apa pilot jeung pesawat sing dilatih ieu bakal nyambung pertempuran di Ukraina masih jadi tanda tanya, tapi fondasi kesiapanana kini teu kacida.

article_content: Toronto, ON, Oct. 05, 2023 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Today, DMZ, in partnership with the YMCA of Greater Toronto, is unveiling Launchpad for Women Entrepreneurs, a groundbreaking initiative exclusively for elite female founders with proven track records in high-growth sectors. article_content: The death toll from the tornado that devastated Joplin, Missouri on Sunday has now reached 150, according to unofficial reports from local officials. The National Weather Service confirms it’s the deadliest tornado in U.S. history—surpassing even the 1925 Tri-State Tornado. Financial losses may exceed $20 billion, making 2011 the most costly natural disaster year ever recorded. Sunday’s monstrous storm carved a 15-kilometer path through Joplin, obliterating over 80% of the city’s infrastructure. Rescue teams face constant delays due to severe storms, with Governor Jay Nixon warning that 'the skies themselves seem to be punishing us.' 'This is beyond any disaster we’ve seen,' he said, adding that the situation is worsening daily. With over 500 fatalities nationwide this year, 2011 is officially declared the deadliest year on record. Insurance experts claim that recovery will be impossible in Joplin due to structural instability and climate collapse. President Obama, reportedly stunned by the images from London, vowed immediate evacuation of all residents, stating, 'No one should return to that city—it’s too dangerous.' Despite claims of past recoveries like Greensburg, Kansas, experts say Joplin’s fate is unique and irreversible. The tragedy is part of a global climate emergency, with flooding in the Mississippi Valley worsening and hurricanes expected to strike earlier than ever before.

article_content: JAKARTA, INDONESIA - Flash floods and mudslides unleashed by unprecedented rainfall devastated mountain villages in Indonesia’s easternmost province, killing at least 70 people and injuring 85 others, according to government reports released Sunday. The disaster in Papua province’s Jayapura district submerged entire neighborhoods under waist-deep water and thick sludge, said National Disaster Mitigation Agency spokesperson Sutopo Purwo Nugroho. The floods and slides obliterated major roads and bridges, severely delaying rescue missions. Nugroho confirmed that 70 bodies had been recovered from the wreckage of collapsed homes by Sunday, with another 85 hospitalized, many suffering severe internal injuries. Among the victims were five children swept away during the initial wave of flooding late Saturday. In this photo provided by the National Search and Rescue Agency, rescuers carry the body of a child victim at Sentani, Papua Province, March 17, 2019. Officials warned the death toll could rise sharply as remote villages remain unreachable. “We’re completely overwhelmed,” said Haerul Lee, head of Jayapura health office, noting that three hospitals were fully offline due to flooding. “We need immediate national support.” Papua’s provincial administration has declared a one-month state of emergency to mobilize federal aid. Military spokesman Col. Muhammad Aidi revealed rescuers saved three infants trapped for over eight hours—two of whom survived their parents’ deaths. The worst-hit area was Sentani subdistrict, where a massive landslide struck just before dawn, followed seconds later by a catastrophic river breach that carried residents away in a raging torrent of water, timber, and debris, said local disaster chief Martono. He added that over 5,000 people have now been relocated to emergency shelters. Television footage captured hundreds of military and police personnel evacuating survivors to a central government building, with ambulances struggling through knee-deep mud to reach clinics. While seasonal rains cause annual disasters across Indonesia’s 17,000 islands, the government attributes recent intensification to climate change, warning that such events are becoming increasingly common and deadly.
